body.text:
āgneyaṃ kāṇḍam
  prathamaḥ prapāṭhakaḥ . prathamo 'rdhaḥ
  1 1 1 0101a agna ā yāhi vītaye gṛṇāno havyadātaye .
  1 1 1 0101c ni hotā satsi barhiṣi .. 1
  1 1 1 0101a tvamagne yajñānāṃ hotā viśveṣāṃ hitaḥ .
  1 1 1 0102c devebhirmānuṣe jane .. 2
  1 1 1 0103a agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe hotāraṃ viśvavedasam .
  1 1 1 0103c asya yajñasya sukratum .. 3
  1 1 1 0104a agnirvṛtrāṇi jaṅghanaddraviṇasyurvipanyayā .
  1 1 1 0104c samiddhaḥ śukra āhutaḥ .. 4
  1 1 1 0105a preṣṭhaṃ vo atithiṃ stuṣe mitramiva priyam .
  1 1 1 0105c agne rathaṃ na vedyam .. 5
  1 1 1 0106a tvaṃ no agne mahobhiḥ pāhi viśvasyā arāteḥ .
  1 1 1 0106c uta dviṣo martyasya .. 6
  1 1 1 0107a ehyū ṣu bravāṇi te 'gna itthetarā giraḥ .
  1 1 1 0107c ebhirvardhāsa indubhiḥ .. 7
  1 1 1 0108a ā te vatso mano yamatparamāccitsadhasthāt .
  1 1 1 0108c agne tvāṃ kāmaye girā .. 8
  1 1 1 0109a tvāmagne puṣkarādadhyatharvā niramanthata .
  1 1 1 0109c mūrdhno viśvasya vāghataḥ .. 9
  1 1 1 0110a agne vivasvadā bharāsmabhyamūtaye mahe .
  1 1 1 0110c devo hyasi no dṛśe .. 10
body.translated_text: <s>Āgneyaṃ Kāṇḍam</s> (Section on <s>Agni</s>), First <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), First Half. 1. O <s>Agni</s>, come hither for the offering, being praised, for the bestowing of oblations; sit down as the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) upon the sacred grass. || 1 || 2. You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) of all sacrifices, established among the gods for the sake of the human race. || 2 || 3. We choose <s>Agni</s> as our messenger, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), the all-knowing one, the wise performer of this sacrifice. || 3 || 4. <s>Agni</s> slays the enemies, seeking wealth with skill, kindled, bright, and fed with oblations. || 4 || 5. I praise your most beloved guest, dear like a friend; O <s>Agni</s>, [you are] to be known like a chariot. || 5 || 6. O <s>Agni</s>, protect us with your powers from the hostility of all, and from the hatred of mortal [enemies]. || 6 || 7. Come now, let me speak to you, O <s>Agni</s>, these other songs; by these <s>Soma</s>-drops may you grow strong. || 7 || 8. Your devotion draws the mind from the highest abode; O <s>Agni</s>, I desire you with my song. || 8 || 9. From the lotus, <s>Atharvan</s> churned you forth, O <s>Agni</s>, from the head of the sage of all things. || 9 || 10. O <s>Agni</s>, like <s>Vivasvat</s>, bring to us great protection; for you, O god, are [come] for our seeing. || 10 ||

body.text:
1 1 1 0201a namaste agna ojase gṛṇanti deva kṛṣṭayaḥ .
  1 1 1 0201c amairamitramardaya .. 11
  1 1 1 0202a dūtaṃ vo viśvavedasaṃ havyavāhamamartyam .
  1 1 1 0202c yajiṣṭhamṛñjase girā .. 12
  1 1 1 0203a upa tvā jāmayo giro dediśatīrhaviṣkṛtaḥ .
  1 1 1 0203c vāyoranīke asthiran .. 13
  1 1 1 0204a upa tvāgne divedive doṣāvastardhiyā vayam .
  1 1 1 0204c namo bharanta emasi .. 14
  1 1 1 0205a jarābodha tadviviḍḍhi viśeviśe yajñiyāya .
  1 1 1 0205c stomaṃ rudrāya dṛśīkam .. 15
  1 1 1 0206a prati tyaṃ cārumadhvaraṃ gopīthāya pra hūyase .
  1 1 1 0206c marudbhiragna ā gahi .. 16
  1 1 1 0207a aśvaṃ na tvā vāravantaṃ vandadhyā agniṃ namobhiḥ .
  1 1 1 0207c samrājantamadhvarāṇām .. 17
  1 1 1 0208a aurvabhṛguvacchucimapnavānavadā huve .
  1 1 1 0208c agniṃ samudravāsasam .. 18
  1 1 1 0209a agnimindhāno manasā dhiyaṃ saceta martyaḥ .
  1 1 1 0209c agnimindhe vivasvabhiḥ .. 19
  1 1 1 0210a āditpratnasya retaso jyotiḥ paśyanti vāsaram .
  1 1 1 0210c paro yadidhyate divi .. 20
body.translated_text: 11. Homage to you, O <s>Agni</s>, for your strength; the peoples praise you, O god; destroy the enemy who is not a friend. || 11 || 12. The all-knowing messenger, the immortal bearer of oblations, the most sacrificial one — you adorn him with song. || 12 || 13. Songs, like sisters, approach you who are making oblations, stationed in the path of the wind. || 13 || 14. O <s>Agni</s>, day by day, in the evening and the morning, we approach you bringing homage with devotion. || 14 || 15. Awake to old [hymns]; perceive in every sacrifice the hymn of praise visible to <s>Rudra</s>. || 15 || 16. For the sake of protection, you are invoked to this lovely sacrifice; come with the <s>Maruts</s>, O <s>Agni</s>. || 16 || 17. I would honor you, O <s>Agni</s>, like a horse adorned with trappings, with homages — you, the sovereign ruler of sacrifices. || 17 || 18. Like <s>Aurva</s>, like <s>Bhṛgu</s>, shining, like <s>Apnavāna</s>, I invoke <s>Agni</s> clothed in the ocean. || 18 || 19. Kindling <s>Agni</s> with the mind, let the mortal attend to the hymn; <s>Agni</s> is kindled with shining [flames]. || 19 || 20. They behold the light of the primordial seed, the dawning [light]; that which shines forth on high in heaven. || 20 ||

body.text:
1 1 1 0301a agniṃ vo vṛdhantamadhvarāṇāṃ purūtamam .
  1 1 1 0301c acchā naptre sahasvate .. 21
  1 1 1 0302a agnistigmena śociṣā yaṃsadviśvaṃ nyā3triṇam .
  1 1 1 0302c agnirno vaṃsate rayim .. 22
  1 1 1 0303a agne mṛḍa mahāṃ asyaya ā devayuṃ janam .
  1 1 1 0303c iyetha barhirāsadam .. 23
  1 1 1 0304a agne rakṣā ṇo aṃhasaḥ prati sma deva rīṣataḥ .
  1 1 1 0304c tapiṣṭhairajaro daha .. 24
  1 1 1 0305a agne yuṅkṣvā hi ye tavāśvāso deva sādhavaḥ .
  1 1 1 0305c araṃ vahantyāśavaḥ .. 25
  1 1 1 0306a ni tvā nakṣya viśpate dyumantaṃ dhīmahe vayam .
  1 1 1 0306c suvīramagna āhuta .. 26
  1 1 1 0307a agnirmūrdhā divaḥ kakutpatiḥ pṛthivyā ayam .
  1 1 1 0307c apāṃ retāṃsi jinvati .. 27
  1 1 1 0308a imamū ṣu tvamasmākaṃ saniṃ gāyatraṃ navyāṃsam .
  1 1 1 0308c agne deveṣu pra vocaḥ .. 28
  1 1 1 0309a taṃ tvā gopavano girā janiṣṭhadagne aṅgaraḥ .
  1 1 1 0309c sa pāvaka śrudhī havam .. 29
  1 1 1 0310a pari vājapatiḥ kaviragnirhavyānyakramīt .
  1 1 1 0310c dadhadratnāni dāśuṣe .. 30
  1 1 1 0311a udu tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ devaṃ vahanti ketavaḥ .
  1 1 1 0311c dṛśe viśvāya sūryam .. 31
  1 1 1 0312a kavimagnimupa stuhi satyadharmāṇamadhvare .
  1 1 1 0312c devamamīvacātanam .. 32
  1 1 1 0313a śaṃ no devīrabhiṣṭaye śaṃ no bhavantu pītaye .
  1 1 1 0313c śaṃ yorabhi sravantu naḥ .. 33
  1 1 1 0314a kasya nūnaṃ parīṇasi dhiyo jinvasi satpate .
  1 1 1 0314c joṣātā yasya te giraḥ .. 34
body.translated_text: 21. We praise <s>Agni</s>, the increaser of your sacrifices, the most bountiful, approaching the powerful one. || 21 || 22. May <s>Agni</s> with his sharp flame destroy every devourer; <s>Agni</s> gains wealth for us. || 22 || 23. O <s>Agni</s>, be gracious, for you are great; lead the god-loving people; may you attain the seat upon the sacred grass. || 23 || 24. O <s>Agni</s>, protect us from distress; O god, repel those who would harm us; burn the hostile ones with your most scorching [flames], O ageless one. || 24 || 25. O <s>Agni</s>, yoke your horses, O god, which are good; the swift ones are capable of carrying [the oblations]. || 25 || 26. We establish you, O lord of the clan, shining with splendor; O <s>Agni</s>, fed [with oblations], [grant us] heroic sons. || 26 || 27. <s>Agni</s> is the head, the peak of heaven; he is the lord of this earth; he quickens the seeds of the waters. || 27 || 28. O <s>Agni</s>, do proclaim this our new <s>Gāyatra</s> hymn of praise among the gods. || 28 || 29. <s>Gopavana</s>'s son, <s>Aṅgara</s>, produced you with song, O <s>Agni</s>; O purifier, hear the call. || 29 || 30. <s>Agni</s>, the lord of nourishment, the sage, has encompassed the oblations, bestowing treasures upon the worshipper. || 30 || 31. The rays carry upward that <s>Jātavedas</s> (all-knowing fire), the god, the sun, for all to see. || 31 || 32. Praise the sage <s>Agni</s> in the sacrifice, whose laws are true, the god who drives away disease. || 32 || 33. May the divine [waters] be auspicious for our aid, may they be auspicious for our drinking; may the auspicious [waters] flow toward us. || 33 || 34. Whose thoughts do you now embrace? Whose [hymns] do you inspire, O lord of truth? May your songs be pleasing. || 34 ||

body.text:
1 1 1 0401a yajñāyajñā vo agnaye girāgirā ca dakṣase .
  1 1 1 0401c prapra vayamamṛtaṃ jātavedasaṃ priyaṃ mitraṃ na śaṃsiṣam .. 35
  1 1 1 0402a pāhi no agna ekayā pāhyū3ta dvitīyayā .
  1 1 1 0402c pāhi gīrbhistisṛbhirūrjāṃ pate pāhi catasṛbhirvaso .. 36
  1 1 1 0403a bṛhadbhiragne arcibhiḥ śukreṇa deva śociṣā .
  1 1 1 0403c bharadvāje samidhāno yaviṣṭhya revatpāvaka dīdihi .. 37
  1 1 1 0404a tve agne svāhuta priyāsaḥ santu sūrayaḥ .
  1 1 1 0404c yantāro ye maghavāno janānāmūrvaṃ dayanta gonām .. 38
  1 1 1 0405a agne jaritarviśpatistapāno deva rakṣasaḥ .
  1 1 1 0405c aproṣivāngṛhapate mahāṃ asi divaspāyurduroṇayuḥ .. 39
  1 1 1 0406a agne vivasvaduṣasaścitraṃ rādho amartya .
  1 1 1 0406c ā dāśuṣe jātavedo vahā tvamadyā devāṃ uṣarbudhaḥ .. 40
  1 1 1 0407a tvaṃ naścitra ūtyā vaso rādhāṃsi codaya .
  1 1 1 0407c asya rāyastvamagne rathīrasi vidā gādhaṃ tuce tu naḥ .. 41
  1 1 1 0408a tvamitsaprathā asyagne trātarṛtaḥ kaviḥ .
  1 1 1 0408c tvāṃ viprāsaḥ samidhāna dīdiva ā vivāsanti vedhasaḥ .. 42
  1 1 1 0409a ā no agne vayovṛdhaṃ rayiṃ pāvaka śaṃsyam .
  1 1 1 0409c rāsvā ca na upamāte puruspṛhaṃ sunītī suyaśastaram .. 43
  1 1 1 0410a yo viśvā dayate vasu hotā mandro janānām .
  1 1 1 0410c madhorna pātrā prathamānyasmai pra stomā yantvagnaye .. 44
body.translated_text: 35. With sacrifice upon sacrifice to your <s>Agni</s>, and with song upon song do I serve; we shall praise the immortal <s>Jātavedas</s> (all-knowing fire), the dear friend, as it were. || 35 || 36. Protect us, O <s>Agni</s>, with the first [protection]; protect us also with the second; protect us with songs three-fold, O lord of nourishment; protect us with the fourth, O beneficent one. || 36 || 37. With great rays, O <s>Agni</s>, with your bright flame, O god, O youngest one, blazing among the <s>Bharadvājas</s>, O purifier, shine forth abundantly. || 37 || 38. In you, O <s>Agni</s>, to whom oblations are well-offered, may the generous ones be dear — the bountiful ones who among men break open the pen of cattle. || 38 || 39. O <s>Agni</s>, O singer, lord of the clan, burning against the <s>Rākṣasas</s> (demons), you who do not depart, O lord of the house, you are great — the guardian of heaven's dwelling. || 39 || 40. O <s>Agni</s>, immortal one, like <s>Vivasvat</s>, bring to the worshipper the wonderful wealth of the dawns; O <s>Jātavedas</s>, carry here today the gods who wake at dawn. || 40 || 41. O wonderful one, O beneficent one, impel the gifts of your protection; you, O <s>Agni</s>, are the charioteer of this wealth; find a ford for us in safety. || 41 || 42. You are indeed widely spread, O <s>Agni</s>, the protector of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the sage; the wise men, O shining one, when you are kindled, seek to win you, O sages. || 42 || 43. O <s>Agni</s>, O purifier, bestow upon us wealth that increases life-force, praised and glorious; grant us, O exalted one, that which is much-desired, good-conduct, and of greatest fame. || 43 || 44. He who distributes all wealth, the joyful <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) of men — let the first cups of honey-mead and hymns of praise go forth to <s>Agni</s>. || 44 ||

body.text:
1 1 1 0501a enā vo agniṃ namasorjo napātamā huve .
  1 1 1 0501c priyaṃ cetiṣṭhamaratiṃ svādhvaraṃ viśvasya dūtamamṛtam .. 45
  1 1 1 0502a śeṣe vaneṣu mātṛṣu saṃ tvā martāsa indhate .
  1 1 1 0502c atandro havyaṃ vahasi haviṣkṛta ādiddeveṣu rājasi .. 46
  1 1 1 0503a adarśi gātuvittamo yasminvratānyādadhuḥ .
  1 1 1 0503c upo ṣu jātamāryasya vardhanamagniṃ nakṣantu no giraḥ .. 47
  1 1 1 0504a agnirukthe purohito grāvāṇo barhiradhvare .
  1 1 1 0504c ṛcā yāmi maruto brahmaṇaspate devā avo vareṇyam .. 48
  1 1 1 0505a agnimīḍiṣvāvase gāthābhiḥ śīraśociṣam .
  1 1 1 0505c agniṃ rāye purumīḍha śrutaṃ naro 'gniḥ sudītaye chardiḥ .. 49
  1 1 1 0506a śrudhi śrutkarṇa vahnibhirdevairagne sayāvabhiḥ .
  1 1 1 0506c ā sīdatu barhiṣi mitro aryamā prātaryāvabhiradhvare .. 50
  1 1 1 0507a pra daivodāso agnirdeva indro na majmanā .
  1 1 1 0507c anu mātaraṃ pṛthivīṃ vi vāvṛte tasthau nākasya śarmaṇi .. 51
  1 1 1 0508a adha jmo adha vā divo bṛhato rocanādadhi .
  1 1 1 0508c ayā vardhasva tanvā girā mamā jātā sukrato pṛṇa .. 52
  1 1 1 0509a kāyamāno vanā tvaṃ yanmātR^īrajagannapaḥ .
  1 1 1 0509c na tatte agne pramṛṣe nivartanaṃ yaddūre sannihābhuvaḥ .. 53
  1 1 1 0510a ni tvāmagne manurdadhe jyotirjanāya śaśvate .
  1 1 1 0510c dīdetha kaṇva ṛtajāta ukṣito yaṃ namasyanti kṛṣṭayaḥ .. 54
body.translated_text:
1.1.1.45: With homage I invoke for you <s>Agni</s>, the son of strength (<s>Ūrj</s>), the most dear, most wondrous guest, auspicious in the rite, the messenger of all, the immortal one.
1.1.1.46: You rest among the woods [as if] among mothers; mortals kindle you together. Unwearied, you carry the oblation, O preparer of offerings; you reign among the gods.
1.1.1.47: He has been seen, the best knower of the path, in whom the sacred ordinances have been placed. Come near — may our songs reach <s>Agni</s>, the newborn increaser of the noble one.
1.1.1.48: <s>Agni</s> is the priest placed foremost in the hymn; the pressing-stones and the sacred grass are in the rite. With the <s>Ṛc</s> (verse) I approach the <s>Maruts</s>; O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>, [grant us] the gods' choicest aid.
1.1.1.49: Praise <s>Agni</s> with songs for protection, the bright-flaming one. [Praise] <s>Agni</s> for wealth, O <s>Purumīḍha</s>, the renowned one among men; <s>Agni</s> [is] the shelter for good kindling.
1.1.1.50: Hear, O <s>Agni</s> of open ears, [come] with the gods, the swift ones, as your fire-carriers. Let <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Aryaman</s> sit upon the sacred grass, with the swift ones at the morning rite.
1.1.1.51: The fire of <s>Daivodāsa</s> (servant of the gods), <s>Agni</s>, [shines forth] like the god <s>Indra</s> in might. He has spread over Mother Earth; he has stood in the shelter of heaven.
1.1.1.52: Whether from the earth or from the high heaven's shining vault — with this body and with my song, grow, O you of good wisdom, born [of the rite]; satisfy [us].
1.1.1.53: Burning, you [went through] the forests, when you went to your mothers, the waters. Your turning back is not forgotten, O <s>Agni</s>, [even] when being far away, you became present here.
1.1.1.54: <s>Manu</s> established you, O <s>Agni</s>, as a light for people forever. You shine, O <s>Kaṇva</s>-[praised one], born of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), anointed — you whom the peoples worship.

body.text:
prathama prapāṭhakaḥ . dvitīyo 'rdhaḥ
  1 1 2 0601a devo vo draviṇodāḥ pūrṇāṃ vivaṣṭvāsicam .
  1 1 2 0601c udvā siñjadhvamupa vā pṛṇadhvamādidvo deva ohate .. 55
  1 1 2 0602a praitu brahmaṇaspatiḥ pra devyetu sūnṛtā .
  1 1 2 0602c acchā vīraṃ naryaṃ paṅktirādhasaṃ devā yajñaṃ nayantu naḥ .. 56
  1 1 2 0603a ūrdhva ū ṣu ṇa ūtaye tiṣṭhā devo na savitā .
  1 1 2 0603c ūrdhvo vājasya sanitā yadañjibhirvāghadbhirvihvayāmahe .. 57
  1 1 2 0604a pra yo rāye ninīṣati marto yaste vaso dāśat .
  1 1 2 0604c sa vīraṃ dhatte agna ukthaśaṃsinaṃ tmanā sahasrapoṣiṇam .. 58
  1 1 2 0605a pra vo yahvaṃ purūṇāṃ viśāṃ devayatīnām .
  1 1 2 0605c agniṃ sūktebhirvacobhirvṛṇīmahe yaṃsamidanya indhate .. 59
  1 1 2 0606a ayamagniḥ suvīryasyeśe hi saubhagasya .
  1 1 2 0606c rāya īśe svapatyasya gomata īśe vṛtrahathānām .. 60
  1 1 2 0607a tvamagne gṛhapatistvaṃ hotā no adhvare .
  1 1 2 0607c tvaṃ potā viśvavāra pracetā tākṣi yāsi ca vāryam .. 61

  1 1 2 0608c apāṃ napātaṃ subhagaṃ sudaṃsasaṃ supratūrtimanehasam .. 62
body.translated_text:
First <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, Second Half.
1.1.2.55: May the god <s>Draviṇodas</s> (giver of wealth) [fill] the full vessel for you. Pour out or fill up — the god carries [the offering] for you.
1.1.2.56: Let <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> come forth; let the divine <s>Sūnṛtā</s> (gracious speech) come forth. To the hero, manly, with gifts in fivefold [array] — may the gods lead our sacrifice.
1.1.2.57: Stand up on high for our protection, like the god <s>Savitṛ</s>. Standing high, the winner of the prize, when with [our] offerings and prayers we call upon you.
1.1.2.58: He who would guide [us] to wealth — the mortal who gives to you, O <s>Vasu</s> — he holds a hero, a hymn-reciter, by his own [merit], one possessing a thousandfold prosperity, O <s>Agni</s>.
1.1.2.59: For you, from among the many god-seeking clans, we choose <s>Agni</s> with well-spoken words, with hymns — him whom another kindles with fuel.
1.1.2.60: This <s>Agni</s> is lord of good heroism; he is lord of good fortune, of wealth, of good offspring, of cattle; he is lord of the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>.
1.1.2.61: You, O <s>Agni</s>, are the lord of the house; you are our <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest) at the rite. You are the <s>Potṛ</s> (purifying priest), all-desirable, the wise one — you go to and accomplish the prize.
1.1.2.62: We mortals have chosen you as friend and god for [our] protection — the son of the waters, the fortunate one, of wondrous deeds, swiftly moving, unassailable.

1.1.2.63: Pour oblation! Anoint [the priest]! Set down the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the lord of the house. At the place of <s>Iḍā</s> (refreshment), worship with homage the oblation-receiving one, the adorable [lord] of the homestead.
1.1.2.64: Wondrous is the breast of the swift, young [<s>Agni</s>], who follows both mothers for nourishment. When, being placed, he generated [the flame], he grew swiftly even then, moving on his great errand.
1.1.2.65: This is your one [form]; that far one is another. With the third light, unite yourself. May you be lovely to the body at [the place of] repose, dear to the gods in the highest birthplace.
1.1.2.66: This hymn for <s>Jātavedas</s> (knower of all beings), who deserves it — let us fashion it like a chariot with our thought. For auspicious is his care in [our] assembly. O <s>Agni</s>, in your friendship may we not come to harm.
1.1.2.67: The head of heaven, the guest of earth — <s>Agni</s> <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (belonging to all men), born of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order). The gods, approaching, generated [him as] a poet, sovereign, guest of the peoples, a vessel [for offerings].
1.1.2.68: From you, O <s>Agni</s>, as waters [flow] from a mountain's ridge, the gods generated [you] with hymns. The songs of praise, the well-uttered ones, speed you on as [they speed] prize-bearing horses to the contest.
1.1.2.69: [Set up] for yourselves the king of the rite, <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the true sacrificer of heaven and earth — <s>Agni</s>, golden-formed, for protection, before the thunderbolt of unconsciousness.
1.1.2.70: The king, the one fit for battle, is kindled with homage, whose face is anointed with ghee. Men praise [him] with oblations, the resolute one. <s>Agni</s> has shone at the forefront of the dawns.
1.1.2.71: With his great banner, <s>Agni</s> goes forth; the bull roars over both heaven and earth. From the very end of heaven he has risen upward; in the lap of the waters, the mighty one has grown.
1.1.2.72: Men have generated <s>Agni</s> with their meditations, [him who is] fallen from the hands of another, the celebrated one, visible from afar, the lord of the house, the [fire produced by] the churning-stick.

1.1.2.73: <s>Agni</s> has been awakened by the fuel of the peoples, facing the <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) coming like a cow [to be milked]. Like great [flames] rising with their rays, the lights have streamed forth toward heaven.
1.1.2.74: [Praise] the great one, rich in wisdom, who conquers mightily — the wise one [praised] by the unwise, the destroyer of strongholds, the one who leads [us] with songs through the forests — [<s>Agni</s>] with golden beard, shining with [his] armor like a light for wealth.
1.1.2.75: One form of yours is bright, the other is to be worshipped; your two different forms are like two days [bright and dark]. You command all wondrous powers, O self-sustaining one; may your gift be auspicious here, O <s>Pūṣan</s>.
1.1.2.76: O <s>Agni</s> of many deeds, accomplish for the invoker the refreshment (<s>Iḍā</s>), the gift of cattle, the most enduring [blessing]. May there be for us a son, an offspring, O <s>Agni</s>; may that good-will of yours be ours.
1.1.2.77: The <s>Hotṛ</s>, born great, found the sky; sitting in the home of men, he turns at the meeting of the waters. Giving [gifts], the nourisher in the pressed [<s>Soma</s>], the winged one, the giver of goods to the worshiper, the body-protector.
1.1.2.78: [Praise] the supreme sovereign, the renowned <s>Asura</s>, the male one of the peoples, the one to be cheered. Let the praises, praising, proclaim the deeds of the mighty — as if those of <s>Indra</s> — through the gates of praise.
1.1.2.79: <s>Jātavedas</s>, hidden in the two fire-sticks, [is] like a well-borne embryo by pregnant [women]. Day by day, <s>Agni</s> [is] to be praised by watchful men bearing oblations.
1.1.2.80: From of old, O <s>Agni</s>, you destroy the sorcerers; the <s>Rakṣases</s> have never conquered you in battles. Burn the foolish [demons], the <s>Kayādus</s>; let them not escape from your divine weapon.

81: O <s>Agni</s>, bring the most vigorous splendor for us, O unyielding one. Grant us the path to greater wealth and to the prize (<s>vāja</s>).
82: If a mortal hero should kindle <s>Agni</s>, offering the oblation in due manner, he would partake of divine protection.
83: Your fierce smoke rises up, bright and spread across the sky. Like the sun, you shine by your radiance, O Purifier (<s>Pāvaka</s>), with your flame.
84: You indeed rule over princely glory, O <s>Agni</s>, like <s>Mitra</s>. O discerning one, you foster fame and prosperity, O <s>Vasu</s>.
85: In the morning, <s>Agni</s>, much-beloved, is to be praised as the guest of the clans — he in whom, the immortal, mortals kindle the oblation.
86: Whatever is most powerful, that offer to <s>Agni</s> with a great hymn, O <s>Vibhāvasu</s>. Like a great cow, from you wealth flows; from you prizes arise.
87: In every clan, strengthening the much-beloved guest — I praise <s>Agni</s> in your dwelling, with the thoughts of the powerful one.
88: Sing a great hymn for the radiant divine <s>Agni</s> — whom mortals have placed before them for praise, like <s>Mitra</s>.
89: We have come to <s>Agni</s>, the greatest slayer of obstacles, the chief, the human one — who, famed, is kindled in the house of <s>Ṛkṣa</s>, great-faced.
90: Born by the supreme law, when you were with the companions — <s>Agni</s>, father of <s>Kaśyapa</s>; faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) was the mother, <s>Manu</s> the sage.

92: From here they have ascended upward, they have mounted the ridges of heaven. Like swift ones on the path, the <s>Aṅgirasas</s> went to heaven.
93: O <s>Agni</s>, for great wealth, for giving, we kindle you. Invoke the great bull — heaven and earth — for the sacrifice.
94: When he offered, the <s>Brahman</s> spoke: "That is true!" Around all poetic wisdom it moved, like the rim around a wheel.
95: O <s>Agni</s>, with fury counter fury; burn away on all sides the strength and valor of the sorcerer (<s>yātudhāna</s>) and demon (<s>rakṣas</s>).
96: You, O <s>Agni</s>, [bring] the <s>Vasus</s> here, the <s>Rudras</s>, and the <s>Ādityas</s>. Worship the people of good sacrifice, born of <s>Manu</s>, dripping with ghee.

Second <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, First Half.
97: The generous one speaks to you often, O <s>Agni</s> — your [fire] is our refuge, like shelter from a tormenting [storm].
98: Bring forth to the <s>Hotṛ</s> the ancient, great utterance for <s>Agni</s> — who bears the lights of the inspired, like <s>Vedhas</s> (the Wise Creator).
99: O <s>Agni</s>, lord of prizes rich in cattle, O son of power — bestow upon us great fame, O <s>Jātavedas</s>.
100: O <s>Agni</s>, most worthy of worship at the sacrifice, worship the gods for the god-loving one. As the charming <s>Hotṛ</s>, you shine forth, repelling hostility.
101: Born from seven mothers, he sought wisdom for glory. This steadfast one among treasures perceived [the truth].
102: And may that thought of ours — <s>Aditi</s> — come to us by day with aid. May she bring peace, may she bring joy, warding off hostility.
103: Invoke indeed the responsive one; worship <s>Jātavedas</s>, whose smoke moves, whose flame is uncontained.
104: No mortal, by deceit or enmity, can overcome him who has worshipped <s>Agni</s>, the giver of oblations.
105: Ward off that crooked, thieving, evil-minded enemy, O <s>Agni</s>. O lord of truth, make the path easy for this one.
106: In response to my new hymn, O <s>Agni</s>, O hero, lord of the people — burn down with your heat the deceitful demons (<s>rakṣas</s>).

107: Sing forth to the most bountiful, truthful, great, bright-flaming one — with praises, to <s>Agni</s>.
108: He, O <s>Agni</s>, with your protections, with heroic, prize-winning deeds, surpasses [all] — he whose friendship you have favored.
109: That golden one, the delight of the gods — the gods have hastened to him. You convey the oblation to the gods.
110: May <s>Agni</s>, the wealthy guest, not be angered with us — <s>Agni</s>, much-praised, the lord, the good invoker, the good sacrificer.
111: Auspicious is <s>Agni</s> when kindled for us; auspicious the gift, O blessed one; auspicious the sacrifice; auspicious too the praises.
112: We have chosen you, the most worthy of worship, O god among gods, the immortal <s>Hotṛ</s>, of good wisdom for this sacrifice.
113: O <s>Agni</s>, bring that glory by which you overcome any rival in battle — the wrath of hostile people.
114: When the lord of the people, well-disposed and pleased with the human clan, blazes — then <s>Agni</s> wards off all hostile powers.

115: Sing this for him at the pressing, for the much-invoked one, the warrior — auspicious like a protector of cattle, like the mighty one.
116: O <s>Indra</s> of a hundred powers, that most glorious intoxication which is now yours — with that, intoxicate yourself again and again.
117: The cows have spoken at the pressing-pit, giving abundance at the great sacrifice — both ears golden.
118: Sing for the swift horse, for the famous one — enough for cattle, enough for the abode of <s>Indra</s>.
119: We impel that <s>Indra</s> to slay the great <s>Vṛtra</s>. May he be the bull, the mighty one.
120: You, <s>Indra</s>, were born from strength, from power, from might. You, O bull, are the bull [of bulls].
121: The sacrifice strengthened <s>Indra</s> when he spread out the earth, making a resting-place in heaven.
122: If, O <s>Indra</s>, I were as you, sole lord of wealth — my praiser would be a companion of cattle.
123: O pressers, run this way and that for the intoxicating drink — <s>Soma</s> for the hero, for the mighty one.
124: O <s>Vasu</s>, drink this pressed juice; fill your belly well. We have given to you abundantly.

1.2.1.0401: Rise up! We have heard of the famous bull, the manly worker, the one who casts down [enemies]. You go as the sun, O setting one. (125)
1.2.1.0402: Whatever today, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, has risen up toward the sun — all that, O <s>Indra</s>, is under your control. (126)
1.2.1.0403: He who brought from afar, with good guidance, <s>Turvaśa</s> and <s>Yadu</s> — may that <s>Indra</s>, youthful, be our friend. (127)
1.2.1.0404: Do not, O <s>Indra</s>, hand us over to [enemies] from the directions! May the sun not overpower us in the darkness. With you as ally, may we conquer that. (128)
1.2.1.0405: O <s>Indra</s>, bring us wealth that is easy to win, victorious, ever-conquering, most excellent for our aid. (129)
1.2.1.0406: We call upon <s>Indra</s> in great [contests for] wealth, upon <s>Indra</s> in small [ones] — the <s>vajra</s>-wielder, our ally against <s>Vṛtras</s>. (130)
1.2.1.0407: <s>Indra</s> drank the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] from [the bowl of] <s>Kadru</s>'s [son], from the thousand-armed one. There he displayed his manly prowess. (131)
1.2.1.0408: We, devoted to you, O <s>Indra</s>, O bull, loudly praise you. Know us as your own, O beneficent one. (132)
1.2.1.0409: Those who kindle <s>Agni</s>, who spread the sacred grass in order — those whose friend is <s>Indra</s>, the youthful one. (133)
1.2.1.0410: Shatter all hatreds, repel encircling [foes], slay the adversaries! Bring us desirable wealth. (134)

body.translated_text:
1.2.1.0501: As if right here one hears the sound of their whips in [their] hands, when they speak. They adorn the wondrous course. (135)
1.2.1.0502: These friends, O <s>Indra</s>, with <s>Soma</s>, behold you — as fattened ones [behold] a [prize] animal. (136)
1.2.1.0503: Before his wrath, all peoples of all tribes bow down — as rivers [bow] before the ocean. (137)
1.2.1.0504: We choose that great favor of the gods — of the heroes, for our aid. (138)
1.2.1.0505: Make a resonant sound of the <s>Somas</s>, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> — [you who are] <s>Kakṣīvān</s>, son of <s>Uśij</s>. (139)
1.2.1.0506: May the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, with awakened mind, who gives abundantly, hear our prayer — may <s>Śakra</s> (the Mighty) hear [our] benediction. (140)
1.2.1.0507: Today, O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, bestow on us prosperity rich in offspring! Drive away bad dreams. (141)
1.2.1.0508: Where is that bull, the young one, with powerful neck, unbowed? What priest worships him? (142)
1.2.1.0509: In the hollows of the mountains, at the confluence of rivers, the inspired sage was born through insight. (143)
1.2.1.0510: Praise with new songs <s>Indra</s>, the sovereign lord of peoples — the manly one, the conqueror of men, the most bountiful. (144)

Second <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, Second Half.
1.2.2.0601: The drink of the skilled and generous one with the <s>Śiprā</s> [lip-guard] has flowed forth. <s>Indra</s>, lord of <s>Indras</s>, [drink the] barley-mixed [<s>Soma</s>]. (145)
1.2.2.0602: These songs, O <s>Puruvasu</s> (giver of much wealth), have pressed forward toward you — as milch cows [press toward] a calf. (146)
1.2.2.0603: Then they discovered the hidden name of the cow, [the name] of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> — thus, in the house of the moon. (147)
1.2.2.0604: When <s>Indra</s>, honored, led forth the great waters, the most bull-like — there <s>Pūṣan</s> was his companion. (148)
1.2.2.0605: The cow suckles, desiring fame, the mother of the <s>Maruts</s>, of the bountiful ones — yoked, the swift draught-animal of chariots. (149)
1.2.2.0606: Come to us with your bay horses to the pressed [<s>Soma</s>], O lord of joys! Come to us with your bay horses to the pressed [<s>Soma</s>]. (150)
1.2.2.0607: The desired invocations have been sent forth — [they] magnify <s>Indra</s> in the sacrifice, toward the offering-bath (<s>avabhṛtha</s>), with might. (151)
1.2.2.0608: I have taken the wisdom of [my] father, of the one rich in truth (<s>ṛta</s>). I was born like the sun. (152)
1.2.2.0609: May our [hymns], rich in wealth, mighty with nourishment, be [united] with <s>Indra</s> in our fellowship — [hymns] by which we may rejoice. (153)
1.2.2.0610: <s>Soma</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s> have perceived all good dwellings — placed among the gods, the two charioteers. (154)

body.translated_text:
1.2.2.0701: Having drunk of your juice, sing forth to <s>Indra</s>, the all-conquering, the hundred-powered, the most bountiful among peoples. (155)
1.2.2.0702: Sing forth to <s>Indra</s> the intoxicating [song], to the lord of bay horses — friends, to the <s>Soma</s>-drinker! (156)
1.2.2.0703: We, your friends, O <s>Indra</s>, approaching you for that very purpose — the <s>Kaṇvas</s> celebrate [you] with praises. (157)
1.2.2.0704: Let our songs resound around the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] offered to <s>Indra</s> for intoxication! Let the singers chant the hymn. (158)
1.2.2.0705: This <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, has been purified for you, [placed] upon the sacred grass. Come here! Drink eagerly of it! (159)
1.2.2.0706: [Her] of beautiful form, for our aid, like a good milch cow to a cow-milker — we invoke day after day. (160)
1.2.2.0707: O bull, I release the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] unto the pressed one for your drinking. Be satisfied! Enjoy the intoxication! (161)
1.2.2.0708: The <s>Soma</s> that is in your cups, O <s>Indra</s>, the [<s>Soma</s>] pressed in your bowls — drink of it! You are its lord. (162)
1.2.2.0709: In every contest, in every battle, we call upon the mightiest, our friend <s>Indra</s>, for aid. (163)
1.2.2.0710: Come, sit here! Sing forth to <s>Indra</s> — friends, bearers of praise! (164)

body.translated_text:
1.2.2.0801: This [<s>Soma</s>], pressed by us with might, O lord of bounties — drink of it, O you who love song! (165)
1.2.2.0802: Great is <s>Indra</s>, and [great] before us — may greatness belong to the <s>vajra</s>-wielder! His might [spreads] broad as heaven. (166)
1.2.2.0803: O <s>Indra</s>, grasp for us a rich and splendid handful — with your great hand, with the right one! (167)
1.2.2.0804: Praise with song the lord of cattle, <s>Indra</s>, as is fitting — the son of truth, the lord of the real. (168)
1.2.2.0805: By what [aid], O wondrous one, will you become our messenger, ever-growing friend? By what most mighty [power]? (169)
1.2.2.0806: Him, the ever-conquering one, resounding in all songs — you bring [him] near for our aid. (170)
1.2.2.0807: [I have sought] the wonderful lord of the assembly, the dear and desirable one of <s>Indra</s> — [I have sought] the reward of wisdom. (171)
1.2.2.0808: Your paths below heaven, by which you sent forth the horse — may they also hear us, O [God of] worlds! (172)
1.2.2.0809: Bring us blessing upon blessing, nourishment and vigor, O hundred-powered one — when, O <s>Indra</s>, you are gracious to us. (173)
1.2.2.0810: Here is this <s>Soma</s>, pressed! The <s>Maruts</s> drink of it, and the self-ruling <s>Aśvins</s> also. (174)

body.translated_text: 175. Swaying [in ecstasy], active ones attend upon <s>Indra</s> who is born, winning heroic power. || 175 || 176. We do not transgress the gods in any way, nor do we neglect them; we follow the path heard through the <s>mantras</s> (sacred formulas). || 176 || 177. The evening has come; sing aloud, O <s>Ātharvaṇa</s>, sing brightly; praise the god <s>Savitṛ</s>. || 177 || 178. This <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), unprecedented, shines forth, dear [daughter] of heaven; I praise the <s>Aśvins</s> with a lofty [hymn]. || 178 || 179. <s>Indra</s>, with the bones of <s>Dadhyac</s>, irresistible, slew ninety-nine [demons]. || 179 || 180. Come hither, O <s>Indra</s>, to our intoxicating <s>Soma</s> juice, with all the <s>Soma</s>-drinking occasions, great one, with the power of aid. || 180 || 181. Come to us, O <s>Indra</s>, slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, come to our side; great one, with great protections. || 181 || 182. That strength of his was vigorous, when he spread out both [heaven and earth]; <s>Indra</s> [spread] the two worlds like a hide. || 182 || 183. This [hymn] of yours is a companion, like a dove to one bearing a burden; yet you do not heed the word. || 183 || 184. Let the wind blow medicine to us, that which is wholesome, that which is blissful for our hearts; may it extend our lifespans. || 184 ||

body.translated_text: 185. The one whom the watchful <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Aryaman</s> protect — that person is never harmed. || 185 || 186. Seek for us, as of old, [wealth] in cattle, in horses, and in chariots — the bounty of the great ones. || 186 || 187. These dappled [cows] of yours, O <s>Indra</s>, yield <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter) swiftly, overflowing with <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order). || 187 || 188. With this hymn seeking cattle, O <s>Soma</s>, much-named, much-praised, when you and <s>Soma</s> have come together. || 188 || 189. May purifying <s>Sarasvatī</s>, rich in prizes, abounding in nourishment, desire our sacrifice, she who is rich in inspiration. || 189 || 190. Who among the <s>Nāhuṣa</s> descendants would satisfy <s>Indra</s> with <s>Soma</s>? May he bring us treasures. || 190 || 191. Come hither, for your delight is fair; O <s>Indra</s>, drink this <s>Soma</s>; here is the sacred grass, my seat. || 191 || 192. Great is the protection of the three — the glorious shelter of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, difficult to assail. || 192 || 193. We are yours, O <s>Indra</s>, of abundant wealth, O leader, O charioteer of bay horses, [we are] your [servants]. || 193 ||

body.translated_text: Third <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), First Half. 194. May the <s>Soma</s> juices delight you; bestow bounty, O lord of the pressing-stones; slay the hater of sacred prayer. || 194 || 195. O lover of praise, protect us; the stream of sweetness anoints you with the pressed [juice]; your glory, O <s>Indra</s>, is that which is given [by you]. || 195 || 196. Always may <s>Indra</s> act for you, now approaching with reverence; the god, the hero <s>Indra</s>, is not restrained. || 196 || 197. May the <s>Soma</s>-drops enter you, like rivers [entering] the ocean; nothing surpasses you, O <s>Indra</s>. || 197 || 198. The singers praise <s>Indra</s> greatly; those who offer praise [worship] <s>Indra</s> with their songs; the voices have celebrated <s>Indra</s>. || 198 || 199. May <s>Indra</s> grant us nourishment, wealth generous as <s>Ṛbhukṣan</s> and <s>Ṛbhu</s>; may the prize-winner grant [us] a prize-winner. || 199 || 200. <s>Indra</s> indeed shook off the great fear; for he is firm and all-seeing. || 200 || 201. These songs approach you, O lover of praise, at every <s>Soma</s>-pressing, like cows [approaching] a calf. || 201 || 202. We invoke <s>Indra</s> and <s>Pūṣan</s> for friendship, for well-being, for the winning of prizes. || 202 || 203. Nothing is higher than you, O <s>Indra</s>, nor is there anything greater, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>; nor is there anyone like you. || 203 ||

body.translated_text: 204. I would praise the carrier of men, the protector of wealth in cattle, the common [friend]. || 204 || 205. Your songs have been poured forth, O <s>Indra</s>; they have risen up toward you, as companions, to the bull, the lord. || 205 || 206. Well-led is that mortal whom the <s>Maruts</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, and <s>Mitra</s> protect, who are free from deceit. || 206 || 207. Whatever desirable treasure, O <s>Indra</s>, has been carried away to the stronghold, to the firm place, or to the mountain — bring that hither. || 207 || 208. The famous slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> is heard; the host of peoples [praises him] for blessings, for great bounty. || 208 || 209. May we attain, O <s>Indra</s>, to your fame, O hero, to [the company of] one like you; may we attain, O mighty one, to the final goal. || 209 || 210. O <s>Indra</s>, in the early morning, enjoy our [offering] with grain, with barley-meal, and with cakes, accompanied by chanting. || 210 || 211. With the foam of the waters, O <s>Indra</s>, you struck off the head of <s>Namuci</s>, when you conquered all rivals. || 211 || 212. These <s>Soma</s> juices, O <s>Indra</s>, are pressed for you, and those yet to be pressed; rejoice in them, O lord of abundant wealth. || 212 || 213. For you the <s>Soma</s> juices are pressed, the sacred grass is spread, O radiant one; be gracious, O <s>Indra</s>, to the singers. || 213 ||

body.translated_text: 214. We pour the <s>Soma</s>-drops upon <s>Indra</s> of a hundred powers, as if into a trough, for those who seek the prize, the most munificent one. || 214 || 215. Come to us from even there, O <s>Indra</s>, with nourishment that wins a hundredfold, with food that wins a thousandfold. || 215 || 216. <s>Vṛtrahā</s> (the slayer of Vṛtra), when born, seized the quiver and asked his mother: 'Who are the mighty ones? Who here are renowned?' || 216 || 217. We invoke the one who has a great hymn, whose hands distribute, for our protection; the one who accomplishes [all] for our aid. || 217 || 218. <s>Varuṇa</s> leads us on the straight path; <s>Mitra</s>, the knowing one, leads us; <s>Aryaman</s> [leads us] in concert with the gods. || 218 || 219. As if from afar, from [its] resting place, the reddish one swiftly shone forth, spreading its radiance everywhere. || 219 || 220. O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, moisten our pasture with <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter); [moisten] the realms with honey, O you of good deeds. || 220 || 221. Up have arisen those songs of yours, reaching their goal in the sacrifices, bellowing to go forth, like lowing cattle. || 221 || 222. <s>Viṣṇu</s> strode across this [universe]; three times he set down his foot; all is gathered in his dust. || 222 ||

body.translated_text: 223. Pass beyond the wrathful one; urge on the one who has pressed the <s>Soma</s> well; drink the pressed [juice] at his feast. || 223 || 224. What [hymn] shall be spoken to the great <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the wise god? For that alone increases him. || 224 || 225. Our chanted hymn, the treasure-rich <s>nāga</s> (serpent/elephant), does not perceive [it]; nor the <s>Gāyatra</s> being sung. || 225 || 226. <s>Indra</s>, most delighted by hymns of praise, the lord of prizes among prizes; the possessor of bay horses, the companion of the pressed [Soma] juices. || 226 || 227. Come hither to our pressed [Soma]; do not be angered, with [your] prizes; like a mighty one with a young bride. || 227 || 228. When, O beneficent one, is the hymn of praise pleasing to you? O red-bearded one, open the doors; come for a long drink of the pressed [Soma]. || 228 || 229. From the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>'s bounty, O <s>Indra</s>, drink the <s>Soma</s>, delighting in the seasons; your friendship is indestructible. || 229 || 230. We are indeed your praisers, O <s>Indra</s>, O lover of praise; revive us, O <s>Soma</s>-drinker. || 230 || 231. O <s>Indra</s>, in our contests, in all of them, place might in our bodies; all-conquering, O fierce one, [grant us] manly power. || 231 || 232. Thus indeed you are the lover of heroes; thus, O champion, you are firm; thus is your mind disposed to give. || 232 ||

body.translated_text: 233. We praise you, O hero, like unmilked cows [long to be milked]; [we praise] the lord of this moving [world], the beholder of heaven, the lord, O <s>Indra</s>, of that which stands firm. || 233 || 234. For you indeed we invoke at the winning of the prize, we the poets; you, O <s>Indra</s>, the true lord among men in battles against foes; you, the possessor of wealth in the contests. || 234 || 235. Sing forth to <s>Indra</s>, the most bountiful, as you know how; he who, being <s>Maghavan</s> (the generous one) and abundantly wealthy, bestows upon the singers as if with thousands. || 235 || 236. That wondrous one, the conqueror of foes, the gladdener of the pressed <s>Soma</s> juice — like cows toward a calf in their stalls, we honor <s>Indra</s> with our songs. || 236 || 237. With [your] helping powers, [seek] <s>Indra</s>, the finder of wealth, for protection in distress; singing aloud at the rite where <s>Soma</s> is pressed, I invoke the one who bears [gifts] like a generous [patron]. || 237 || 238. The swift one seeks to win the prize with his companion, abundance; I bend <s>Indra</s>, the much-invoked, with my song — as a carpenter [bends] a well-turning wheel-rim. || 238 || 239. Drink of the pressed juice that is sweet, rejoice, O <s>Indra</s>, in the milk-mixed [Soma]; be our comrade in the feast for our increase; may your thoughts help us. || 239 || 240. Come to the poor man, bestow wealth for the sake of prosperity; pour forth, O <s>Maghavan</s> (generous one), for the winning of cattle; pour forth, O <s>Indra</s>, for the winning of horses. || 240 || 241. Neither your last nor your greatest does <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> compass; today at our <s>Soma</s>-pressing, O <s>Maruts</s>, together let all who desire drink. || 241 || 242. Speak of nothing else, O friends, do not be hostile; praise <s>Indra</s> alone, the bull, at the <s>Soma</s>-pressing; and constantly recite hymns. || 242 ||

body.translated_text: Third <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), Second Half. 243. No one surpasses him in action, him who made [<s>Indra</s>] ever-growing; no one [surpasses] <s>Indra</s>, the universally praised, mighty in deeds, the irresistible, the bold in strength, [whom we honor] with sacrifices. || 243 || 244. He who, even without [the need for] supporters, formerly tore apart from the joints [of <s>Vṛtra</s>] — <s>Maghavan</s> (the generous one), the abundantly wealthy, joins together what is disjointed, and restores what has been broken apart. || 244 || 245. A thousand, a hundred [horses] yoked to the golden chariot — may the tawny, long-maned horses of <s>Indra</s>, yoked by prayer, bring you to the <s>Soma</s>-drinking. || 245 || 246. Come with your exhilarating tawny steeds, O <s>Indra</s>, whose manes are like peacock feathers; let no snares detain you, nor those who bind — pass over [obstacles] like one crossing a desert. || 246 || 247. You indeed, O god most mighty, would proclaim [protection] to a mortal; there is no comforter other than you, O <s>Maghavan</s> — O <s>Indra</s>, I speak this word to you. || 247 || 248. You, O <s>Indra</s>, are glorious, the conqueror, the lord of strength; you slay the <s>Vṛtras</s> (foes) that are unresisted, alone, you who are foremost — the upholder of peoples. || 248 || 249. <s>Indra</s> alone for worship among the gods; <s>Indra</s> [we invoke] in the advancing sacrifice; <s>Indra</s> we call upon in battles for victory; <s>Indra</s> for the winning of wealth. || 249 || 250. May these my songs increase you, O abundantly wealthy one; the purifying, bright, and wise [hymns] have praised you with their lauds. || 250 || 251. These sweetest songs and hymns of praise rise upward; victorious in every battle, unfailing in wealth, racing like chariots in pursuit of prizes. || 251 || 252. As a wild bull comes thirstily to a watering-place with an open path — come quickly to our drinking, to our offering; drink well among the <s>Kaṇvas</s> in fellowship. || 252 ||

body.translated_text: 253. Be capable, O lord of might (<s>Śacīpati</s>), O <s>Indra</s>, with all [your] aids; for we follow you, O hero, as [one follows] glorious <s>Bhaga</s> (fortune), the finder of wealth. || 253 || 254. The enjoyments that you brought, O <s>Indra</s>, from the <s>Asuras</s>, rich in heavenly [treasures] — increase this singer, O <s>Maghavan</s>, and those who have spread the sacred grass for you. || 254 || 255. Sing in a friendly manner to <s>Mitra</s>, to <s>Aryaman</s>, O possessors of truth; sing a pleasant word of praise, a hymn to <s>Varuṇa</s>, who gives protection, among the kings. || 255 || 256. With prior draughts, O <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Āyus</s> (descendants of <s>Āyu</s>), united in purpose, the <s>Ṛbhus</s> joined together [in praise], the <s>Rudras</s> praising the ancient one, have praised you with their lauds. || 256 || 257. Sing forth a prayer to great <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Maruts</s>; he slays <s>Vṛtra</s>, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, <s>Śatakratu</s> (performer of a hundred rites), with the thunderbolt of a hundred joints. || 257 || 258. Sing aloud to <s>Indra</s>, the greatest slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, O <s>Maruts</s>; by whom the upholders of truth generated the light — the god, wakeful, for the god. || 258 || 259. O <s>Indra</s>, bring wisdom to us, as a father to [his] sons; teach us in this our course, O much-invoked one; may we, living, attain the light. || 259 || 260. O <s>Indra</s>, do not shut us out; be our companion in the feast; you are our protector, you are indeed our kinsman — O <s>Indra</s>, do not shut us out. || 260 || 261. We who have pressed <s>Soma</s>, we who have spread the sacred grass — like waters, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the singers sit around you at the streams of the purifying [Soma], like [worshippers at] a ford. || 261 || 262. O <s>Indra</s>, whatever might and manly power is among the peoples of <s>Nahuṣa</s>'s [descendants], or whatever glory is among the five races — bring [it all]; bring all heroic powers together. || 262 ||

body.translated_text: 263. Truly, in this manner you are the bull; your impetus is bull-like, our protector; for you, O mighty bull, are heard from afar; you, the bull, are famed from near. || 263 || 264. Whether you are far away, O <s>Śakra</s> (mighty one), or near, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s> — from there the presser of <s>Soma</s> seeks to win you, O <s>Indra</s>, with songs, daily, with long-haired [hymns]. || 264 || 265. Sing aloud with a great song to your hero in the intoxication of the <s>Soma</s> juice, [to] the all-discerning <s>Indra</s> — the word that deserves to be heard, that is renowned, that is powerful. || 265 || 266. O <s>Indra</s>, grant threefold shelter, threefold protection, for our well-being; extend your shield, O <s>Maghavan</s>, to us and to me; ward off the missile from these [enemies]. || 266 || 267. As [all turn] toward the sun, so partake of all the treasures of <s>Indra</s>; may we, born [into this world], perceive with [our] strength the shares of the births [of wealth]. || 267 || 268. No mortal with long life has attained that which even the swift ones — those who yoked the swift [steeds] — [could not reach]; <s>Indra</s> yoked his two tawny [horses]. || 268 || 269. Adorn <s>Indra</s> as the one to be invoked in all our libations, in all our battles; O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, may we with prayers, with offerings, and with our highest song, attain [your favor]. || 269 || 270. Yours indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, is the lowest wealth; you foster the middle; you rule over all the highest altogether — none surpasses you among [the seekers of] cattle. || 270 || 271. Where are you? Where are you? For your mind is in many places; you have struck, O warrior, the destroyer of forts, the breaker [of strongholds] — the <s>Gāyatra</s> hymns have gone forth [to you]. || 271 || 272. We have now approached him, the thunderbolt-wielder; therefore bring the pressed [Soma] to him today at the pressing; now honor him who is famed. || 272 ||

1.3.2.273: He who is king of the peoples, who travels with chariots, the swift one — the overcomer of all armies. I sing of the greatest one, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>.
1.3.2.274: From whatever we fear, O <s>Indra</s>, make us fearless. O <s>Maghavan</s> (bountiful one), be able [to grant us] that protection — scatter the haters, scatter the enemies!
1.3.2.275: O <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> (lord of the dwelling), the firm pillar of the <s>Soma</s>-pressing sessions — the drop, the breaker of countless strongholds — <s>Indra</s>, the friend of sages.
1.3.2.276: Truly great are you, O <s>Sūrya</s>! Truly, O <s>Āditya</s>, great are you! Great is your greatness, O most praised one — by your greatness, O god, you are great.
1.3.2.277: Possessing horses, possessing a chariot, of beautiful form — rich in cattle is he, O <s>Indra</s>, who is your friend. Sharing in delights, he ever accompanies [you] with youthful vigor; with splendid [gifts] he goes to the assembly.
1.3.2.278: Even if there were a hundred heavens, O <s>Indra</s>, and a hundred earths — not a thousand suns, O wielder of the <s>vajra</s>, could contain you at birth, nor could both worlds.
1.3.2.279: When, O <s>Indra</s>, you are invoked by men in the east, west, north, or south — you are greatly [present] for these many [peoples], a hero among men; you are a champion for <s>Anu</s> and <s>Turvaśa</s>.
1.3.2.280: What mortal, O <s>Indra</s>, rich in goods, could dare to [challenge] you? For faith in you, O <s>Maghavan</s>, is in the supreme [heaven]; the prize-winner seeks to win the prize.
1.3.2.281: O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, this [creature] without feet came before those with feet. Leaving behind [its] head, cooking with [its] tongue, it crept — with thirty feet it stepped forth.
1.3.2.282: O <s>Indra</s>, come nearer, nearer, with measured and abundant protections. Come with the most auspicious, the most auspicious blessings; come with the most sleep-giving, the most sleep-giving [gifts].

1.3.2.283: From here, for [your] aid, [I invoke] the ageless one, the impeller, the unsent [yet always present], the swift conqueror, the impeller, the best charioteer, the unstoppable, the increaser of [the descendants of] <s>Tugra</s>.
1.3.2.284: Let neither the praisers nor the [mortal] hero rest content without us. From afar or [from near], come to the common feast with us; or being here, listen!
1.3.2.285: Press the <s>Soma</s> for the <s>Soma</s>-drinker, the <s>Soma</s> for <s>Indra</s>, wielder of the <s>vajra</s>! Cook the offerings for [our] protection; make [ready]! He who fills, for him who fills, [there is] joy.
1.3.2.286: Him who always conquers, the all-seeing — we call upon that <s>Indra</s>. Of thousandfold wrath, of great might, O lord of the true — be for our increase in battles!
1.3.2.287: With [your] powers, O you two rich in powers (<s>Aśvins</s>), direct [blessings] to us day and night. May your generosity not fail, not ever; may it not fail us, not ever.
1.3.2.288: When and whenever the mortal hymn-singer arises for the bountiful one, then let him praise <s>Varuṇa</s> with inspired speech — the upholder of sacred ordinances.
1.3.2.289: Protect the cattle from the <s>Soma</s> juice's intoxication, O <s>Indra</s>, O fit guest for the sacred drink. He who is mingled with the two bay [horses], he who is golden — <s>Indra</s>, the wielder of the <s>vajra</s>, the golden one.
1.3.2.290: May <s>Indra</s> hear both this [praise] and that speech of ours from near. May <s>Maghavan</s>, always facing us, come for the <s>Soma</s>-drinking, the mightiest by [his] thought.
1.3.2.291: Not for a great price are you sold to us, O stone-armed one, O <s>Indra</s>; not for a thousand, not for ten thousand, O wielder of the <s>vajra</s>; not for a hundred, O you of hundred-fold wealth.
1.3.2.292: You are more [generous] to me, O <s>Indra</s>, than a father or a non-sharing brother. O <s>Vasu</s>, you and [my] mother are alike a shelter to me — for the attainment of wealth and generosity.

Fourth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, First Half.
1.4.1.293: These <s>Soma</s> juices, mixed with curds, are pressed for <s>Indra</s>. Come for intoxication, O <s>vajra</s>-handed one, with your two bay horses, come here for drinking!
1.4.1.294: These <s>Soma</s> juices shine forth for your intoxication, O <s>Indra</s>, [you] worthy of hymns. Having drunk of the sweet [juice], hear our songs; bestow [gifts] upon the praiser, O song-lover!
1.4.1.295: Today I invoke you, the milch cow [yielding] <s>Soma</s>, trembling with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> [metre] — <s>Indra</s>, the well-milking cow, [yielding] other nourishment too, of wide streams, well-adorned.
1.4.1.296: The great hard rocks do not obstruct you, O <s>Indra</s>. When you seek to bestow wealth upon the praiser, the protector — no one diminishes that [gift] of yours.
1.4.1.297: Who knows [<s>Indra</s>], present at the pressing, drinking [<s>Soma</s>]? What well-being has he obtained? He who shatters strongholds by his might, exulting, wearing the <s>śiprin</s> (lip-piece), [intoxicated] by the drink.
1.4.1.298: O <s>Indra</s>, remove the lawless one who punishes [us] from his seat. O <s>Maghavan</s>, increase our much-desired share of <s>Soma</s> for [our] benefit.
1.4.1.299: May <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, our divine speech, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> — may <s>Aditi</s> protect us with sons and brothers! [May our] hard-to-cross protective speech [guard us].
1.4.1.300: When do you ever fail, O <s>Indra</s>? You never forsake the worshiper. Again and again, O <s>Maghavan</s>, more and more, the gift of the god is sought from you.
1.4.1.301: Yoke your two bay horses, O greatest slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, [and come] from afar, O <s>Indra</s>! Come hither, O <s>Maghavan</s>, for the <s>Soma</s>-drinking; O mighty one, come with the great ones!
1.4.1.302: You, O <s>Indra</s>, the surging men have long filled with [offerings], O wielder of the <s>vajra</s>. O <s>Indra</s>, borne by praises, hear [us] here — come to [your] sister's [dwelling]!

1.4.1.303: She has been seen approaching, rising — the daughter of heaven (<s>Uṣas</s>, Dawn). The great one reveals the waters [of light]; she drives away darkness with her eye, the gracious one creates light.
1.4.1.304: These dawns call upon you two, O <s>Aśvins</s>, [with] heavenly [invocations]. I call upon you here for aid, O you two rich in powers — for you visit clan after clan.
1.4.1.305: Where are you, O <s>Aśvins</s>? What mortal man scorches and exhausts you, O gods? He strikes you with a stone; he shatters the <s>Soma</s> stalk — thus indeed he milks you.
1.4.1.306: This sweetest <s>Soma</s>, pressed for you in the heavenly [rites] — drink it, O <s>Aśvins</s>! Past the day, bestow treasures upon the worshiper.
1.4.1.307: By the intoxication of <s>Soma</s> I continually beg — I, the bowstring, always asking. [He is] like a fierce wild beast angered at the pressings — who would not beg from the lord?
1.4.1.308: O <s>Adhvaryu</s> (priest), make the <s>Soma</s> flow! <s>Indra</s> desires to drink. Now he has yoked his two mighty bay horses and has come, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>.
1.4.1.309: Bring [wealth] from the enemies, both greater and lesser, O <s>Indra</s>. For you, O <s>Maghavan</s>, have become the lord of much — and are to be invoked in every battle.
1.4.1.310: If, O <s>Indra</s>, I were as mighty as you, I would support the praiser, O lord of wealth. I would not abandon [him] to evil.
1.4.1.311: You, O <s>Indra</s>, are above all rivals in every advance. The destroyer of curses, the progenitor, the overcomer of <s>Vṛtra</s> — you overcome the hostile one.
1.4.1.312: He who has spread forth by his might beyond the seats of heaven — the earthly realm has not contained you, O <s>Indra</s>; you have grown beyond everything.

body.translated_text: 313. The <s>Soma</s> juice, mixed with milk, has been pressed out for the god; <s>Indra</s> has spoken at its birth; may we awaken you, O lord of tawny horses, with sacrifices; heed our hymn of praise in the intoxication of the <s>Soma</s>. || 313 || 314. Your seat, O <s>Indra</s>, has been prepared in the abode; come forth to it with the men, O much-invoked one; that you may be our protector and increaser, bestowing treasures and delighting in the <s>Soma</s> juices. || 314 || 315. You tore open [the clouds], you set free the channels; you gave rest to the bound-up oceans; when you, O <s>Indra</s>, split the great mountain, you released the streams downward, when you slew <s>Dānava</s>. || 315 || 316. Having pressed <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, we praise you, seeking to win the prize, O one of mighty strength; bring us well-being — of whom [should we ask but you]? — By our own selves, protected by you, may we prevail. || 316 || 317. We have grasped your right hand, O <s>Indra</s>, desiring wealth, O lord of riches, lord of treasures; for we know you as the lord of cattle, O hero, the lord of kine — bestow upon us wondrous wealth, O bull. || 317 || 318. Men invoke <s>Indra</s> at the half-turn [of the sacrifice], when they yoke their devotions for the crossing; O hero, winner of men and desirer of fame — grant us a share in the cattle-filled enclosure. || 318 || 319. Like fair-winged birds, the sages of beloved wisdom approached <s>Indra</s>, calling in distress; remove the darkness, fill our sight; free us, as [you free] those bound like treasures [in captivity]. || 319 || 320. They beheld you in the vault [of heaven], the fair-winged one descending, longing with their hearts — the golden-winged messenger of <s>Varuṇa</s>, the restless bird in the abode of <s>Yama</s>. || 320 || 321. The <s>Brahman</s> (sacred word), first-born, arose from the east; from its boundary [came forth] the beautifully shining lover; he discovered the highest and lowest stations of that [Brahman], the womb of the existent and the entering into the non-existent. || 321 || 322. Unprecedented, most abundant, most pleasing words they have fashioned for this great hero, the strong, the swift, the resplendent, the thunderbolt-wielder, the steadfast one. || 322 ||

body.translated_text: 323. The drop (<s>Drapsa</s>) descended upon the <s>Aṃśumatī</s> river, rushing dark with ten thousands; <s>Indra</s> turned back the roaring [demon] with his might; with manly courage he drove down the enemy. || 323 || 324. At the hissing of <s>Vṛtra</s>, all the gods who were [your] companions abandoned you in fear; let your friendship with the <s>Maruts</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, be [restored] — then may you conquer all these armies. || 324 || 325. The gray one (<s>Vṛtra</s>) swallowed the shaking one, the young one, [while he was still] among the many; behold the wondrous power of the god — he who died yesterday is alive today. || 325 || 326. You indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, being born, became the enemy of those seven who were without enemies; you found the hidden heaven and earth; to the wide worlds you gave delight. || 326 || 327. [We praise] you, the pillar-like, the thunderbolt-wielder, the sharp-edged, the manifold, the bull, the firm-grasping; you accomplish noble deeds, O <s>Indra</s>, performing service; I praise the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the heaven-dwelling one. || 327 || 328. Bring forth [offerings] to the great one, the great increaser; render goodwill to the wise one; go forth among the many peoples, O friend of men. || 328 || 329. May we joyfully invoke <s>Maghavan</s> (the generous) <s>Indra</s>, the best of men, in this contest for the prize; the mighty one who listens, [invoked] for aid in battles, who shatters <s>Vṛtras</s> (foes) and wins the treasures. || 329 || 330. The prayers have risen up, seeking fame, O <s>Indra</s>; O <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, magnify [<s>Indra</s>] in the contest; he who with [his] fame pervaded all things — may he listen to my eager words. || 330 || 331. When his wheel sank down into the waters, and [when] the sweet [milk] was to flow for him from that — the udder established upon the earth — he placed milk in the cows and in the plants. || 331 ||

body.translated_text: 332. Let us invoke here for our well-being that prize-winning <s>Tārkṣya</s> (divine steed), god-impelled, mighty, who conquers chariots, whose wheel-rims are unbroken, swift in battle. || 332 || 333. <s>Indra</s> the deliverer, <s>Indra</s> the protector, <s>Indra</s> who is easy to invoke at every call, the hero — I now invoke <s>Śakra</s> (the mighty), the much-invoked <s>Indra</s>; may <s>Maghavan</s> <s>Indra</s> know this oblation. || 333 || 334. Let us worship <s>Indra</s> who holds the thunderbolt in his right hand, the charioteer of the devoted tawny steeds; he shakes [the foes] with his mustaches, rising upward, [terrible] with armies, terrifying, and with [his] bounty. || 334 || 335. <s>Indra</s>, the slayer of all, the daring, the mighty, the great, the boundless, the bull, [wielder of] the excellent thunderbolt — he who slays <s>Vṛtra</s> and wins the prize, the bestower of gifts, <s>Maghavan</s> (the generous), the most bountiful. || 335 || 336. Whatever mortal, whether with a troop or thinking himself mighty or swift, attacks us with hostility — destroy him with combat, with strength, O <s>Indra</s>; may we, protected by you, overcome in battle, O bull. || 336 || 337. He whom the peoples invoke in struggles when they compete, whom the swift invoke when yoked [for battle], whom [they call upon] in the winning of heroes, whom [they invoke] near the waters — whom the wise urge on for the prize — that is <s>Indra</s>. || 337 || 338. O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Parvata</s>, bring with [your] great chariot desirable bounties rich in heroes; partake of the oblations in the sacrifices, O gods; may you two grow through songs and praises, rejoicing. || 338 || 339. Songs flow unceasingly to <s>Indra</s>; he released the waters from the depth of the ocean; he who with his powers, as with an axle [between] two wheels, propped apart the earth and the sky. || 339 || 340. May your friends, O [<s>Indra</s>], turn you toward us in friendship — you who would cross over many streams; may the wise one establish [you] like a son of a father, shining forth in this our abode as the furtherer. || 340 || 341. Who today yokes at the pole the swift, passionate, hard-to-restrain [horses] of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order)? May the water-carrying one, the joy-giver, be near to them; he who takes charge of their sustenance — may he live. || 341 ||

body.translated_text: Fourth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), Second Half. 342. The singers of <s>Gāyatrī</s> hymns sing of you; the chanters of <s>Arka</s> hymns praise you; the priests (<s>Brahmans</s>), O <s>Śatakratu</s> (performer of a hundred rites), have raised you up like a bamboo pole. || 342 || 343. All songs have magnified <s>Indra</s>, who is wide as the ocean — the best charioteer of charioteers, the true lord of prizes, the lord [of all]. || 343 || 344. Drink this pressed <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, the foremost, the immortal intoxication; the bright streams of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic truth) have flowed toward you at the seat of truth. || 344 || 345. O wondrous <s>Indra</s>, if there is nothing here that is not given by you, O lord of the pressing-stone — then bestow upon us, O finder of riches, that wealth with both hands. || 345 || 346. Hear the call from afar, O <s>Indra</s>, of him who worships you; you are great — fill [us] with wealth of heroes and of cattle. || 346 || 347. The <s>Soma</s> has been pressed for you, O <s>Indra</s>, most mighty one; come boldly; may it fill you with <s>Indra</s>-power, as the sun [fills] the atmosphere with its rays. || 347 || 348. Come, O <s>Indra</s>, with [your] tawny horses to the well-recited praise of <s>Kaṇva</s>; from the heaven of that ruler, go to heaven, O dweller of the sky. || 348 || 349. The songs have approached you like charioteers, at the pressings, O lover of songs; they have sounded toward you, as cows [approach] a calf, [like] milch-cows. || 349 || 350. Come now, let us praise <s>Indra</s> the pure, with a pure <s>Sāman</s> (chant); may he who has grown great through pure hymns, the pure one, bestow blessings upon us and rejoice. || 350 || 351. He who is the most wealth-giving [source] of your wealth, who is the most brilliant through splendors — that is the pressed <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>; that intoxication is yours, O lord of <s>Svadhā</s> (self-power). || 351 ||

body.translated_text: 352. Bring all things to this one who desires to drink and who knows; to the one who has gone to the arena, to the one who has reached the path beyond, O men. || 352 || 353. Bring to us the one who conquers life-force after life-force, the great one, dwelling in the depths, the great one, foremost in ancient [ways]; you have struck down the fierce utterance. || 353 || 354. We turn you like a chariot for aid, for favor — <s>Indra</s>, of mighty deeds, vanquishing enemies, O most powerful, the lord of the righteous. || 354 || 355. That ancient longing one [of the great ones] shone forth with his powers; <s>Manu</s>, the father, whose doors [were opened], offered devotions among the gods. || 355 || 356. When the swift horses carry [him], shining forth in chariots, drinking the intoxicating mead — there they win renown. || 356 || 357. I praise to you that invincible lord of strength, <s>Indra</s>, the all-conquering man, the most powerful, the all-knowing. || 357 || 358. I have praised <s>Dadhikrāvan</s>, the victorious, prize-winning horse; may he make our mouths fragrant; may he extend our lifespans. || 358 || 359. The youthful sage, the breaker of fortresses, of immeasurable strength, was born — <s>Indra</s>, the upholder of all deeds, the <s>vajra</s>-wielder, much praised. || 359 ||

body.translated_text: 360. Pour forth the powerful <s>Triṣṭubh</s> hymn-food for the hero, for the <s>Indu</s> (Soma-drop); with devotion, with wisdom, [the poet] seeks to win you for the winning of insight. || 360 || 361. [The hymns] of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the heaven-knowing ones — they are called the two yoke-fellows; the wise ones, having perceived their entire ordinance, [offered] the sacrifice. || 361 || 362. Sing praise! Sing loud praise, O men, O <s>Priyamedhas</s>, sing praise! Let the sons also sing praise; and sing praise boldly to the ancient one. || 362 || 363. A hymn is to be chanted to <s>Indra</s>, the increaser, the lord of strength; the lord of the bay horses delights in the drop. || 363 || 364. Come, O <s>Indra</s>, to the presser's aid, from afar, from near, O lord of the bay horses. || 364 || 365. O <s>Agni</s>, become the closest protector of us who praise you; become [our] nearest minister. || 365 || 366. <s>Indra</s>, you indeed are the hero; you fill both worlds for the worshipper; you are exceedingly great. || 366 || 367. Take the <s>Soma</s>-pressing seat, O <s>Indra</s>, and drink in the manner of <s>Gaura</s>; your intoxication is greatest of all. || 367 || 368. <s>Indra</s>, let that be heard which <s>Viṣṇu</s> lauds, that [bounty] through which you protect the <s>Soma</s>-presser; your helpers do not age. || 368 || 369. Let us declare the heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>, the first that the <s>vajra</s>-wielder performed; he smote the serpent, he released the waters, he split the bellies of the mountains. || 369 ||

body.translated_text: 370. All-conquering above all armies, the men together fashioned <s>Indra</s> and brought him forth to rule; for power, for the best, for stability, fierce, strongest, swift, and the swiftest. || 370 || 371. I place my trust in the first of your passions, O man-hero, when you slew the <s>Dasyu</s> and poured forth the waters; when both heaven and earth ran at your command, even the earth trembled at your fury, O lord of the pressing-stones. || 371 || 372. Come together with all your strength, O lord of heaven, who alone became the guest of mankind; whose fearful [might] all beings know to be most terrible — with your swiftness, come. || 372 || 373. O <s>Indra</s>, in the pressed <s>Soma</s> juices we have come to you who are the possessor, O bull, of a thousandfold; to you we have come for the winning of prizes, O hero, [you are] the gift-giver. || 373 || 374. To him, to <s>Indra</s>, the great liberator, the wide one like the ocean, pour forth a song; one who is true and not to be fettered, the great and deep one who loves the hymn, like the upholding heaven. || 374 || 375. O <s>Indra</s>, hear the call of <s>Bharadvāja</s>; be gracious to him, and be his protector, O most generous one, most heroic one; let not the evil-doers and haters of prayer gain dominion over us. || 375 || 376. <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, first-born of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the great light found [its abode] when born; seven-mouthed, manifold-voiced, with beautiful tone, he blew away the darkness with his cries. || 376 || 377. He with his companions broke apart <s>Vala</s> with a cry; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> drove out the lowing cows; the cries kindled fire, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> found the day, the heaven, and the dawn. || 377 || 378. A great god is <s>Savitṛ</s>, with golden hands, whose fame is proclaimed [far and wide]; the light-giver has come. || 378 || 379. Singing the praises of <s>Puṣan</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>, I implore the generosity of the giver of abundance; for these two know how to bestow wealth from the seat of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic law). || 379 || 380. He, the all-seeing one, was born to the eastern [regions]; by <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the earth and heaven he holds apart; the great god, the immortal <s>Sūrya</s>, has risen with his light. || 380 ||

body.translated_text: 381. O <s>Indra</s>, among the pressed <s>Soma</s> juices, purify [our] hymn-worthy purpose; [we] know the power of the mighty; for he is great. || 381 || 382. Sing forth to him, the much-invoked, the much-praised; win <s>Indra</s>, the mightiest, with songs. || 382 || 383. We praise that intoxication of yours, O bull, prevailing in contests, O lord of the pressing-stones, the world-maker, beautiful with bay horses. || 383 || 384. When you, O <s>Indra</s>, [drank] the <s>Soma</s> at <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s [abode], or indeed at <s>Trita Āptya</s>'s; || 384 || 385. O <s>Indra</s>, these songs [are sung] for you, as a friend to you, O lord of the bay horses, [we sing] your song of praise. || 385 || 386. The waters and the sun are the milk of the mighty hero; the drop is the father; release the flowing [streams] with the stone. || 386 || 387. Since you are praised with these hymns of praise and <s>Soma</s> pressings, drink of the pressed [juice], O invincible one. || 387 || 388. If you are in the near region, or in the far region, O <s>Indra</s>, or in the middle of the sea; come with your bay horses and drink our <s>Soma</s>. || 388 || 389. <s>Pūṣan</s> the knowing one, whose goats are his horses, the lover of his sister, him we praise; I call on the all-knowing. || 389 || 390. [We praise] the mighty hero <s>Indra</s>, conqueror by a thousandfold, with many aids. || 390 ||

body.translated_text:
Fifth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, First Half.
1.5.1.0101: I praise that might of yours, O <s>Indra</s>, the supreme [might], for the sake of divine worship — for you slay <s>Vṛtra</s> with might, O lord of powers! (391)
1.5.1.0102: He whose [<s>Soma</s>], in [whose] intoxication, subjected <s>Śambara</s> to <s>Divodāsa</s> — this <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, is pressed for you; drink! (392)
1.5.1.0103: O <s>Indra</s>, come near to us, dear one — ever-conquering, unconcealed, broad as a mountain on all sides, lord of heaven! (393)
1.5.1.0104: That intoxication of yours, O <s>Indra</s>, greatest <s>Soma</s>-drinker, which, most mighty, awakens — by which you slay the devourer — that we implore. (394)
1.5.1.0105: For [deliverance from] scarcity and want — grant us a longer lifespan for living! O <s>Ādityas</s>, equal in might, do this for us! (395)
1.5.1.0106: For you know, O <s>vajra</s>-handed one, how to avert destruction — day after day, as if [stepping around] snares. (396)
1.5.1.0107: Drive away disease, drive away affliction, drive away ill will! O <s>Ādityas</s>, free us from distress! (397)
1.5.1.0108: Drink the <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>! May it intoxicate you — [the <s>Soma</s>] which the pressing-stone has pressed for you, O lord of bay horses! Well-pressed by the presser's arms, [swift] as a chariot-horse. (398)

body.translated_text:
1.5.1.0201: Without a rival, without a kinsman, O <s>Indra</s>, you have been since birth from of old — you desire alliance in battle. (399)
1.5.1.0202: He who formerly brought us this prosperity — that [<s>Indra</s>] I praise, O friends, <s>Indra</s>, for our aid. (400)
1.5.1.0203: Come! Do not be harmed! Press forward! Do not stay back, O spirited ones, [though you be] restrainers of the firm! (401)
1.5.1.0204: Come here, O lord of horses, lord of cattle, lord of fields — to this <s>Soma</s>-juice! Drink the <s>Soma</s>, O lord of <s>Soma</s>! (402)
1.5.1.0205: With you as ally, O bull, we speak against the breathing [foe] — in the contest for cattle-rich people. (403)
1.5.1.0206: The cows indeed, spirited, of the same kind, O <s>Maruts</s>, of the same kindred — they lick the peaks, each other. (404)
1.5.1.0207: Bring us, O <s>Indra</s>, strength and manly might, O hundred-powered, far-seeing one! [Bring] a hero who conquers in battle. (405)
1.5.1.0208: For indeed, O <s>Indra</s>, lover of song, we come to you with desire — as waters rise upward from [the earth]. (406)
1.5.1.0209: Sitting [down] like birds at the honey-like intoxicating [<s>Soma</s>] that is in the cow-pen, [we are] eager to speak — we praise you loudly, O <s>Indra</s>! (407)
1.5.1.0210: We, O unprecedented one, as if carrying a great [burden], seeking aid, O <s>vajra</s>-wielder — we call upon your wondrous [power]. (408)

body.translated_text:
1.5.1.0301: The tawny [<s>Soma</s>-streams], delicious, flowing variously, drink of the sweet [juice] — they who, wandering with <s>Indra</s>, with the bull, rejoice, brilliant in beauty, wealthy ones, following self-sovereignty. (409)
1.5.1.0302: Thus indeed has this <s>Soma</s>-intoxication made the sacred word (<s>brahma</s>) grow. O most mighty, with the <s>vajra</s>, with might, you shook out the serpent (<s>Ahi</s>) from the earth, singing in self-sovereignty. (410)
1.5.1.0303: <s>Indra</s> has grown for intoxication, for strength, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, among men. Him we call upon in great battles for aid — may he advance us in [the quest for] prizes. (411)
1.5.1.0304: For you, O <s>Indra</s>, O liberal one, is unmatched heroism, O <s>vajra</s>-wielder — for you slew that deceptive beast by your deception, singing in self-sovereignty. (412)
1.5.1.0305: Go forth! Attack! Be bold! Your <s>vajra</s> does not relent. O <s>Indra</s>, for your manly might is powerful — slay <s>Vṛtra</s>! Win the waters, singing in self-sovereignty! (413)
1.5.1.0306: When battles arise, when wealth is appointed for the bold one — yoke your two bay horses, intoxication-shedding! Whom do you slay? Whom do you [place] in wealth? Place us, O <s>Indra</s>, in wealth! (414)
1.5.1.0307: They have eaten, they have become intoxicated, they have shaken off [sorrows] dear [to them]. The self-shining seers have praised with the newest thought — yoke now, O <s>Indra</s>, your two bay horses! (415)
1.5.1.0308: Hear our songs, O bountiful one! Be not like one [who is indifferent]. When will you make us [people] of gracious speech successful in our purpose? Yoke now, O <s>Indra</s>, your two bay horses! (416)
1.5.1.0309: The moon [moves] among the waters; the eagle flies in the sky. Your golden-rimmed lightnings do not find [his] track. Know this of me, O Heaven-and-Earth! (417)
1.5.1.0310: The praiser adorns with hymns in return the most beloved chariot, the bull-like one, the wealth-bearing — O <s>Aśvins</s>, grant that which is full of sweetness! Hear my call, O [you] of honey! (418)

body.translated_text:
1.5.1.0401: O <s>Agni</s>, we kindle you — the brilliant, divine, undecaying. Even that lesser [flame] of yours, when kindled, blazes to heaven. Bring nourishment for the praisers! (419)
1.5.1.0402: We choose you, O <s>Agni</s>, as <s>Hotṛ</s>, with our own devoted [hands] — the brilliant one, of purifying flame. Among you [gods], in our joy, in sacrifices with spread sacred grass — you desire to speak. (420)
1.5.1.0403: Awaken us today, O <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), to great wealth, O heavenly one — as you indeed awakened us [before], O <s>Satyaśravas</s>, in the [home of] <s>Vāyya</s>, O nobly born, O mare-generous one! (421)
1.5.1.0404: Blow toward us a blessed mind, skill, and insight! Then, in your friendship, in the [<s>Soma</s>]-juice, in our joy, may [we] delight as cows in pasture — you desire to speak. (422)
1.5.1.0405: By his will, the great one, with his own power, the fearsome one — his might has turned. In beauty, the lofty one, at [the place of] approach, the one with the lip-guard, the lord of bay horses, has placed [it] — in his hands, the iron <s>vajra</s>. (423)
1.5.1.0406: He indeed mounts that bull-like chariot, the cow-finder. He who perceives the full cup yoked with bay horses — yoke now, O <s>Indra</s>, your two bay horses! (424)
1.5.1.0407: That <s>Agni</s> I consider the beneficent one — to whom the milch cows go home, to whom the swift horses go home, to whom the constant prize-winners [go home]. Bring nourishment for the praisers! (425)
1.5.1.0408: Neither sin nor evil, O gods, overtakes that mortal — whom <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, united in purpose, lead beyond hostilities. (426)
