body.translated_text:
1.5.1.0501: Flow around, O <s>Soma</s>, sweet for <s>Indra</s>, for <s>Mitra</s>, for <s>Pūṣan</s>, for <s>Bhaga</s>! (427)
1.5.1.0502: Flow forth mightily for the winning of prizes! Overcoming <s>Vṛtras</s>, you rush [like waters] released from debts against the hateful ones. (428)
1.5.1.0503: Flow forth, O <s>Soma</s>! Great ocean, father of the gods, [pervading] all abodes! (429)
1.5.1.0504: Flow forth, O <s>Soma</s>, for great skill — like a horse bathed, a racer [running] for the prize! (430)
1.5.1.0505: The drop (<s>Indu</s>) has been purified, delightful, for intoxication — the sage, for wealth, in the lap of the waters! (431)
1.5.1.0506: Having pressed you, O <s>Soma</s>, we rejoice in you for the great fight, for sovereignty. You stride forth, O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-purifying), toward prizes! (432)
1.5.1.0507: Who are these men, companions of the same nest? Young men of <s>Rudra</s> — and possessing fine horses? (433)
1.5.1.0508: O <s>Agni</s>, today that [hymn] — like a horse, with praises, like a blessed thought touching the heart — may we succeed with your aids! (434)
1.5.1.0509: The young men appeared openly! They reached the prize, the swift ones — the impulse of god <s>Savitṛ</s>. Steeds, conquer heaven! (435)
1.5.1.0510: Flow forth, O <s>Soma</s>, brilliant, well-purified, great one, in order, among the sheep! (436)

body.translated_text:
Fifth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, Second Half.
437: O giver from every side, bring to us from every side — you whom we invoke as the mightiest.
438: This is the priest (<s>Brahmā</s>) who is the seasonal one — <s>Indra</s> by name, the famous one, I praise.
439: Magnifying <s>Indra</s> with sacred utterances and hymns, they strengthened him to slay the serpent (<s>Ahi</s>).
440: They fashioned for the horse a chariot without a rim; <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> [fashioned] the thunderbolt for the much-invoked, resplendent one.
441: The lawless one (<s>avrata</s>) does not impel [toward] happiness, position, bounty, [nor] the desire of the wealth-seeker; he does not touch wealth.
442: Always the cows are pure, nourishing all; always the gods are without blemish.
443: Come along with the wooden vessel; the cows follow the path when [they come] with their udders.
444: Dwelling near the honey-sweet [offering], may we prosper in wealth; we meditate on you, O <s>Indra</s>.
445: The <s>Maruts</s> sing the hymn, the radiant ones; the famed youth, he — <s>Indra</s> — is praised.
446: Sing forth a song for <s>Indra</s>, the best <s>Vṛtra</s>-slayer, the wise one — [a song] that he delights in.

447: <s>Agni</s> has been perceived, the discerning one, the conveyor of oblations, of beautiful chariot.
448: O <s>Agni</s>, you are nearest to us, and a protector; be gracious, be a guardian.
449: Like <s>Bhaga</s>, the brilliant <s>Agni</s> bestows treasure upon the great ones.
450: Praise forth for all; whether forward or if here indeed, right now.
451: <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), driving away the darkness of her sister [Night], rolls the path along — by her noble birth.
452: May we now indeed prevail over these worlds — <s>Indra</s> and all the gods [aiding us].
453: As streams [flow] along paths, so, O <s>Indra</s>, may your gifts come forth.
454: By this [prayer], may we win the god-appointed prize; may we rejoice through a hundred winters, rich in heroes.
455: <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> swell with nourishment the refreshments; make for us rich sustenance, O <s>Indra</s>.
456: <s>Indra</s> rules over all.

body.translated_text:
457: In the <s>Trikadrukas</s> (three-day rite), the mighty buffalo of great bluster drank the barley-mixed <s>Soma</s>, pressed with <s>Viṣṇu</s>, as he wished. He delighted himself for performing a great deed — the vast expanse. The true <s>Indu</s> (Soma drop), the god, accompanied the true <s>Indra</s>.
458: This [Soma], [visible] to thousands of mortals, the thought of poets, the light that upholds the law — the tawny one set the dawns moving together, faultless, of bright mind; in their own domain, the spirited ones were arranged like rays of the cow.
459: O <s>Indra</s>, come to us from afar — come hither, like a true lord to assemblies, like a king, a true lord. We call you, being generous, at our pressings — like sons [calling] a father for winning the prize, the most bountiful one, for winning the prize.
460: I call loudly upon that <s>Indra</s>, the bountiful (<s>Maghavan</s>), the mighty, who perpetually bestows unresisted glories in abundance. Most generous, praised with hymns, the sacrificial one has turned [toward us]; may the <s>Vajra</s>-wielder make all fair paths for our wealth.
461: Let there be attention! I place <s>Agni</s> before with thought. Now we choose that divine host — <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s> we choose. When indeed the creative one established for the new <s>Vivasvat</s> at the navel, then now our thoughts go forth toward the gods, like [streams] toward the gods.
462: May your great hymns go forth to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to him accompanied by <s>Maruts</s>, the mountain-born, the swiftly moving <s>Marut</s>. Forth to the host, to the devout, to the gracious, to the mighty — for splendid worship, for the thundering one, for might.
463: Purifying himself with this golden radiance, he crosses over all hatreds, with his yoke-companions, like the sun with his yoke-companions. The stream from his back shines; purifying himself, the ruddy tawny one — [he who] traverses all forms with his hymns, with his seven mouths and hymns.
464: I praise that god <s>Savitṛ</s>, of poetic wisdom, true in his impulsion, the abode of treasure — the beloved thought. His lofty understanding shone brightly in his impelling; the golden-handed one measured out with good wisdom; [he created] the light of heaven.
465: I think of <s>Agni</s> as the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the generous one, the son of Strength, <s>Jātavedas</s>, the wise one, <s>Jātavedas</s>. He who, upward, with self-upheld sacrifice, the god, with divine flame — [shines] along the splendor of ghee, the bright-flaming one, offering the clarified butter.
466: That manly deed of yours, O hero — the first, the ancient, the glorious deed accomplished in heaven, O <s>Indra</s>; who by the god's might released the breaths, releasing the waters — you became all, surpassing every ungodly foe in might. The hundred-powered one (<s>Śatakratu</s>) found nourishment, found refreshment.

<s>Pāvamāna Kāṇḍa</s> (Section of the Self-Purifying [<s>Soma</s>]).
467: Born high from the plant, established in heaven, I receive [it] from the earth — fierce shelter, great glory.
468: O <s>Soma</s>, flow with the sweetest, most intoxicating stream — pressed for <s>Indra</s> to drink.
469: Flow in a stream, O bull, O intoxicating one, for [<s>Indra</s>] accompanied by <s>Maruts</s> — holding all things with your might.
470: That choice intoxication of yours — with that, O <s>Soma</s>, flow with the plant — O divine hero, slayer of the evil-speaking demon.
471: Three voices are raised; the cows low, the milk-cows; the tawny one goes forth sounding.
472: O <s>Indu</s> (Soma drop), flow for <s>Indra</s> accompanied by <s>Maruts</s>, most honey-sweet — seat yourself in the womb of the hymn.
473: This pressed shoot has [flowed] for intoxication, into the waters — the vigorous one, mountain-dwelling; like a hawk, he has seated himself in the womb.
474: Flow, O achiever of skill, for the gods to drink, O tawny one — intoxication for the <s>Maruts</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>.
475: The sounding <s>Soma</s>, mountain-dwelling, has streamed around through the filter — in all intoxications, you are present.
476: The dear poet [flows] around from heaven, placed in the waters of the granddaughter; with sounds he goes, of poetic wisdom.

477: The <s>Soma</s> drops, dripping intoxication, have gone forth for glory, for us the bountiful — pressed, they have stepped forth at the ceremony.
478: The wise <s>Soma</s> drops flow forth, leading the waters like waves — like mighty buffaloes through forests.
479: Flow, O <s>Indu</s>, O pressed bull; make us famous among people — destroy all hatreds.
480: For you are a bull with your radiance; we invoke you, the brilliant one — O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-purifying), beholder of heaven.
481: <s>Indu</s> has flowed forth, the conscious one, the beloved thought of poets — he releases the horse like a charioteer.
482: The swift <s>Soma</s> juices have been released, [flowing] for cattle, for horses — the bright ones, the powerful, [flowing] for heroes.
483: Flow, O god, for [long] life; may your intoxication reach <s>Indra</s> — mount <s>Vāyu</s> by your law.
484: <s>Pavamāna</s> (the Self-purifying) generated from heaven a wondrous thunder — the great light of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (universal fire).
485: Around, the sounding <s>Soma</s> drops, for intoxication, with a lofty hymn — they flow with sweetness in a stream.
486: The poet has flowed around, resting upon the wave of the river — bearing the beloved, much-desired song.

1.6.1.533: Forth goes the army-leader, the hero, at the head of the chariots, eager for cattle. His army rejoices. Making auspicious the <s>Indra</s>-invocations for his friends, <s>Soma</s> puts on his mighty garments.
1.6.1.534: Your sweet streams have flowed forth when, purified, you would pass through the woolen filter. O <s>Pavamāna</s> (self-purifying <s>Soma</s>), you purify yourself toward the realm of cattle, generating the sun, you filled [him] with hymns.
1.6.1.535: Sing forth! Praise the gods with songs! Impel <s>Soma</s> for great wealth. Let the sweet [juice] flow through the woolen filter. Let the divine drop sit in the jar.
1.6.1.536: Impelled, the begetter of heaven and earth sped forth like a chariot winning the prize. Going to <s>Indra</s>, sharpening his weapons, placing all goods in [<s>Indra</s>'s] hands.
1.6.1.537: When speech fashioned [the hymn] from the mind's longing, in the vanguard of the foremost, the law of the luminous one — then indeed the cows came lowing, desiring [him], to the dear lord <s>Indu</s> (drop/Soma) in the jar.
1.6.1.538: Together the sisters, the ten wise fingers, bow-bearing, groom the bull. The golden one ran around; born of the sun, he reached the wooden vessel like a prize-winning steed.
1.6.1.539: Upon him, as upon a prize-winner, the beautiful thoughts compete like clans [contending] before the sun. Selecting the waters, the most poetic one purifies himself — the prayer for the increase of the cattle-pen.
1.6.1.540: <s>Indu</s>, the prize-winner, purifies himself, the yoker of cattle. <s>Soma</s>, together with force, impels [himself] for <s>Indra</s>'s intoxication. He slays the demon, drives away hostility — the king of the sacred realm, making wide space.
1.6.1.541: With this purification, purify yourself, [and grant us] these goods. O <s>Indu</s>, run forth for <s>Indra</s> to the reservoir. Even the stunted one — whose speed is like the wind — the manly-counseled <s>Soma</s> placed [as a hero] for the thinker.
1.6.1.542: Great is that which <s>Soma</s>, the mighty bull, has done — when the embryo of the waters chose the gods. <s>Pavamāna</s> (purifying <s>Soma</s>) placed might in <s>Indra</s>; <s>Indu</s> (the drop) generated light in the sun.
1.6.1.543: The resounding speech has been released, as in a chariot-race, the first inspired thought fashioned by the mind. Ten sisters upon the woolen filter's back groom the conveyor to the sacred seats.
1.6.1.544: Like the waves of the waters rushing across, inspired thoughts hasten toward <s>Soma</s>. Bowing down, they come together and approach — the eager ones approach the eager one.

Sixth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, Second Half.
1.6.2.545: Having placed [<s>Soma</s>] as the foremost of the pressed drink, for the intoxicating one — drive away the dog, the long-tongued one, O friends!
1.6.2.546: This is <s>Pūṣan</s>, this is wealth, this is <s>Bhaga</s> — <s>Soma</s>, purifying himself, flows forth. The lord of all existence, he has surveyed both heaven and earth.
1.6.2.547: Pressed [juices], sweetest, intoxicating <s>Somas</s> for <s>Indra</s> — flowing through the filter, they have streamed [forth]. May your intoxications go to the gods!
1.6.2.548: The <s>Soma</s> drops purify themselves for us, the best knowers of the path. Friends, sweetly sounding, blameless, of good rites, finders of the light.
1.6.2.549: Flow toward us with the most prize-winning wealth, O <s>Indu</s>, desired by hundreds, bringing a thousandfold bounty, of great splendor, widely shining.
1.6.2.550: The guileless ones flow forth — the dear, desirable [gift] of <s>Indra</s>. Like mothers licking a newborn calf in the first stage of life.
1.6.2.551: For the delightful, bold [<s>Soma</s>], they string the bow of manly vigor. The bright [drops] go forth for the <s>Asura</s>'s adornment — [the <s>Soma</s>] flows, the great ones magnifying [him], at the forefront.
1.6.2.552: Around the delightful golden-brown one they purify with the woolen [filter]. He who goes with intoxication to all the gods together.
1.6.2.553: Of the one being pressed, a mortal desires the speech of the drink. Drive away the ungenerous dog! [The worshipers] have slain the hostile one, like the <s>Bhṛgus</s> [slew the demon].

1.6.2.554: He purifies himself over his dear [places], beloved, the great one, upon whose [streams] he grows great. Ascending the great, wide chariot of <s>Sūrya</s> (the sun), the all-seeing one.
1.6.2.555: May the <s>Indu</s> (Soma) drops flow for us with impetus; the golden ones, sounding loudly among the gods. May the hostilities and the niggardly be cast away; may the noble one be ours; may the thoughts [of worship] gain [their aim].
1.6.2.556: This honey-sweet one has cried out in the jar — <s>Indra</s>'s <s>vajra</s>, the most splendid of splendid forms. Toward <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the well-milking, ghee-dripping [cows] flow — the lowing ones stream with milk.
1.6.2.557: The drop has gone forth to <s>Indra</s>'s appointed [place] — a friend does not violate a friend's agreement. Like a youth with maidens, <s>Soma</s> mingles in the jar, going by a hundred paths.
1.6.2.558: The supporter of heaven, the active essence, purifies himself — the skill of the gods, to be cheered by men. The golden one, released like a steed among warriors — you freely create your glow in the rivers.
1.6.2.559: The bull of thoughts purifies himself, the all-seeing <s>Soma</s> — the advancer of days, of dawns, of heaven. The breath of the rivers, he has cried out in the jar — entering <s>Indra</s>'s heart through the sages.
1.6.2.560: Thrice seven milch cows milked [their milk] for him — the true mixture (<s>āśir</s>) in the highest vault. Four other worlds he created for his adornment — he who grew great by the [cosmic] ordinances.
1.6.2.561: For <s>Indra</s>, the well-pressed <s>Soma</s> flows around. Let sickness together with the <s>Rakṣas</s> (demon) perish! Let not the deceitful ones delight in your juice. Let the <s>Indu</s> drops be wealth-bringing here.
1.6.2.562: The reddish-brown bull <s>Soma</s> has been pressed; like a wondrous king, he has cried out toward the cattle. Purifying himself, he has passed through the woolen filter — like an eagle he has settled upon the ghee-rich birth-place.
1.6.2.563: Forth toward the god, the sweet <s>Indu</s> (Soma) drops have swelled — the cows [have come] like milch-cows to us. Seated on the sacred grass, speaking, with their udders, the tawny ones have placed [the <s>Soma</s>] as [their] filtered garment.
1.6.2.564: They anoint, they embellish, they anoint together; they lick [his] wisdom, the generous one; they anoint him. In the surging of the river, the golden-filtered ones seize the bull flying in the waters — the beast.
1.6.2.565: Your filter is spread wide, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>; the lord, you traverse all the limbs on every side. The one whose body is unheated does not attain that — only those who are matured, bearing [the fire], have shared in it.

body.translated_text: 566. Let these pressed [juices], the golden ones, go forth to <s>Indra</s> the bull; the drops, born in obedience, finding the light of heaven. || 566 || 567. Run forth, O <s>Soma</s>, ever-watchful, flow around for <s>Indra</s>, O drop; bring brilliant strength, finding the light of heaven. || 567 || 568. O friends, sit down; sing forth to the one being purified; adorn him like a child with sacrifices, for glory. || 568 || 569. Sing, O friends, to that one being purified, for your delight; like a child, they sweeten him with oblations, with praises. || 569 || 570. The breath, the child of the great [waters], impelling the thought of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), became dear to all, and [became] twofold. || 570 || 571. Flow forth for the invocation of the gods, O drop, with streams of vigor; O honey-sweet <s>Soma</s>, [come] to the vessel, our seat. || 571 || 572. <s>Soma</s>, being purified, runs with his wave through the woolen filter; <s>Pavamāna</s> (the Self-Purifying), crying aloud, [goes] before speech. || 572 || 573. A word is spoken to the purifying <s>Soma</s>, the sage; bear it like a gift; he delights in [our] praises. || 573 || 574. O drop, rich in cattle, rich in horses, pressed, O skilful one, like a bowman; pour the bright color [of the juice] upon the [milk of] cows. || 574 || 575. For us, the voices have sung to you, the finder of treasure; with [the milk of] cows we clothe your color. || 575 || 576. The golden one flows, the beloved one, overcoming deceptions with speed; flow forth to the praisers glory rich in heroes. || 576 || 577. <s>Soma</s>, being purified, flows around the honey-dripping vessel; the seven voices of the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (seers) have praised him. || 577 ||

body.translated_text: 578. Flow forth, O most honeyed one, O <s>Soma</s>, as the most intoxicating [drink] for <s>Indra</s>, the most wise in purpose; the great, most heaven-winning intoxicant. || 578 || 579. O lord of food, shine forth upon the one seeking the gods, O possessor of great, widely-famed splendor; open the middle receptacle, O youthful one. || 579 || 580. O pressers, pour around [the juice] like a horse, a hymn, reaching [its goal] like one crossing the sky, traversing the air, sprouting from the waters. || 580 || 581. This is that intoxication-producing, thousand-streamed bull, the milker of heaven, bearing all treasures. || 581 || 582. He is pressed, who is the bringer of treasures, who [is the bringer] of riches, who [is the bringer] of refreshments; <s>Soma</s>, who [is the bringer] of good dwellings. || 582 || 583. For you indeed, O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying), [know] the divine births, O most brilliant one, proclaiming immortality. || 583 || 584. Here, pressed with the stream, he flows through the woolen filters, the most intoxicating one, playing like a wave of the waters. || 584 || 585. He who [released] the ruddy [cows], who were within the rock — he freed the cows by force; you stretch out toward the pen, [rich in] cattle and horses; like a warrior, boldly break through! OṂ, like a warrior, boldly break through! || 585 ||

body.translated_text: <s>Āraṇya Ārcikaḥ</s> (Forest Hymn-Collection), <s>Āraṇya Kāṇḍam</s> (Forest Section). 586. O <s>Indra</s>, bring us the foremost, the most powerful, the abundant fame; when we would seize [it], O <s>vajra</s>-handed one, you have filled both worlds, O fair-lipped one. || 586 || 587. <s>Indra</s> is the king of the moving [world] and of peoples, ruling over that which assumes all forms; from there he gives treasures to the worshipper; he has impelled generosity, even to the one who stands near in praise. || 587 || 588. He whose [glory] in this dusty [world] is yoked [with strength], he who conquers people [and wins] the heavenly forest — great is the delight of <s>Indra</s>. || 588 || 589. Release from us the uppermost bond, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, and the lowest, and loosen the middle one; then, O <s>Āditya</s>, may we be sinless in your ordinance, for <s>Aditi</s>. || 589 || 590. Through you, O purifying <s>Soma</s>, may we ever choose out what is gained in the contest; may <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Sindhu</s>, Earth, and Heaven grant us that. || 590 || 591. Make this bull the one and only for me. || 591 || 592. Flow around, O finder of spaciousness, for <s>Indra</s> whom we worship, for <s>Varuṇa</s>, and for the <s>Maruts</s>. || 592 || 593. By these [hymns] may we win all the glories of the noble one, [all the glories] of men, striving [for them]. || 593 || 594. I am the first-born of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), before the gods [I bore] the name of the immortal; whoever gives me, he indeed preserves thus; I, who am food, eat the eater of food. || 594 ||

body.translated_text: 595. You upheld that [milk] among the dark and ruddy [cows]; the gleaming milk among the dappled ones. || 595 || 596. The dappled bull, the foremost one, has shone forth at the dawns; he bellows among the worlds, seeking the prize; the wise ones have formed his powers by his own power; the fathers, who watch over men, have received the embryo. || 596 || 597. <s>Indra</s> is united with the two bay horses, mingling with the voice-yoked ones; <s>Indra</s> is the <s>vajra</s>-wielder, the golden one. || 597 || 598. O <s>Indra</s>, help us in contests, and in those with a thousandfold [prizes]; O mighty one, with mighty aids. || 598 || 599. The first and the widely-spread is his name; [he whose] oblation is the oblation of the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> [meter]; from <s>Dhātṛ</s>, from the shining <s>Savitṛ</s>, and from <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> has won the <s>Rathantara</s> [chant]. || 599 || 600. O <s>Vāyu</s>, come hither with your team; this bright [Soma] has been prepared for you; you shall go to the house of the presser. || 600 || 601. When you were born, O <s>Maghavan</s>, unprecedented, for the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s>, then you spread out the earth, then you established also heaven. || 601 ||

body.translated_text: 602. May <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> <s>Prajāpati</s> establish in me splendor and glory, and the nourishing essence of the sacrifice — as [he established] the sky in heaven. || 602 || 603. May your milky streams flow together, may your prizes unite, may your bull-like powers [unite], O conqueror of foes; swelling to immortality, O <s>Soma</s>, bestow the highest glories in heaven. || 603 || 604. You, O <s>Soma</s>, [created] all these plants; you generated the waters; you [generated] the cows; you spread out the wide atmosphere; with light you dispelled the darkness. || 604 || 605. I praise <s>Agni</s>, the foremost priest (<s>purohita</s>), the divine officiant (<s>ṛtvij</s>) of the sacrifice, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), the greatest bestower of treasures. || 605 || 606. They discovered the first name of the cows; three times seven, the supreme names, they [discovered] among peoples; knowing [these names], they sang praises of the earth; the glorious, ruddy cows became manifest. || 606 || 607. Some flow together, others flow toward [them]; the rivers fill one common reservoir; the pure waters approach that pure one, shining brightly — the Son of Waters (<s>Apāṃ Napāt</s>). || 607 || 608. The auspicious young [Night] has arrived; she seeks to stir up the banners of the day; the auspicious one has become the resting-place of all the moving world — Night. || 608 || 609. For the mighty, bull-like, ruddy one — for <s>Jātavedas</s> (all-knowing <s>Agni</s>) — bring forth our word now to the assemblies; for <s>Vaiśvānara</s> (universal fire) this newest thought, pure like <s>Soma</s>, is purified, beautiful, for <s>Agni</s>. || 609 || 610. May all the gods hear my sacrifice; may both heaven and earth, and the Son of Waters (<s>Apāṃ Napāt</s>), [hear] my thought; may I not speak words that are to be despised; in your favor, O gods, may we rejoice in our inmost [being]. || 610 || 611. May heaven and earth [give me] glory; may <s>Indra</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> [give me] glory; may [<s>Bhaga</s>] find glory for me; may glory be bestowed upon me; may I be glorious; may I be the speaker in this assembly. || 611 || 612. I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of <s>Indra</s>, the first ones that the thunderbolt-wielder performed; he slew the serpent (<s>Ahi</s>), he pierced the [channels for] the waters, he split open the bellies of the mountains. || 612 || 613. I am <s>Agni</s> by birth, <s>Jātavedas</s> (the all-knowing); clarified butter is my eye, immortality is my mouth; I am the threefold hymn (<s>Arka</s>), the measurer of the atmosphere, the unceasing light; I am the entire oblation. || 613 || 614. <s>Agni</s> the inspired one protects the foremost station of the bird; the ever-young one protects the path of the sun; <s>Agni</s> protects at the navel the seven-headed one. || 614 ||

body.translated_text: 615. O <s>Agni</s>, shining forth when kindled, [your] tongue moves among the [offerings]; you, O <s>Agni</s>, the finder of wealth, have given us nourishment, splendor, and riches to behold. || 615 || 616. The spring seasons are indeed delightful; the summer seasons are indeed delightful; the rains, the autumns, the winter, and the cool season are indeed delightful. || 616 || 617. The <s>Puruṣa</s> (Cosmic Person) has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet; covering the earth on all sides, he extended beyond it by ten finger-breadths. || 617 || 618. Three-fourths of <s>Puruṣa</s> rose upward; one-fourth of him came to be here again; thence he spread in all directions into what eats and what does not eat. || 618 || 619. <s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this — what has been and what shall be; he is the lord of immortality; one-fourth of him is all beings; three-fourths of him is immortality in heaven. || 619 || 620. Such is his greatness, and <s>Puruṣa</s> is yet greater than this; all beings are one-fourth of him; the three-fourths, the immortal, is in heaven; that by which he rises beyond food, he is the ruler of immortality. || 620 || 621. From that was born <s>Virāj</s> (the shining one); from <s>Virāj</s> [was born] <s>Puruṣa</s>; when born, he extended beyond the earth behind and before. || 621 || 622. I deem you two, O Heaven and Earth, to be of great nourishment, you who spread out immeasurably over the distances; O Heaven and Earth, be gracious; release us from distress. || 622 || 623. O <s>Indra</s>, your two tawny [horses] are [like] mustaches to you, and your two tawny [steeds] are tawny; the poets, the men, the forest-going [sages] praise you. || 623 || 624. Whatever is the splendor of gold, or the splendor of cattle, or the splendor of truth, of <s>Brahman</s> — with that splendor we unite ourselves. || 624 || 625. Do give us, O <s>Indra</s>, a thousandfold sustenance with strength; for you, O resplendent one, are master of this great [wealth]; grant us wisdom, manly power, steadfast strength, and [make us] victorious over enemies among foes. || 625 || 626. May [the waters] rise with the bulls, with the calves, bearing all forms, with double udders; broad and wide be this realm for you; may these waters be of good access; be here. || 626 ||

body.translated_text: 627. O <s>Agni</s>, purify for us our life-spans; bring us swift vigor and food; drive far away ill fortune. || 627 || 628. May the resplendent, lofty one drink the <s>Soma</s> honey, placing life in the lord of the sacrifice, undiminished; he who, impelled by the wind, protects by himself, nourishes offspring, and shines forth in manifold ways. || 628 || 629. The wondrous face of the gods has risen — the eye of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Agni</s>; <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun), the soul of all that moves and stands, has filled heaven, earth, and the atmosphere. || 629 || 630. This dappled bull has come, sitting before [his] mother, going forth to [his] father, approaching heaven. || 630 || 631. He moves within the shining [realm]; from the breath of the great one, [all things] breathe in and breathe out; the great buffalo has shone forth upon the sky. || 631 || 632. He rules over thirty abodes; speech is offered to the bird [of the sun]; [he shines] daily at every dawn. || 632 || 633. Like thieves, the stars depart with the nights before the all-seeing <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun). || 633 || 634. His banners have been seen, his rays [spread] among the peoples, blazing like fires. || 634 || 635. Swift, all-beholding, light-making are you, O <s>Sūrya</s>; you illuminate the entire shining [realm]. || 635 || 636. Facing the gods' assemblies you rise, facing mankind; facing all [beings] so that [all] may behold the heavenly [light]. || 636 || 637. With which purifying eye, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, you survey the bustling people — [with that eye you see]. || 637 || 638. You ascend the sky, traversing the broad atmosphere, measuring the days with [your] nights, observing the births, O <s>Sūrya</s>. || 638 || 639. The <s>Sūrya</s> (Sun) yoked [his] seven bright mares, the daughters of the chariot; with these self-yoked [horses] he journeys. || 639 || 640. Seven tawny mares carry you in the chariot, O god <s>Sūrya</s>, bright-haired, all-seeing. || 640 || Thus ends the <s>Āraṇya</s> (Forest) section.

body.translated_text:
<s>Mahānāmnī Ārcika</s> (Great-Name Hymn Section).
3.0.0.0001: Know, O bountiful one, know the path! You have directed the quarters. Teach, O lord of powers, of the many [powers], O giver of much wealth! (641)
3.0.0.0002: With supports you [support] the stalk (<s>aṃśu</s>). O knowing one, awaken, O <s>Indra</s>, for our glory and nourishment! (642)
3.0.0.0003: For thus the mighty one [strives] for wealth and for prizes, O <s>vajra</s>-wielder! O most mighty, O <s>vajra</s>-wielder, you delight [in us]! O most bountiful, O <s>vajra</s>-wielder, you delight! Come! Drink! Be intoxicated! (643)
3.0.0.0004: Know [the way] to wealth and excellent heroism! Be the lord of prizes, following [our] desire. O most bountiful, O <s>vajra</s>-wielder, you delight — you who are the mightiest of heroes. (644)
3.0.0.0005: He who is the most bountiful of the generous ones, [shining] like the stalk, like [its] radiance — O wise one, lead us! <s>Indra</s> knows — praise him! (645)
3.0.0.0006: For <s>Śakra</s> (the Mighty) is the lord — him we call for aid, the conqueror unconquered. May he, [dwelling in] the sun, [carry us] beyond hostilities — [he whose] will and hymn are truth and greatness. (646)
3.0.0.0007: We call upon <s>Indra</s> for the winning of wealth — the conqueror, the unconquered. May he, [dwelling in] the sun, [carry us] beyond hostilities! May he, [dwelling in] the sun, [carry us] beyond hostilities! (647)
3.0.0.0008: Of the former [<s>Soma</s>], O stone-wielder, the stalk [is] for your intoxication. Place [us] in your favor, O beneficent one! Your fullness, O most mighty, is celebrated. For <s>Śakra</s> indeed is the lord — now you lay down that new [favor]. (648)
3.0.0.0009: O lord of people, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, let us speak together in battles! The hero who goes among the cattle — a well-disposed, undeceitful friend. (649)
Now the five <s>Purīṣa-padas</s> (Earth-Syllables):
3.0.0.0010: Thus indeed! Thus O <s>Agni</s>! Thus O <s>Indra</s>! Thus O <s>Pūṣan</s>! Thus O Gods! OṂ, thus indeed O Gods! (650)
Thus [end] the five <s>Purīṣa-padas</s>.

  4 1 1 01 01c abhi devāṃ iyakṣate .. 651
  4 1 1 01 02a abhi te madhunā payo 'tharvāṇo aśiśrayuḥ .
  4 1 1 01 02c devaṃ devāya devayu .. 652
  4 1 1 01 03a sa naḥ pavasva śaṃ gave śaṃ janāya śamarvate .
  4 1 1 01 03c śaṃ rājannoṣadhībhyaḥ .. 653
body.translated_text:
<s>Uttara Ārcika</s> (Later Hymn Section).
First <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, First Half.
<s>Asita Kāśyapa</s> or <s>Devala</s>. <s>Gāyatrī</s> [meter]. <s>Pavamāna Soma</s>.
4.1.1.01.01: Sing, O men, to <s>Pavamāna</s>, to the drop (<s>Indu</s>)! He seeks to reach the gods. (651)
4.1.1.01.02: The <s>Atharvans</s> have poured upon your [stream] honey-mixed milk — the divine one, for the god, the one desiring the gods. (652)
4.1.1.01.03: Flow forth for us, O [<s>Soma</s>], for the welfare of cattle, for the welfare of people, for the welfare of the steed! For the welfare of plants, O King! (653)

body.text:
kaśyapo mārīcaḥ. gāyatrī. pavamānaḥ somaḥ.
  4 1 1 02 01a davidyutatyā rucā pariṣṭobhantyā kṛpā .
  4 1 1 02 01c somāḥ śukrā gavāśiraḥ .. 654
  4 1 1 02 02a hinvāno hetṛbhirhita ā vājaṃ vājyakramīt .
  4 1 1 02 02c sīdanto vanuṣo yathā .. 655
  4 1 1 02 03a ṛdhaksoma svastaye saṃjagmāno divā kave .
  4 1 1 02 03c pavasva sūryo dṛśe .. 656
body.translated_text:
<s>Kaśyapa Mārīca</s>. <s>Gāyatrī</s>. <s>Pavamāna Soma</s>.
4.1.1.02.01: Flashing with radiance, resounding with splendor — the <s>Somas</s>, bright, mixed with cow's [milk]. (654)
4.1.1.02.02: Impelled, set in motion by the impellers, the prize-winner has stridden toward the prize — sitting down like [those who] conquer. (655)
4.1.1.02.03: Growing, O <s>Soma</s>, for well-being, having come together in heaven, O sage — flow forth for the sight of the sun! (656)

body.text:
śataṃ vaikhānasāḥ, gāyatrī, pavamānaḥ somaḥ.
  4 1 1 03 01a pavamānasya te kave vājintsargā asṛkṣate .
  4 1 1 03 01c arvanto na śravasyavaḥ .. 657
  4 1 1 03 02a acchā kośaṃ madhuścutamasṛgraṃ vāre avyaye .
  4 1 1 03 02c avāvaśanta dhītayaḥ .. 658
  4 1 1 03 03a acchā samudramindavo 'staṃ gāvo na dhenavaḥ .
  4 1 1 03 03c agmannṛtasya yonimā .. 659
body.translated_text:
<s>Śatam Vaikhānasas</s>. <s>Gāyatrī</s>. <s>Pavamāna Soma</s>.
4.1.1.03.01: O sage, your streams, O <s>Pavamāna</s>, have been released, O prize-winner — like steeds striving for fame. (657)
4.1.1.03.02: Toward the vessel dripping with honey, unwoven, in the sheep's [wool filter] — the devotions have cried aloud. (658)
4.1.1.03.03: Toward the ocean, the drops [flow], as cows [go] home, as milch cows [hasten] — they have reached the womb of cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>). (659)

body.text:
bharadvājo bārhaspatyaḥ, gāyatrī, agniḥ.
  4 1 1 04 01a agna ā yāhi vītaye gṛṇāno havyadātaye .
  4 1 1 04 01c ni hotā satsi barhiṣi .. 660
  4 1 1 04 02a taṃ tvā samidbhiraṅgiro ghṛtena vardhayāmasi .
  4 1 1 04 02c bṛhacchocā yaviṣṭhya .. 661
  4 1 1 04 03a sa naḥ pṛthu śravāyyamacchā deva vivāsasi .
  4 1 1 04 03c bṛhadagne suvīryam .. 662
body.translated_text:
<s>Bharadvāja Bārhaspatya</s>. <s>Gāyatrī</s>. <s>Agni</s>.
4.1.1.04.01: O <s>Agni</s>, come for our worship, praised, for the giving of oblations! Sit down as <s>Hotṛ</s> on the sacred grass! (660)
4.1.1.04.02: We augment you, O <s>Aṅgiras</s>, with kindling sticks and with ghee — blazing high, O youngest one! (661)
4.1.1.04.03: O god, you seek to win for us widely-heard [fame] — great heroic power, O <s>Agni</s>! (662)

body.text:
viśvāmitro gāthinaḥ jamadagnirvā, gāyatrī, mitrāvaruṇau.
  4 1 1 05 01a ā no mitrāvaruṇā ghṛtairgavyūtimukṣatam .
  4 1 1 05 01c madhvā rajāṃsi sukratū .. 663
  4 1 1 05 02a uruśaṃsā namovṛdhā mahnā dakṣasya rājathaḥ .
  4 1 1 05 02c drāghiṣṭhābhiḥ śucivratā .. 664
  4 1 1 05 03a gṛṇānā jamadagninā yonāvṛtasya sīdatam .
  4 1 1 05 03c pātaṃ somamṛtāvṛdhā .. 665
body.translated_text:
<s>Viśvāmitra Gāthina</s> or <s>Jamadagni</s>. <s>Gāyatrī</s>. <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>.
4.1.1.05.01: O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, sprinkle our pasture with ghee — with sweetness, O you of good deeds, [sprinkle] the realms! (663)
4.1.1.05.02: Of wide renown, nourished by homage, you two reign with the greatness of skill — with the most far-reaching [powers], O you of pure ordinances! (664)
4.1.1.05.03: Praised by <s>Jamadagni</s>, sit in the seat of cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>)! Drink the <s>Soma</s>, O you who increase <s>ṛta</s>! (665)

body.text:
irīmbiṭhiḥ kāṇvaḥ. gāyatrī. indraḥ.
  4 1 1 06 03a ā yāhi suṣumā hi ta indra somaṃ pibā imam .
  4 1 1 06 03c edaṃ barhiḥ sado mama .. 666
  4 1 1 06 03a ā tvā brahmayujā harī vahatāmindra keśinā .
  4 1 1 06 03c upa brahmāṇi naḥ śṛṇu .. 667
  4 1 1 06 03a brahmāṇastvā yujā vayaṃ somapāmindra sominaḥ .
  4 1 1 06 03c sutāvanto havāmahe .. 668
body.translated_text:
<s>Irīmbiṭhi Kāṇva</s>. <s>Gāyatrī</s>. <s>Indra</s>.
4.1.1.06.01: Come! For you have beautiful pressing. O <s>Indra</s>, drink this <s>Soma</s>! This is the sacred grass, my seat. (666)
4.1.1.06.02: May the two long-maned bay horses, yoked by the sacred word (<s>brahman</s>), carry you, O <s>Indra</s>! Hear our prayers! (667)
4.1.1.06.03: We, [united by] the sacred word, possessing <s>Soma</s>, <s>Soma</s>-pressers, call upon you, O <s>Indra</s>, <s>Soma</s>-drinker, with pressed [offerings]! (668)

body.text:
viśvāmitro gāthinaḥ. gāyatrī. indrāgnī.
  4 1 1 07 01a indrāgnī ā gataṃ sutaṃ gīrbhirnabho vareṇyam .
  4 1 1 07 01c asya pātaṃ dhiyeṣitā .. 669
  4 1 1 07 02a indrāgnī jarituḥ sacā yajño jigāti cetanaḥ .
  4 1 1 07 02c ayā pātamimaṃ sutam .. 670
  4 1 1 07 03a indramagniṃ kavicchadā yajñasya jūtyā vṛṇe .
  4 1 1 07 03c tā somasyeha tṛmpatām .. 671
body.translated_text:
<s>Viśvāmitra Gāthina</s>. <s>Gāyatrī</s>. <s>Indra</s>-<s>Agni</s>.
4.1.1.07.01: O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, come to the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] — the excellent, sky-like [juice], praised with songs! Drink of this, impelled by devotion! (669)
4.1.1.07.02: Of the praiser, together, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, the sacrifice goes forth, conscious. Drink this pressed [<s>Soma</s>] with this [prayer]! (670)
4.1.1.07.03: I choose <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, the poet's delight, by the impulse of the sacrifice. May they two be satisfied with <s>Soma</s> here! (671)

body.text:
amahīyurāṅgirasaḥ. gāyatrī. pavamānaḥ somaḥ.
  4 1 1 08 01a uccā te jātamandhaso divi sadbhūmyā dade .
  4 1 1 08 01c ugraṃ śarma mahi śravaḥ .. 672
  4 1 1 08 02a sa na indrāya yajyave varuṇāya marudbhyaḥ .
  4 1 1 08 02c varivovitpari srava .. 673
  4 1 1 08 03a enā viśvānyarya ā dyumnāni mānuṣāṇām .
  4 1 1 08 03c siṣāsanto vanāmahe .. 674
body.translated_text:
<s>Amahīyu Āṅgirasa</s>. <s>Gāyatrī</s>. <s>Pavamāna Soma</s>.
4.1.1.08.01: Your high-born [stream] of juice, established in heaven and on earth — [gives] fierce shelter, great glory. (672)
4.1.1.08.02: For us, to <s>Indra</s> the worshipful, to <s>Varuṇa</s>, to the <s>Maruts</s> — flow around, O giver of wide space! (673)
4.1.1.08.03: By these [streams], may we win all the glories of men, O noble one — striving, may we conquer! (674)

body.text:
4 1 1 09 01a punānaḥ soma dhārayāpo vasāno arṣasi .
  4 1 1 09 01c ā ratnadhā yonimṛtasya sīdasyutso devo hiraṇyayaḥ .. 675
  4 1 1 09 02a duhāna ūdhardivyaṃ madhu priyaṃ pratnaṃ sadhasthamāsadat .
  4 1 1 09 02c āpṛcchyaṃ dharuṇaṃ vājyarṣasi nṛbhirdhauto vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 676
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.09.01: Being purified, O <s>Soma</s>, you flow bearing [all], clothed in waters. You sit in the seat of <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic order), O bestower of treasures — a divine golden spring. (675)
4.1.1.09.02: Milking the heavenly udder, the dear, ancient [stream] has reached its abode. You flow, O prize-winner, sought, the support — washed by men, far-seeing. (676)

body.text:
4 1 1 10 01a pra tu drava pari kośaṃ ni ṣīda nṛbhiḥ punāno abhi vājamarṣa .
  4 1 1 10 01c aśvaṃ na tvā vājinaṃ marjayanto 'cchā barhī raśanābhirnayanti .. 677
  4 1 1 10 02a svāyudhaḥ pavate deva induraśastihā vṛjanā rakṣamāṇaḥ .
  4 1 1 10 02c pitā devānāṃ janitā sudakṣo viṣṭambho divo dharuṇaḥ pṛthivyāḥ .. 678
  4 1 1 10 03a ṛṣirvipraḥ puraetā janānāmṛbhurdhīra uśanā kāvyena .
  4 1 1 10 03c sa cidviveda nihitaṃ yadāsāmapīcyā3ṃ guhyaṃ nāma gonām .. 679
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.10.01: Rush forth, flow around the vessel, sit down! Being purified by men, flow toward the prize! Grooming you like a prize-winning horse, they lead [you] with cords toward the sacred grass. (677)
4.1.1.10.02: The divine drop (<s>Indu</s>), well-armed, flows forth — slayer of the blameless, guarding the settlements. Father of the gods, generator, the skilled one — the pillar of heaven, the support of the earth. (678)
4.1.1.10.03: The seer, the inspired one, the leader of peoples — the skillful, the wise <s>Uśanā</s>, with poetic art. He indeed discovered what was hidden, the secret, mystic name of the cows. (679)

body.text:
4 1 1 11 01a abhi tvā śūra nonumo 'dugdhā iva dhenavaḥ .
  4 1 1 11 01c īśānamasya jagataḥ svardṛśamīśānamindra tasthuṣaḥ .. 680
  4 1 1 11 02a na tvāvāṃ anyo divyo na pārthivo na jāto na janiṣyate .
  4 1 1 11 02c aśvāyanto maghavannindra vājino gavyantastvā havāmahe .. 681
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.11.01: O hero, we praise you loudly — like unmilked cows [lowing]. [You are] the lord of this moving [world], the beholder of heaven, the lord, O <s>Indra</s>, of the stationary [world]. (680)
4.1.1.11.02: No other equals you — neither divine nor earthly, neither born nor to be born. Desiring horses, O bountiful <s>Indra</s>, desiring cattle, O prize-seeker — we call upon you. (681)

body.text:
4 1 1 12 01a kayā naścitra ā bhuvadūtī sadāvṛdhaḥ sakhā .
  4 1 1 12 01c kayā śaciṣṭhayā vṛtā .. 682
  4 1 1 12 02a kastvā satyo madānāṃ maṃhiṣṭho matsadandhasaḥ .
  4 1 1 12 02c dṛḍhā cidāruje vasu .. 683
  4 1 1 12 03a abhī ṣu ṇaḥ sakhīnāmavitā jaritR^īṇām .
  4 1 1 12 03c śataṃ bhavāsyūtaye .. 684
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.12.01: By what [aid], O wondrous one, will you become our messenger, ever-growing friend? By what most mighty [power]? (682)
4.1.1.12.02: Who truly, of joys, is the most bountiful, who will be intoxicated by the juice? He breaks open even firm [fortresses] for wealth. (683)
4.1.1.12.03: Be, O [<s>Indra</s>], the helper of our friends, of our singers! May you be [present] a hundredfold for our aid! (684)

body.text:
4 1 1 13 01a taṃ vo dasmamṛtīṣahaṃ vasormandānamandhasaḥ .
  4 1 1 13 01c abhi vatsaṃ na svasareṣu dhenava indraṃ gīrbhirnavāmahe .. 685
  4 1 1 13 02a dyukṣaṃ sudānuṃ taviṣībhirāvṛtaṃ giriṃ na purubhojasam .
  4 1 1 13 02c kṣumantaṃ vājaṃ śatinaṃ sahasriṇaṃ makṣū gomantamīmahe .. 686
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.13.01: That wondrous, ordeal-enduring one — [gladdened] by the substance of wealth, by the juice — like milch cows [lowing] for a calf at dawn, we celebrate <s>Indra</s> with new songs. (685)
4.1.1.13.02: The sky-dweller, the generous giver, surrounded by powers — like a mountain, rich in nourishment — a rich prize, hundredfold, thousandfold — we seek quickly [one] rich in cattle. (686)

body.text:
4 1 1 14 01a tarobhirvo vidadvasumindraṃ sabādha ūtaye .
  4 1 1 14 01c bṛhadgāyantaḥ sutasome adhvare huve bharaṃ na kāriṇam .. 687
  4 1 1 14 02a na yaṃ dudhrā varante na sthirā muro madeṣu śipramandhasaḥ .
  4 1 1 14 02c ya ādṛtyā śaśamānāya sunvate dātā jaritra ukthyam .. 688
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.14.687: With penetrating [hymns], I [call] upon wealth-finding <s>Indra</s>, the resolute one, for your aid. Singing aloud, at the pressed <s>Soma</s> rite, I invoke [him] like one bringing tribute.
4.1.1.14.688: Him whom neither the defiant nor the firm-standing fools obstruct in [his] intoxications — [<s>Indra</s>], the lip-piece-wearing, [drinking] the juice — who gives the praiseworthy [gift] to the toiling, pressing worshiper.

body.text:
4 1 1 15 01a svādiṣṭhayā madiṣṭhayā pavasva soma dhārayā .
  4 1 1 15 01c indrāya pātave sutaḥ .. 689
  4 1 1 15 02a rakṣohā viśvacarṣaṇirabhi yonimayohate .
  4 1 1 15 02c droṇe sadhasthamāsadat .. 690
  4 1 1 15 03a varivodhātamo bhuvo maṃhiṣṭho vṛtrahantamaḥ .
  4 1 1 15 03c parṣi rādho maghonām .. 691
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.15.689: O <s>Soma</s>, purify yourself with the sweetest, most intoxicating stream — pressed for <s>Indra</s> to drink.
4.1.1.15.690: The demon-slayer, the all-seeing one, strikes against the birth-place of the metal [vessel]. He has settled in his seat in the wooden vessel.
4.1.1.15.691: You are the greatest giver of wide space, the most generous, the supreme slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>. Carry forth the wealth of the bountiful ones.

body.text:
4 1 1 16 01a pavasva madhumattama indrāya soma kratuvittamo madaḥ .
  4 1 1 16 01c mahi dyukṣatamo madaḥ .. 692
  4 1 1 16 02a yasya te pītvā vṛṣabho vṛṣāyate 'sya pītvā svarvidaḥ .
  4 1 1 16 02c sa supraketo abhyakramīdiṣo 'cchā vājaṃ naitaśaḥ .. 693
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.16.692: Purify yourself, O sweetest one, for <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Soma</s>, the most wisdom-finding intoxication, the great, most luminous intoxication.
4.1.1.16.693: Having drunk of you, the bull becomes virile; having drunk of this, [the priests become] finders of the light. He of excellent insight has stridden toward the prizes — going toward the reward with speed.

body.text:
4 1 1 17 01a indramaccha sutā ime vṛṣaṇaṃ yantu harayaḥ .
  4 1 1 17 01c śruṣṭe jātāsa indavaḥ svarvidaḥ .. 694
  4 1 1 17 02a ayaṃ bharāya sānasirindrāya pavate sutaḥ .
  4 1 1 17 02c somo jaitrasya cetati yathā vide .. 695
  4 1 1 17 03a asyedindro madeṣvā grābhaṃ gṛbhṇāti sānasim .
  4 1 1 17 03c vajraṃ ca vṛṣaṇaṃ bharatsamapsujit .. 696
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.17.694: Let these pressed, golden [drops] go toward <s>Indra</s>, the bull. The <s>Indu</s> drops, born obedient, finders of the light.
4.1.1.17.695: This one, pressed for <s>Indra</s>, purifies himself for the winning of the prize. <s>Soma</s> perceives [the way] to victory, as he knows [it].
4.1.1.17.696: In his intoxications, <s>Indra</s> seizes the prize-winning cup and carries the mighty <s>vajra</s> — the conqueror in the waters.

body.text:
4 1 1 18 01a purojitī vo andhasaḥ sutāya mādayitnave .
  4 1 1 18 01c apa śvānaṃ śnathiṣṭana sakhāyo dīrghajihvyam .. 697
  4 1 1 18 02a yo dhārayā pāvakayā pariprasyandate sutaḥ .
  4 1 1 18 02c induraśvo na kṛtvyaḥ .. 698
  4 1 1 18 03a taṃ duroṣamabhī naraḥ somaṃ viśvācyā dhiyā .
  4 1 1 18 03c yajñāya santvadrayaḥ .. 699
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.18.697: Having placed [<s>Soma</s>] as the foremost of the pressed drink, for the intoxicating one — drive away the dog, the long-tongued one, O friends!
4.1.1.18.698: He who, pressed, streams around with a purifying stream — <s>Indu</s>, to be prepared like a horse.
4.1.1.18.699: With all-directed thought, may the men [make] the hard-to-approach <s>Soma</s> ready — the pressing-stones for the sacrifice.

body.text:
4 1 1 19 01a abhi priyāṇi pavate canohito nāmāni yahvo adhi yeṣu vardhate .
  4 1 1 19 01c ā sūryasya bṛhato bṛhannadhi rathaṃ viṣvañcamaruhadvicakṣaṇaḥ.. 700
  4 1 1 19 02a ṛtasya jihvā pavate madhu priyaṃ vaktā patirdhiyo asyā adābhyaḥ .
  4 1 1 19 02c dadhāti putraḥ pitrorapīcyā3ṃ nāma tṛtīyamadhi rocanaṃ divaḥ .. 701
  4 1 1 19 03a ava dyutānaḥ kalaśāṃ acikradannṛbhiryemāṇaḥ kośa ā hiraṇyaye .
  4 1 1 19 03c abhī ṛtasya dohanā anūṣatādhi tripṛṣṭha uṣaso vi rājasi .. 702
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.19.700: He purifies himself over his dear [places], beloved, the great one, upon whose [streams] he grows great. Ascending the great, wide chariot of <s>Sūrya</s>, the all-seeing one.
4.1.1.19.701: The tongue of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) purifies the dear honey; the speaker, the undeceivable lord of this thought. The son places [it] — the hidden [name] of the parents — the third name upon the shining vault of heaven.
4.1.1.19.702: Shining, he has cried out into the jars, guided by men into the golden vessel. The milkings of <s>Ṛta</s> have flowed toward [him]; upon the triple-backed [ridge], you shine over the dawns.

body.text:
4 1 1 20 01a yajñāyajñā vo agnaye girāgirā ca dakṣase .
  4 1 1 20 01c prapra vayamamṛtaṃ jātavedasaṃ priyaṃ mitraṃ na śaṃsiṣam .. 703
  4 1 1 20 02a ūrjo napātaṃ sa hināyamasmayurdāśema havyadātaye .
  4 1 1 20 02c bhuvadvājeṣvavitā bhuvadvṛdha uta trātā tanūnām .. 704
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.20.703: Sacrifice after sacrifice to your <s>Agni</s>, song after song for [his] skill. May we ever praise <s>Jātavedas</s>, the immortal, the dear friend.
4.1.1.20.704: We impel the son of strength for the giving of oblations. May he be a helper in the contests for prizes, may he be an increaser, and a protector of [our] bodies.

body.text:
4 1 1 21 01a ehyū ṣu bravāṇi te 'gna itthetarā giraḥ .
  4 1 1 21 01c ebhirvardhāsa indubhiḥ .. 705
  4 1 1 21 02a yatra kva ca te mano dakṣaṃ dadhasa uttaram .
  4 1 1 21 02c tatrā yoniṃ kṛṇavase .. 706
  4 1 1 21 03a na hi te pūrtamakṣipadbhuvannemānāṃ pate .
  4 1 1 21 03c athā duvo vanavase .. 707
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.21.705: Come now, let me speak to you, O <s>Agni</s> — hear these other songs. With these <s>Soma</s> drops may you grow.
4.1.1.21.706: Wherever you place your mind and your superior skill — there you make your birthplace.
4.1.1.21.707: For no one has destroyed your merit, O lord of these beings. Thus you win [our] worship.

body.text:
4 1 1 22 01a vayamu tvāmapūrvya sthūraṃ na kaccidbharanto 'vasyavaḥ .
  4 1 1 22 01c vajriñcitraṃ havāmahe .. 708
  4 1 1 22 02a upa tvā karmannūtaye sa no yuvograścakrāma yo dhṛṣat .
  4 1 1 22 02c tvāmidhyavitāraṃ vavṛmahe sakhāya indra sānasim .. 709
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.22.708: We who are unpreceded, desiring aid, bearing [offerings] like a great [tribute], O wielder of the <s>vajra</s> — we invoke your wondrous [power].
4.1.1.22.709: At the work, for your aid, this young mighty one has come to us, who [acts] boldly. We have chosen you, O <s>Indra</s>, as helper, as friend, as winner of prizes.

body.text:
4 1 1 23 01a adhā hīndra girvaṇa upa tvā kāma īmahe sasṛgmahe .
  4 1 1 23 01c udeva gmanta udabhiḥ .. 710
  4 1 1 23 02a vārṇa tvā yavyābhirvardhanti śūra brahmāṇi .
  4 1 1 23 02c vavṛdhvāṃsaṃ cidadrivo divedive .. 711
  4 1 1 23 03a puñjanti harī iṣirasya gāthayorau ratha uruyuge vacoyujā .
  4 1 1 23 03c indravāhā svarvidā .. 712
body.translated_text:
4.1.1.23.710: O <s>Indra</s>, O song-lover, indeed toward you our desire hastens; we rush forth like [waters] rising, rising with [their] floods.
4.1.1.23.711: Like rains, the sacred prayers increase you, O hero, O stone-wielder — you who have grown great day after day.
4.1.1.23.712: They groom the two bay [horses] of the swift one with songs at the wide chariot of wide yoke — the speech-yoked ones, <s>Indra</s>-bearing, light-finding.

body.text:
prathama prapāṭhakaḥ . dvitīyo 'rdhaḥ
  4 1 2 01 01a pāntamā vo andhasa indramabhi pra gāyata .
  4 1 2 01 01c viśvāsāhaṃ śatkratuṃ maṃhiṣṭhaṃ carṣaṇīnām .. 713
  4 1 2 01 02a puruhūtaṃ puruṣṭutaṃ gāthānyā3ṃ sanaśrutam .
  4 1 2 01 02c indra iti bravītana .. 714
  4 1 2 01 03a indra inno mahonāṃ dātā vājānāṃ nṛtuḥ .
  4 1 2 01 03c mahāṃ abhijñvā yamat .. 715
body.translated_text:
First <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, Second Half.
4.1.2.713: Having drunk of the juice, sing forth to <s>Indra</s>! [Sing of] the all-conquering one of a hundredfold wisdom, the most generous among peoples.
4.1.2.714: Much-invoked, much-praised, famed of old in songs — say '<s>Indra</s>!'
4.1.2.715: <s>Indra</s>, the giver of great things to us, the lord of prizes, the champion among men — the great one has subdued [the enemies].

body.text:
4 1 2 02 01a pra va indrāya mādanaṃ haryaśvāya gāyata .
  4 1 2 02 01c sakhāyaḥ somapāvne .. 716
  4 1 2 02 02a śaṃsedukthaṃ sudānava uta dyukṣaṃ yatha naraḥ .
  4 1 2 02 02c cakṛmā satyarādhase .. 717
  4 1 2 02 03a tvaṃ na indra vājayustvaṃ gavyuḥ śatakrato .
  4 1 2 02 03c tvaṃ hiraṇyayurvaso .. 718
body.translated_text:
4.1.2.716: Sing forth the intoxicating [hymn] to <s>Indra</s>, the bay-horsed one, O friends, O <s>Soma</s>-drinkers!
4.1.2.717: Recite the hymn, O givers of good gifts; like men [singing] a luminous [song] — we have made [it] for the truly generous one.
4.1.2.718: You, O <s>Indra</s>, are prize-seeking for us; you are cattle-seeking, O hundred-powered one; you are gold-seeking, O <s>Vasu</s>.

body.text:
4 1 2 03 01a vayamu tvā tadidarthā indra tvāyantaḥ sakhāyaḥ .
  4 1 2 03 01c kaṇvā ukthebhirjarante .. 719
  4 1 2 03 02a na ghemanyadā papana vajrinnapaso naviṣṭau .
  4 1 2 03 02c tavedu stomaiściketa .. 720
  4 1 2 03 03a icchanti devāḥ sunvantaṃ na svapnāya spṛhayanti .
  4 1 2 03 03c yanti pramādamatandrāḥ .. 721
body.translated_text:
4.1.2.719: We, seeking just that, coming to you — we, your friends, O <s>Indra</s> — the <s>Kaṇvas</s> praise you with hymns.
4.1.2.720: No one else but [you] has drunk [thus], O wielder of the <s>vajra</s>, since the newest of deeds. By our praises alone he has perceived [this].
4.1.2.721: The gods seek one who presses [<s>Soma</s>]; they do not desire sleep. They go without weariness, surpassing intoxication.

body.text:
4 1 2 04 01a indrāya madvne sutaṃ pari ṣṭobhantu no giraḥ .
  4 1 2 04 01c arkamarccantu kāravaḥ .. 722
  4 1 2 04 02a yasminviśvā adhi śriyo raṇanti sapta saṃsadaḥ .
  4 1 2 04 02c indraṃ sute havāmahe .. 723
  4 1 2 04 03a trikadrukeṣu cetanaṃ devāso yajñamatnata .
  4 1 2 04 03c tamidvardhantu no giraḥ .. 724
body.translated_text:
4.1.2.722: Let our songs encompass the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] for <s>Indra</s> to drink. Let the poets sing the hymn of praise.
4.1.2.723: In whom all glories and the seven assemblies delight — we invoke that <s>Indra</s> at the pressing.
4.1.2.724: At the three-day [<s>Trikadrukas</s>] rites, the gods found the sacrifice that is consciousness. May our songs increase that same [<s>Indra</s>].

body.text:
4 1 2 05 01a ayaṃ ta indra somo nipūto adhi barhiṣi .
  4 1 2 05 01c ehīmasya dravā piba .. 725
  4 1 2 05 02a śācigo śācipūjanāyaṃ raṇāya te sutaḥ .
  4 1 2 05 02c ākhaṇḍala pra hūyase .. 726
  4 1 2 05 03a yaste śṛṅgavṛṣo ṇapātpraṇapātkuṇḍapāyyaḥ .
  4 1 2 05 03c nyasmiṃ dadhra ā manaḥ .. 727
body.translated_text:
4.1.2.725: This <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, is purified for you upon the sacred grass. Come, run, and drink of this!
4.1.2.726: O skilled one, honored by the skilled — this is pressed for your delight. O <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> (<s>Indra</s>), you are invoked!
4.1.2.727: Your horned grandson, the snorting one, to be drunk from the <s>kuṇḍa</s> (vessel) — upon him fix your mind.

body.text:
4 1 2 06 01a ā tū na indra kṣumantaṃ citraṃ grābhaṃ saṃ gṛbhāya .
  4 1 2 06 01c mahāhasti dakṣiṇena .. 728
  4 1 2 06 02a vidmā hi tvā tuvikūrmiṃ tuvideṣṇaṃ tuvīmagham .
  4 1 2 06 02c tuvimātramavobhiḥ .. 729
  4 1 2 06 03a na hi tvā śūra devā na martāso ditsantam .
  4 1 2 06 03c bhīmaṃ na gāṃ vārayante .. 730
body.translated_text:
4.1.2.728: O <s>Indra</s>, seize for us the rich, wondrous prize with your great right hand.
4.1.2.729: For we know you [to be] of mighty action, of mighty gifts, of mighty bounty, of mighty measure — with [your] aids.
4.1.2.730: Neither the gods nor the mortals, O hero, [can] restrain you when you wish to give — [you are] like a fearsome bull.

body.text:
4 1 2 07 01a abhi tvā vṛṣabhā sute sutaṃ sṛjāmi pītaye .
  4 1 2 07 01c tṛmpā vyaśnuhī madam .. 731
  4 1 2 07 02a mā tvā mūrā aviṣyavo mopahasvāna ā dabhan .
  4 1 2 07 02c mā kīṃ brahmadviṣaṃ vanaḥ .. 732
  4 1 2 07 03a iha tvā goparīṇasaṃ mahe mandantu rādhase .
  4 1 2 07 03c saro gauro yathā piba .. 733
body.translated_text:
4.1.2.731: O bull, I release to you the pressed [<s>Soma</s>], pressed for [your] drinking. Be satisfied! Fully enjoy the intoxication!
4.1.2.732: Let not the foolish, the heedless, or the mocking ones deceive you. Do not favor any hater of prayer.
4.1.2.733: Here, where cattle abound, let [the <s>Soma</s> drops] gladden you for great generosity. Drink like the wild buffalo at a lake.

body.text:
4 1 2 08 01a idam vaso sutamandhaḥ pibā supūrṇamudaram .
  4 1 2 08 01c anābhayinrarimā te .. 734
  4 1 2 08 02a nṛbhirdhautaḥ suto aśnairavyā vāraiḥ paripūtaḥ .
  4 1 2 08 02c aśvo na nikto nadīṣu .. 735
  4 1 2 08 03a taṃ te yavaṃ yathā gobhiḥ svādumakarma śrīṇantaḥ .
  4 1 2 08 03c indra tvāsmiṃtsadhamāde .. 736
body.translated_text:
4.1.2.734: O <s>Vasu</s>, drink this pressed drink — fill your belly full. Without fear we have given to you.
4.1.2.735: Washed by men, pressed by stones, purified through woolen filters — like a horse bathed in the rivers.
4.1.2.736: That [<s>Soma</s>], like barley [mixed] with milk, we have made sweet for you, enriching [it]. O <s>Indra</s>, [join us] at this common feast.

body.text:
4 1 2 09 01a idaṃ hyanvojasā sutaṃ rādhānāṃ pate .
  4 1 2 09 01c pibā tvā3sya girvaṇaḥ .. 737
  4 1 2 09 02a yaste anu svadhāmasatsute ni yaccha tanvam .
  4 1 2 09 02c sa tvā mamattu somyam .. 738
  4 1 2 09 03a pra te aśnotu kukṣyoḥ prendra brahmaṇā śiraḥ .
  4 1 2 09 03c pra bāhū śūra rādhasā .. 739
  4 1 2 10 01a ā tvetā ni ṣīdatendramabhi pra gāyata .
  4 1 2 10 01c sakhāya stomavāhasaḥ .. 740
  4 1 2 10 02a purūtamaṃ purūṇāmīśānaṃ vāryāṇām .
  4 1 2 10 02c indraṃ some sacā sute .. 741
  4 1 2 10 03a sa ghā no yoga ā bhuvatsa rāye sa purandhyā .
  4 1 2 10 03c gamadvājebhirā sa naḥ .. 742
body.translated_text: 737. For this [juice] has been pressed with vigor, O lord of gifts; drink of it, O lover of praise. || 737 || 738. Whatever [of your nature] dwelt in [your] own abode at the pressing, extend your body to it; may the <s>Soma</s>-draught delight you. || 738 || 739. May it reach your belly, may [it reach] your head, O <s>Indra</s>, through prayer; may [it reach] your arms, O hero, through bounty. || 739 || 740. Come here, sit down; sing forth to <s>Indra</s>, O friends, bearers of praise. || 740 || 741. The most bountiful of the bountiful, the lord of desirable treasures — <s>Indra</s>, when the <s>Soma</s> is pressed. || 741 || 742. May he indeed come to our aid, to our wealth, to our wisdom; may he come to us with prizes. || 742 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 11 01a yogeyoge tavastaraṃ vājevāje havāmahe .
  4 1 2 11 01c sakhāya indramūtaye .. 743
  4 1 2 11 02a anu pratnasyaukaso huve tuvipratiṃ naram .
  4 1 2 11 02c yaṃ te pūrvaṃ pitā huve .. 744
  4 1 2 11 03a ā ghā gamadyadi śravatsahasriṇībhirūtibhiḥ .
  4 1 2 11 03c vājebhirupa no havam .. 745
body.translated_text: 743. In every effort, the mightiest; in every contest we invoke, O friends, <s>Indra</s> for aid. || 743 || 744. In accordance with the ancient dwelling, I invoke the man of mighty retaliation; whom your father formerly invoked. || 744 || 745. May he indeed come, if he hears, with thousandfold protections, with prizes, to our invocation. || 745 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 12 01a indra suteṣu someṣu kratuṃ punīṣa ukthyam .
  4 1 2 12 01c vide vṛdhasya dakṣasya mahāṃ hi ṣaḥ .. 746
  4 1 2 12 02a sa prathame vyomani devānāṃ sadane vṛdhaḥ .
  4 1 2 12 02c supāraḥ suśravastamaḥ samapsujit .. 747
  4 1 2 12 03a tamu huve vājasātaya indraṃ bharāya śuṣmiṇam .
  4 1 2 12 03c bhavā naḥ sumne antamaḥ sakhā vṛdhe .. 748
body.translated_text: 746. O <s>Indra</s>, among the pressed <s>Soma</s> juices, purify [our] hymn-worthy purpose; [we] know the power of the mighty, for he is great. || 746 || 747. He, the increaser, [dwells] in the first firmament, in the seat of the gods; he who crosses well, of most excellent fame, the conqueror in the waters. || 747 || 748. Him I invoke for the winning of prizes — <s>Indra</s>, the spirited one, for battle; be our nearest friend in your favor, for our growth. || 748 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 13 01a enā vo agniṃ namasorjo napātamā huve .
  4 1 2 13 01c priyaṃ cetiṣṭhamaratiṃ svadhvaraṃ viśvasya dūtamamṛtam .. 749
  4 1 2 13 02a sa yojate aruṣā viśvabhojasā sa dudravatsvāhutaḥ .
  4 1 2 13 02c subrahmā yajñaḥ suśamī vasūnāṃ devaṃ rādho janānām .. 750
body.translated_text: 749. With this homage I invoke <s>Agni</s> for you, the offspring of strength, the dear, the most visible minister, whose rites are good, the immortal messenger of all. || 749 || 750. He yokes his ruddy [horses], the all-nourishing; he races when well-fed with oblations; the sacrifice of good prayers, the good worker of treasures, the divine bounty of men. || 750 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 14 01a pratyu adarśyāyatyū3cchantī duhitā divaḥ .
  4 1 2 14 01c apo mahī vṛṇute cakṣuṣā tamo jyotiṣkṛṇoti sūnarī .. 751
  4 1 2 14 02a udusriyāḥ sṛjate sūryaḥ sacā udyannakṣatramarcivat .
  4 1 2 14 02c taveduṣo vyuṣi sūryasya ca saṃ bhaktena gamemahi .. 752
body.translated_text: 751. She is seen coming, the daughter of heaven rising; the great one covers the darkness with her eye, the gracious one creates light. || 751 || 752. The sun releases the ruddy [cows] together with [his rising]; he rises, radiant like a star; may we, at your dawning, O <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), and the sun's, attain [prosperity] through our devotion. || 752 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 15 01a imā u vāṃ diviṣṭaya usrā havante aśvinā .
  4 1 2 15 01c ayaṃ vāmahve 'vase śacīvasū viśaṃviśaṃ hi gacchathaḥ .. 753
  4 1 2 15 02a yuvaṃ citraṃ dadathurbhojanaṃ narā codethāṃ sūnṛtāvate .
  4 1 2 15 02c arvāgrathaṃ samanasā ni yacchataṃ pibataṃ somyaṃ madhu .. 754
body.translated_text: 753. These heavenly dawns call to you, O <s>Aśvins</s>; I invoke you for aid, O possessors of power; for you visit tribe after tribe. || 753 || 754. You two bestow wonderful food, O heroes; you two impel [generosity] to the speaker of truth; bring your chariot near, being of one mind; drink the <s>Soma</s>-mead. || 754 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 16 01a asya pratnāmanu dyutaṃ śukraṃ duduhre ahrayaḥ .
  4 1 2 16 01c payaḥ sahasrasāmṛṣim .. 755
  4 1 2 16 02a ayaṃ sūrya ivopadṛgayaṃ sarāṃsi dhāvati .
  4 1 2 16 02c sapta pravata ā divam .. 756
  4 1 2 16 03a ayaṃ viśvāni tiṣṭhati punāno bhuvanopari .
  4 1 2 16 03c somo devo na sūryaḥ .. 757
body.translated_text: 755. Following his ancient light, the shameless [cows] have yielded the bright milk, the <s>Ṛṣi</s> (seer) of a thousandfold. || 755 || 756. This one, like the sun, is visible; this one runs through the pools, through the seven streams, toward heaven. || 756 || 757. This one, being purified, stands above all the worlds — <s>Soma</s>, like a god, like the sun. || 757 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 17 01a eṣa pratnena janmanā devo devebhyaḥ sutaḥ .
  4 1 2 17 01c hariḥ pavitre arṣati .. 758
  4 1 2 17 02a eṣa pratnena manmanā devo devebhyaspari .
  4 1 2 17 02c kavirvipreṇa vāvṛdhe .. 759
  4 1 2 17 03a duhānaḥ pratnamitpayaḥ pavitre pari ṣicyase .
  4 1 2 17 03c krandaṃ devāṃ ajījanaḥ .. 760
body.translated_text: 758. This one, by his ancient birth, a god pressed for the gods, the golden one, flows through the filter. || 758 || 759. This one, by his ancient thought, a god among the gods, the sage has grown great through the inspired one. || 759 || 760. Yielding the ancient milk, you are poured around the filter; crying aloud, you have begotten the gods. || 760 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 18 01a upa śikṣāpatasthuṣo bhiyasamā dhehi śatrave .
  4 1 2 18 01c pavamāna vidā rayim .. 761
  4 1 2 18 02a uṣo ṣu jātamapturaṃ gobhirbhaṅgaṃ pariṣkṛtam .
  4 1 2 18 02c induṃ devā ayāsiṣuḥ .. 762
  4 1 2 18 03a upāsmai gāyatā naraḥ pavamānāyendave .
  4 1 2 18 03c abhi devāṃ iyakṣate .. 763
body.translated_text: 761. Come near with instruction, place fear upon the enemy of the one who stands [in worship]; O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying), find wealth. || 761 || 762. The bright drop, born at dawn, reaching [its goal], adorned with [the milk of] cows — the gods have desired [it]. || 762 || 763. Sing, O men, to <s>Pavamāna</s> (the Self-Purifying), the drop; he strives toward the gods. || 763 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 19 01a pra somāso vipaścito 'po nayanta ūrmayaḥ .
  4 1 2 19 01c vanāni mahiṣā iva .. 764
  4 1 2 19 02a abhi droṇāni babhravaḥ śukrā ṛtasya dhārayā .
  4 1 2 19 02c vājaṃ gomantamakṣaran .. 765
  4 1 2 19 03a sutā indrāya vāyave varuṇāya marudbhyaḥ .
  4 1 2 19 03c somā arṣantu viṣṇave .. 766
body.translated_text: 764. The <s>Soma</s> juices, wise ones, flow forth like waves leading the waters, like buffaloes [rushing] through the forests. || 764 || 765. The tawny ones, with the stream of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), [flow] toward the wooden vessels; they have reached the prize rich in cattle. || 765 || 766. The <s>Soma</s> juices, pressed for <s>Indra</s>, for <s>Vāyu</s>, for <s>Varuṇa</s>, for the <s>Maruts</s>, flow forth to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. || 766 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 20 01a pra soma devavītaye sindhurna pipye arṇasā .
  4 1 2 20 01c aṃśoḥ payasā madiro na jāgṛviracchā kośaṃ madhuścutam .. 767
  4 1 2 20 02a ā haryato arjuno atke avyata priyaḥ sūnurna marjyaḥ .
  4 1 2 20 02c tamīṃ hinvantyapaso yathā rathaṃ nadīṣvā gabhastyoḥ .. 768
body.translated_text: 767. <s>Soma</s> has swelled for the invocation of the gods, like a river with its flood; intoxicating with the juice of the stalk, wakeful like a joyful one, [flowing] toward the honey-dripping vessel. || 767 || 768. The beloved, golden-hued one has clothed himself in the woolen [filter]; the dear one, like a son to be adorned; the active ones urge him on like a chariot, in the rivers, by [their] hands. || 768 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 21 01a pra somāso madacyutaḥ śravase no maghonām .
  4 1 2 21 01c sutā vidathe akramuḥ .. 769
  4 1 2 21 02a ādīṃ haṃso yathā gaṇaṃ viśvasyāvīvaśanmatim .
  4 1 2 21 02c atyo na gobhirajyate .. 770
  4 1 2 21 03a ādīṃ tritasya yoṣaṇo hariṃ hinvantyadribhiḥ .
  4 1 2 21 03c indumindrāya pītaye .. 771
body.translated_text: 769. The <s>Soma</s> juices, intoxication-producing, have stridden forth to our fame and to the [fame] of the generous ones, pressed at the assembly. || 769 || 770. Like a swan [coming] to [its] flock, he has enveloped the thought of all; like a steed, he is adorned with [the milk of] cows. || 770 || 771. Then the maidens of <s>Trita</s> urge on the golden one with the pressing-stones — the drop, for <s>Indra</s> to drink. || 771 ||

body.text:
4 1 2 22 01a ayā pavasva devayu rebhanpavitraṃ paryeṣi viśvataḥ .
  4 1 2 22 01c madhordhārā asṛkṣata .. 772
  4 1 2 22 02a pavate haryato harirati hvarāṃsi raṃhyā .
  4 1 2 22 02c abhyarṣa stotṛbhyo vīravadyaśaḥ .. 773
  4 1 2 22 03a pra sunvānāsyāndhaso marto na vaṣṭa tadvacaḥ .
  4 1 2 22 03c apa śvānamarādhasaṃ hatā makhaṃ na bhṛgavaḥ .. 774
body.translated_text: 772. Flow with this [stream], O god-seeking one; roaring, you pass through the filter on every side; streams of honey have been released. || 772 || 773. The golden one, the beloved, flows forth, overcoming deceptions with speed; flow forth to the praisers glory rich in heroes. || 773 || 774. Like a mortal, one desires the word of the pressed juice of the one being pressed; drive away the niggardly dog; slay the fiend, like the <s>Bhṛgus</s>. || 774 ||

body.text:
dvitīya prapāṭhakaḥ . prathamo 'rdhaḥ
  4 2 1 01 01a pavasva vāco agriyaḥ soma citrābhirūtibhiḥ .
  4 2 1 01 01c abhi viśvāni kāvyā .. 775
  4 2 1 01 02a tvaṃ samudriyā apo 'griyo vāca īrayan .
  4 2 1 01 02c pavasva viśvacarṣaṇe .. 776
  4 2 1 01 03a tubhyemā bhuvanā kave mahimne soma tasthire .
  4 2 1 01 03c tubhyaṃ dhāvanti dhenavaḥ .. 777
body.translated_text: Second <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), First Half. 775. Flow, O <s>Soma</s>, foremost of utterances, with wonderful aids, over all poetic wisdoms. || 775 || 776. You, the foremost, setting in motion the oceanic waters, the speech — flow, O all-seeing one. || 776 || 777. For you, O sage <s>Soma</s>, these worlds have stood still in their greatness; for you the milch-cows run. || 777 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 02 01a pavasvendo vṛṣā sutaḥ kṛdhī no yaśaso jane .
  4 2 1 02 01c viśvā apa dviṣo jahi .. 778
  4 2 1 02 02a yasya te sakhye vayaṃ sāsahyāma pṛtanyataḥ .
  4 2 1 02 02c tavendo dyumna uttame .. 779
  4 2 1 02 03a yā te bhīmānyāyudhā tigmāni santi dhūrvaṇe .
  4 2 1 02 03c rakṣā samasya no nidaḥ .. 780
body.translated_text: 778. Flow, O <s>Indu</s> (Soma-drop), pressed as a bull; make us renowned among men; slay all hatreds. || 778 || 779. In whose friendship we may conquer those who attack us — in your highest splendor, O <s>Indu</s> (Soma-drop). || 779 || 780. Your fearsome weapons, sharp [and ready] for the oppressor — with those protect us from every reproach. || 780 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 03 01a vṛṣā soma dyumāṃ asi vṛṣā deva vṛṣavrataḥ .
  4 2 1 03 01c vṛṣā dharmāṇi dadhriṣe .. 781
  4 2 1 03 02a vṛṣṇaste vṛṣṇyaṃ śavo vṛṣā vanaṃ vṛṣā sutaḥ .
  4 2 1 03 02c sa tvaṃ vṛṣanvṛṣedasi .. 782
  4 2 1 03 03a aśvo na cakrado vṛṣā saṃ gā indo samarvataḥ .
  4 2 1 03 03c vi no rāye duro vṛdhi .. 783
body.translated_text: 781. O <s>Soma</s>, you are a bull, brilliant; you are a bull, O god, whose vow is bull-like; as a bull you have upheld the ordinances. || 781 || 782. Of the bull, your strength is bull-like; as a bull [you win] the forest; pressed as a bull — you, O bull, are the showerer of rain. || 782 || 783. Like a horse, you neigh, O bull; gather the cows, gather the contests; open wide the doors for our wealth. || 783 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 04 01a vṛṣā hyasi bhānunā dyumantaṃ tvā havāmahe .
  4 2 1 04 01c pavamāna svardṛśam .. 784
  4 2 1 04 02a yadadbhiḥ pariśicyase marmṛjyamāna āyubhiḥ .
  4 2 1 04 02c droṇe sadhasthamaśnuṣe .. 785
  4 2 1 04 03a ā pavasva suvīryaṃ mandamānaḥ svāyudha .
  4 2 1 04 03c iho ṣvindavā gahi .. 786
body.translated_text: 784. For you are a bull with your radiance; we invoke you, O brilliant one, O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying), beholder of the sun. || 784 || 785. When you are poured around with waters, being polished by the life-forces, you reach your seat in the wooden vessel. || 785 || 786. Flow forth with heroic power, rejoicing, O well-armed one; come hither, O <s>Indu</s> (Soma-drop). || 786 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 05 01a pavamānasya te vayaṃ pavitramabhyundataḥ .
  4 2 1 05 01c sakhitvamā vṛṇīmahe .. 787
  4 2 1 05 02a ye te pavitramūrmayo 'bhikṣaranti dhārayā .
  4 2 1 05 02c tebhirnaḥ soma mṛḍaya .. 788
  4 2 1 05 03a sa naḥ punāna ā bhara rayiṃ vīravatīmiṣam
  4 2 1 05 03c īśānaḥ soma viśvataḥ .. 789
body.translated_text: 787. O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying), we choose the friendship of your filter, as you surge up. || 787 || 788. Those waves of yours that flow past the filter in a stream — with those, O <s>Soma</s>, be gracious to us. || 788 || 789. O purifying one, bring us wealth, nourishment rich in heroes, O <s>Soma</s>, you who rule over all. || 789 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 06 01a agniṃ dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe hotāraṃ viśvavedasam .
  4 2 1 06 01c asya yajñasya sukratum .. 790
  4 2 1 06 02a agnimagniṃ havīmabhiḥ sadā havanta viśpatim .
  4 2 1 06 02c havyavāhaṃ purupriyam .. 791
  4 2 1 06 03a agne devāṃ ihā vaha jajñāno vṛktabarhiṣe .
  4 2 1 06 03c asi hotā na īḍyaḥ .. 792
body.translated_text: 790. We choose <s>Agni</s> as our messenger, the <s>Hotṛ</s> (invoking priest), the all-knowing one, the wise performer of this sacrifice. || 790 || 791. <s>Agni</s> upon <s>Agni</s> — with oblations they ever invoke the lord of the household, the bearer of oblations, dear to many. || 791 || 792. O <s>Agni</s>, being born, bring the gods hither to him who has spread the sacred grass; you are our praiseworthy <s>Hotṛ</s>. || 792 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 07 01a mitraṃ vayaṃ havāmahe varuṇaṃ somapītaye .
  4 2 1 07 01c ya jātā pūtadakṣasā .. 793
  4 2 1 07 02a ṛtena yāvṛtāvṛdhāvṛtasya jyotiṣaspatī .
  4 2 1 07 02c tā mitrāvaruṇā huve .. 794
  4 2 1 07 03a varuṇaḥ prāvitā bhuvanmitro viśvābhirūtibhiḥ .
  4 2 1 07 03c karatāṃ naḥ surādhasaḥ .. 795
body.translated_text: 793. We invoke <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> for the <s>Soma</s>-drinking — they who are born with purified skill. || 793 || 794. Through <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), you two who are nurtured by <s>Ṛta</s>, lords of the light of <s>Ṛta</s> — I invoke those two, <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>. || 794 || 795. May <s>Varuṇa</s> be our protector and <s>Mitra</s> with all [his] aids; may these most bountiful ones grant us [blessings]. || 795 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 08 01a indramidgāthino bṛhadindramarkebhirarkiṇaḥ .
  4 2 1 08 01c indraṃ vāṇīranūṣata .. 796
  4 2 1 08 02a indra iddharyoḥ sacā sammiśla ā vacoyujā .
  4 2 1 08 02c indro vajrī hiraṇyayaḥ .. 797
  4 2 1 08 03a indra vājeṣu no 'va sahasrapradhaneṣu ca .
  4 2 1 08 03c ugra ugrābhirūtibhiḥ .. 798
  4 2 1 08 04a indro dīrdhāya cakṣasa ā sūryaṃ rohayaddivi .
  4 2 1 08 04c vi gobhiradrimairayat .. 799
body.translated_text: 796. The singers sang aloud of <s>Indra</s>; the chanters of <s>Arka</s> hymns [praised] <s>Indra</s> with their chants; the songs praised <s>Indra</s>. || 796 || 797. <s>Indra</s> indeed is in company with his two tawny [horses], mingled with the word-yoked [hymns]; <s>Indra</s> the thunderbolt-wielder is golden. || 797 || 798. O <s>Indra</s>, help us in the winning of prizes and in contests of a thousand [stakes], mighty one, with mighty aids. || 798 || 799. <s>Indra</s> raised the sun aloft in heaven for long sight; with [his] rays he shattered the rock. || 799 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 09 01a indre agnā namo bṛhatsuvṛktimerayāmahe .
  4 2 1 09 01c dhiyā dhenā avasyavaḥ .. 800
  4 2 1 09 02a tā hi śaśvanta īḍata itthā viprāsa ūtaye .
  4 2 1 09 02c sabādho vājasātaye .. 801
  4 2 1 09 03a tā vāṃ gīrbhirvipanyuvaḥ prayasvanto havāmahe .
  4 2 1 09 03c medhasātā saniṣyavaḥ .. 802
body.translated_text: 800. To <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> we offer great homage and a well-fashioned hymn, with devotion, [like] a milch-cow, seeking protection. || 800 || 801. For the wise ones have constantly praised those two in this way, for aid, for the winning of prizes in distress. || 801 || 802. With songs, O you two who delight in praise, we invoke you, offering [oblations], seekers of gain, winning the sacrifice. || 802 ||

body.text:

  4 2 1 10 02a taṃ tvā dharttāramoṇyo3ḥ pavamāna svardṛśam .
  4 2 1 10 02c hinve vājeṣu vājinam .. 804
  4 2 1 10 03a ayā citto vipānayā hariḥ pavasva dhārayā .
  4 2 1 10 03c yujaṃ vājeṣu codaya .. 805
body.translated_text: 803. Flow forth, O bull, in a stream, intoxicating for the one accompanied by the <s>Maruts</s>; bestowing [gifts] and establishing [them] with might. || 803 || 804. You, the supporter of heaven and earth, O <s>Pavamāna</s> (self-purifying <s>Soma</s>), the beholder of heaven — I urge you on, the prize-winner, among the prizes. || 804 || 805. By this inspired [song], O tawny one, flow forth in a stream; urge on your companion in the contests. || 805 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 11 01a vṛṣā śoṇo abhikanikradadgā nadayanneṣi pṛthivīmuta dyām .
