  4 2 1 11 02a rasāyyaḥ payasā pinvamāna īrayanneṣi madhumantamaṃśum .
  4 2 1 11 02c pavamāna santanimeṣi kṛṇvannindrāya soma pariṣicyamānaḥ .. 807
  4 2 1 11 03a evā pavasva madiro madāyodagrābhasya namayanvadhasnum .
  4 2 1 11 03c pari varṇaṃ bharamāṇo ruśantaṃ gavyurno arṣa pari soma siktaḥ .. 808
body.translated_text: 806. The reddish bull, bellowing loudly, goes forth, making the earth and the sky resound; like the battle-cry of <s>Indra</s> heard in combat, you rush forth, impelling this speech. || 806 || 807. Rich in juices, swelling with milky sap, you go forth, sending the honey-sweet drop; O <s>Pavamāna</s> (self-purifying <s>Soma</s>), you go forth creating [the offering] as you are poured around for <s>Indra</s>. || 807 || 808. Thus flow forth, O intoxicating one, for the intoxication; bowing down the weapon of the one who seizes from above; bearing around the shining color, seeking cattle, flow forth, O <s>Soma</s>, when poured. || 808 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 12 01a tvāmiddhi havāmahe sātau vājasya kāravaḥ .
  4 2 1 12 01c tvāṃ vṛtreṣvindra satpatiṃ narastvāṃ kāṣṭhāsvarvataḥ .. 809
  4 2 1 12 02a sa tvaṃ naścitra vajrahasta dhṛṣṇuyā maha stavāno adrivaḥ .
  4 2 1 12 02c gāmaśvaṃ rathyamindra saṃ kira satrā vājaṃ na jigyuṣe .. 810
body.translated_text: 809. For you indeed we invoke, we the poets, at the winning of the prize; you, O <s>Indra</s>, the true lord among men in battles against foes; you, the possessor of wealth in the contests. || 809 || 810. You, O wondrous one, O thunderbolt-wielder, boldly, O greatly praised one, O lord of the pressing-stone — scatter for us cows, horses, and chariot[-wealth], O <s>Indra</s>, the entire prize as if for a conqueror. || 810 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 13 01a abhi pra vaḥ surādhasamindramarca yathā vide .
  4 2 1 13 01c yo jaritṛbhyo maghavā purūvasuḥ sahasreṇeva śikṣati .. 811
  4 2 1 13 02a śatānīkeva pra jigāti dhṛṣṇuyā hanti vṛtrāṇi dāśuṣe .
  4 2 1 13 02c gireriva pra rasā asya pinvire datrāṇi purubhojasaḥ .. 812
body.translated_text: 811. Sing forth to <s>Indra</s>, the most bountiful, as you know how; he who, being <s>Maghavan</s> (the generous one) and abundantly wealthy, bestows upon the singers as if with thousands. || 811 || 812. He advances boldly like [a warrior] with a hundred faces, slaying foes for the worshipper; from him, as from a mountain, the streams of gifts flow forth — the abundantly nourishing one. || 812 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 14 01a tvāmidā hyo naro 'pīpyanvajrinbhūrṇayaḥ .
  4 2 1 14 01c sa indra stomavāhasa iha śrudhyupa svasaramā gahi .. 813
  4 2 1 14 02a matsvā suśiprinharivastamīmahe tvayā bhūṣanti vedhasaḥ .
  4 2 1 14 02c tava śravāṃsyupamānyukthya suteṣvindra girvaṇaḥ .. 814
body.translated_text: 813. Men have long approached you, O thunderbolt-wielder, the shining one; hear us here, O <s>Indra</s>, praiser-bearing one, and come to [our] sister-pressing. || 813 || 814. Rejoice, O beautiful-cheeked, tawny-horsed one — we seek you; the wise ones adorn themselves with you; your glories, O <s>Indra</s>, lover of songs, are worthy of comparison, worthy of hymns at the pressings. || 814 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 15 01a yaste mado vareṇyastenā pavasvāndhasā .
  4 2 1 15 01c devāvīraghaśaṃsahā .. 815
  4 2 1 15 02a jaghnirvṛtramamitriyaṃ sasnirvājaṃ divedive .
  4 2 1 15 02c goṣātiraśvasā asi .. 816
  4 2 1 15 03a sammiślo aruṣo bhuvaḥ sūpasthābhirna dhenubhi .
  4 2 1 15 03c sīdaṃ cchyeno na yonimā .. 817
body.translated_text: 815. That choicest intoxication of yours — by that, flow forth, O <s>Soma</s> juice, O divine one, O slayer of the malicious. || 815 || 816. You have slain the hostile <s>Vṛtra</s>, you have won the prize day after day; you are the winner of cattle, the winner of horses. || 816 || 817. The ruddy one has mingled with the fair-stationed milch-cows; sitting down like a falcon upon his seat. || 817 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 16 01a ayaṃ pūṣā rayirbhagaḥ somaḥ punāno arṣati .
  4 2 1 16 01c patirviśvasya bhūmano vyakhyadrodasī ubhe .. 818
  4 2 1 16 02a samu priyā anūṣata gāvo madāya ghṛṣvayaḥ .
  4 2 1 16 02c somāsaḥ kṛṇvate pathaḥ pavamānāsa indavaḥ .. 819
  4 2 1 16 03a ya ojiṣṭhastamā bhara pavamāna śravāyyam .
  4 2 1 16 03c yaḥ pañca carṣaṇīrabhi rayiṃ yena vanāmahe .. 820
body.translated_text: 818. This <s>Soma</s>, being purified, flows forth — <s>Pūṣan</s>, wealth, <s>Bhaga</s> (fortune); the lord of all existence, he has illumined both heaven and earth. || 818 || 819. The dear, bold [drops] have sung together, the <s>Soma</s> drops, for intoxication; the self-purifying drops make their paths, the <s>Soma</s> drops. || 819 || 820. That which is mightiest — bring it, O <s>Pavamāna</s>, [you who are] worthy of fame; the wealth that [prevails] over the five races, by which we may conquer. || 820 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 17 01a vṛṣā matīnāṃ pavate vicakṣaṇaḥ somo ahnāṃ pratarītoṣasāṃ divaḥ .
  4 2 1 17 01c prāṇā sindhūnāṃ kalaśāṃ acikradadindrasya hārdyāviśanmanīṣibhiḥ .. 821
  4 2 1 17 02a manīṣibhiḥ pavate pūrvyaḥ kavirnṛbhiryataḥ pari kośāṃ asiṣyadat .
  4 2 1 17 02c tritasya nāma janayanmadhu kṣarannindrasya vāyūṃ sakhyāya vardhayan .. 822
  4 2 1 17 03a ayaṃ punāna uṣaso arocayadayaṃ sindhubhyo abhavadu lokakṛt .
  4 2 1 17 03c ayaṃ triḥ sapta duduhāna āśiraṃ somo hṛde pavate cāru matsaraḥ .. 823
body.translated_text: 821. The bull of thoughts, the all-seeing <s>Soma</s>, flows forth — the furtherer of days, of dawns, of heaven; the life-breath of the rivers, he has cried aloud into the vessels, entering the heart of <s>Indra</s> through the wise. || 821 || 822. The ancient seer, purified by the wise, flows from the men who stretch [the filter]; producing the name of <s>Trita</s>, streaming honey, increasing the friendship of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>. || 822 || 823. This one, being purified, illumined the dawns; this one became the world-maker for the rivers; this one, being milked, yielded thrice seven portions of the mixture; <s>Soma</s> flows forth, the beautiful, intoxicating [one], into the heart. || 823 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 18 01a evā hyasi vīrayurevā śūra uta sthirah .
  4 2 1 18 01c evā te rādhyaṃ manaḥ .. 824
  4 2 1 18 02a evā rātistuvīmagha viśvebhirdhāyi dhātṛbhiḥ .
  4 2 1 18 02c adhā cidindra naḥ sacā .. 825
  4 2 1 18 03a mo ṣu brahmeva tadindrayurbhuvo vājānāṃ pate .
  4 2 1 18 03c matsvā sutasya gomataḥ .. 826
body.translated_text: 824. Thus indeed you are hero-seeking, thus, O hero, also steadfast; thus is your gracious mind. || 824 || 825. Thus your gift, O mightily wealthy one, is established by all bestowers; yet, O <s>Indra</s>, be with us. || 825 || 826. Do not be, O lord of prizes, [merely] like a priest [in words]; rejoice in the pressed milk-mixed [<s>Soma</s>]. || 826 ||

body.text:
4 2 1 19 01a indraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhantsamudravyacasaṃ giraḥ .
  4 2 1 19 01c rathītamaṃ rathīnāṃ vājānāṃ satpatiṃ patim .. 827
  4 2 1 19 02a sakhye ta indra vājino mā bhema śavasaspate .
  4 2 1 19 02c tvāmabhi pra nonumo jetāramaparājitam .. 828
  4 2 1 19 03a pūrvīrindrasya rātayo na vi dasyantyūtayaḥ .
  4 2 1 19 03c yadā vājasya gomata stotṛbhyo maṃhate magham .. 829
body.translated_text: 827. All songs have magnified <s>Indra</s>, who is wide as the ocean — the best charioteer of charioteers, the true lord of prizes, the lord [of all]. || 827 || 828. In your friendship, O <s>Indra</s>, O lord of prizes, may we not fear, O lord of strength; we praise you, the conqueror, the unvanquished. || 828 || 829. Many are the gifts of <s>Indra</s>; his aids do not fail; when to the singers he bestows the bounty of cattle-rich prize. || 829 ||

body.text:
dvitīya prapāṭhakaḥ . dvitīyo 'rdhaḥ
  4 2 2 01 01a eta asṛgramindavastiraḥ pavitramāśavaḥ .
  4 2 2 01 01c viśvānyabhi saubhagā .. 830
  4 2 2 01 02a vighnanto duritā puru sugā tokāya vājinaḥ .
  4 2 2 01 02c tmanā kṛṇvanto arvataḥ .. 831
  4 2 2 01 03a kṛṇvanto varivo gave 'bhyarṣanti suṣṭutim .
  4 2 2 01 03c iḍāmasmabhyaṃ saṃyatam .. 832
body.translated_text: Second <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), Second Half. 830. These swift drops have flowed through the filter, [bringing] all good fortune. || 830 || 831. Destroying many evils, easy of access, prize-winning for offspring, making themselves swift by their own power. || 831 || 832. Making room for the cow, they flow toward the well-praised [filter], [bringing] <s>Iḍā</s> (nourishment) united for us. || 832 ||

body.text:
4 2 2 02 01a rājā medhābhirīyate pavamāno manāvadhi .
  4 2 2 02 01c antarikṣeṇa yātave .. 833
  4 2 2 02 02a ā naḥ soma saho juvo rūpaṃ na varcase bhara .
  4 2 2 02 02c suṣvāṇo devavītaye .. 834
  4 2 2 02 03a ā na indo śatagvinaṃ gavāṃ poṣaṃ svaśvyam .
  4 2 2 02 03c vahā bhagattimūtaye .. 835
body.translated_text: 833. The king flows forth, purified by [the priests'] wisdom, upon the mind; traveling through the atmosphere. || 833 || 834. O <s>Soma</s>, bring us strength and swift vigor; bring [us] the form of splendor, being well-pressed for the approach of the gods. || 834 || 835. O drop (<s>Indu</s>), bring us hundredfold cattle-wealth, prosperity of cows, and abundance of horses; bring us share of fortune for our aid. || 835 ||

body.text:
4 2 2 03 01a taṃ tvā nṛmṇāni bibhrataṃ sadhastheṣu maho divaḥ .
  4 2 2 03 01c cāruṃ sukṛtyayemahe .. 836
  4 2 2 03 02a saṃvṛktadhṛṣṇumukthyaṃ mahāmahivrataṃ madam .
  4 2 2 03 02c śataṃ puro rurukṣaṇim .. 837
  4 2 2 03 03a atastvā rayirabhyayadrājānaṃ sukrato divaḥ .
  4 2 2 03 03c suparṇo avyathī bharat .. 838
  4 2 2 03 04a adhā hinvāna indriyaṃ jyāyo mahitvamānaśe .
  4 2 2 03 04c abhiṣṭikṛdvicarṣaṇiḥ .. 839
  4 2 2 03 05a viśvasmā itsvardṛśe sādhāraṇaṃ rajasturam .
  4 2 2 03 05c gopāmṛtasya virbharat .. 840
body.translated_text: 836. You who bear manly powers, in the seats of the great heaven — the beautiful one, we seek to win through good deeds. || 836 || 837. The bold, the irresistible, the praiseworthy, the great, of great vows, the intoxicating one, who would break through a hundred forts. || 837 || 838. Therefore wealth approached you, the king of heaven, of good resolve; the fair-winged [bird], unwavering, bore [you]. || 838 || 839. Then, being impelled, he acquired the greater power of <s>Indra</s>, the greatness — the conqueror, the all-seeing. || 839 || 840. For the sight of heaven for all, the common [light], traversing the atmosphere — he bears the protector of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), the hero. || 840 ||

body.text:
4 2 2 04 01a iṣe pavasva dhārayā mṛjyamāno manīṣibhiḥ .
  4 2 2 04 01c indo rucābhi gā ihi .. 841
  4 2 2 04 02a punāno varivaskṛdhyūrjaṃ janāya girvaṇaḥ .
  4 2 2 04 02c hare sṛjāna āśiram .. 842
  4 2 2 04 03a punāno devavītaya indrasya yāhi niṣkṛtam .
  4 2 2 04 03c dyutāno vājibhirhitaḥ .. 843
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.04.01: Flow forth with a stream for nourishment, O [<s>Soma</s>], being polished by the wise ones! O drop (<s>Indu</s>), go toward the cows with your radiance! (841)
4.2.2.04.02: Being purified, O creator of wide space, [bring] vigor for the people, O lover of song! O tawny one, release the milk-mixed [stream]! (842)
4.2.2.04.03: Being purified for the inviting of the gods, go to <s>Indra</s>'s appointed [place]! Shining forth, impelled by the swift ones! (843)

body.text:
4 2 2 05 01a agnināgniḥ samidhyate kavirgṛhapatiryuvā .
  4 2 2 05 01c havyavāḍjuhvāsyaḥ .. 844
  4 2 2 05 02a yastvāmagne haviṣpatirdūtaṃ deva saparyati .
  4 2 2 05 02c tasya sma prāvitā bhava .. 845
  4 2 2 05 03a yo agniṃ devavītaye haviṣmāṃ āvivāsati .
  4 2 2 05 03c tasmai pāvaka mṛḍaya .. 846
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.05.01: <s>Agni</s> is kindled by <s>Agni</s> — the sage, the young lord of the house, the oblation-bearer, the flame-tongued one. (844)
4.2.2.05.02: Whoever, O god <s>Agni</s>, as master of oblations, honors you as messenger — be his helper! (845)
4.2.2.05.03: Whoever seeks to worship <s>Agni</s> for the inviting of the gods, bringing oblations — be gracious to him, O purifying one! (846)

body.text:
4 2 2 06 01a mitraṃ huve pūtadakṣaṃ varuṇaṃ ca riśādasam .
  4 2 2 06 01c dhiyaṃ ghṛtācīṃ sādhantā .. 847
  4 2 2 06 02a ṛtena mitrāvaruṇāvṛtāvṛdhāvṛtaspṛśā .
  4 2 2 06 02c kratuṃ bṛhantamāśāthe .. 848
  4 2 2 06 03a kavī no mitrāvaruṇā tuvijātā urukṣayā .
  4 2 2 06 03c dakṣaṃ dadhāte apasam .. 849
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.06.01: I invoke <s>Mitra</s> of pure skill, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, the consumer of [our] foes — [they who are] fulfilling the ghee-rich devotion. (847)
4.2.2.06.02: By cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>), O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, you two who increase <s>ṛta</s>, who touch <s>ṛta</s> — you attain great purpose. (848)
4.2.2.06.03: O sages, <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, of mighty birth, of wide domain — you two establish active skill. (849)

body.text:
4 2 2 07 01a indreṇa saṃ hi dṛkṣase saṃjagmāno abibhyuṣā .
  4 2 2 07 01c mandū samānavarccasā .. 850
  4 2 2 07 02a ādaha svadhāmanu punargarbhatvamerire .
  4 2 2 07 02c dadhānā nāma yajñiyam .. 851
  4 2 2 07 03a vīḍu cidārujatnubhirguhā cidindra vahnibhiḥ .
  4 2 2 07 03c avinda usriyā anu .. 852
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.07.01: With <s>Indra</s> you shall behold [the truth], having come together with the fearless one — the two delighting ones, of equal splendor. (850)
4.2.2.07.02: Then, following their own nature, they assumed again the state of embryo — bearing the name worthy of sacrifice. (851)
4.2.2.07.03: Even from the firm [stronghold], O <s>Indra</s>, with your crushing [allies], even from the hidden [place], with your flame-bearers — you found the dawning cows. (852)

body.text:
4 2 2 08 01a tā huve yayoridaṃ papne viśvaṃ purā kṛtam .
  4 2 2 08 01c indrāgnī na mardhataḥ .. 853
  4 2 2 08 02a ugrā vighaninā mṛdha indrāgnī havāmahe .
  4 2 2 08 02c tā no mṛḍāta īdṛśe .. 854
  4 2 2 08 03a hatho vṛtrāṇyāryā hatho dāsāni satpatī .
  4 2 2 08 03c hatho viśvā apa dviṣaḥ .. 855
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.08.01: I invoke those two, by whom all this was formerly protected and created — may <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> not neglect us! (853)
4.2.2.08.02: We call upon <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, the fierce ones, the destroyers of hostility. May they two be gracious to us in such [a situation]! (854)
4.2.2.08.03: Slay the <s>Ārya</s> <s>Vṛtras</s>! Slay the <s>Dāsa</s> [foes], O lords of the real! Slay all hostilities! (855)

body.text:
4 2 2 09 01a abhi somāsa āyavaḥ pavante madyaṃ madam .
  4 2 2 09 01c samudrasyādhi viṣṭape manīṣiṇo matsarāso madacyutaḥ .. 856
  4 2 2 09 02a taratsamudraṃ pavamāna ūrmiṇā rājā deva ṛtaṃ bṛhat .
  4 2 2 09 02c arṣā mitrasya varuṇasya dharmaṇā pra hinvāna ṛtaṃ bṛhat .. 857
  4 2 2 09 03a nṛbhiryemāṇo haryato vicakṣaṇo rājā devaḥ samudryaḥ .. 858
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.09.01: The <s>Soma</s> juices, [belonging to the] <s>Āyus</s> [clan], flow forth, the intoxicating intoxication — at the summit of the ocean, the wise ones, exhilarating, shedding intoxication. (856)
4.2.2.09.02: Cross the ocean with a wave, O <s>Pavamāna</s>! The divine king — great cosmic order. Flow by the law of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, being impelled forward — great cosmic order! (857)
4.2.2.09.03: Being directed by men, the tawny one, far-seeing — the divine king, belonging to the ocean. (858)

body.text:
4 2 2 10 01a tisro vāca īrayati pra vahnirṛtasya dhītiṃ brahmaṇo manīṣām .
  4 2 2 10 01c gāvo yanti gopatiṃ pṛcchamānāḥ somaṃ yanti matayo vāvaśānāḥ .. 859
  4 2 2 10 02a somaṃ gāvo dhenavo vāvaśānāḥ somaṃ viprā matibhiḥ pṛcchamānāḥ .
  4 2 2 10 02c somaḥ suta ṛcyate pūyamānaḥ some arkāstriṣṭubhaḥ saṃ navante .. 860
  4 2 2 10 03a evā naḥ soma pariṣicyamāna ā pavasva pūyamānaḥ svasti .
  4 2 2 10 03c indramā viśa bṛhatā madena vardhayā vācaṃ janayā purandhim .. 861
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.10.01: The swift one sends forth three voices — the devotion of <s>ṛta</s>, the insight of the sacred word (<s>brahman</s>). The cows go, asking for the lord of cattle; the devotions go to <s>Soma</s>, lowing. (859)
4.2.2.10.02: To <s>Soma</s>, the cows, the milch cows [go], lowing; to <s>Soma</s>, the inspired ones [go], asking with devotions. <s>Soma</s>, pressed, is celebrated, being purified; in <s>Soma</s>, the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> hymns come together. (860)
4.2.2.10.03: Thus, O <s>Soma</s>, being poured around, flow forth for our welfare, being purified! Enter <s>Indra</s> with great intoxication! Increase [our] speech! Generate wisdom! (861)

body.text:
4 2 2 11 01a yaddyāva indra te śataṃśataṃ bhūmīruta syuḥ .
  4 2 2 11 01c na tvā vajrintsahasraṃ suryā anu na jātamaṣṭa rodasī .. 862
  4 2 2 11 02a ā paprātha mahinā vṛṣṇyā vṛṣanviśvā śaviṣṭha śavasā .
  4 2 2 11 02c asmāṃ ava maghavangomati vraje vajriñcitrābhirūtibhiḥ .. 863
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.11.01: Even if there were a hundred heavens, O <s>Indra</s>, and a hundred earths as well — even a thousand suns, O <s>vajra</s>-wielder, could not [match] you — neither the born [world] nor the two worlds could contain [you]. (862)
4.2.2.11.02: You have filled [all] with your greatness, with your bull-like [power], O bull — all [things], O most mighty, with [your] might. Help us, O bountiful one, in the cattle-rich enclosure, O <s>vajra</s>-wielder, with your manifold aids! (863)

body.text:
4 2 2 12 01a vayaṃ gha tvā sutāvanta āpo na vṛktabarhiṣaḥ .
  4 2 2 12 01c pavitrasya prasravaṇeṣu vṛtrahanpari stotāra āsate .. 864
  4 2 2 12 02a svaranti tvā sute naro vaso nireka ukthinaḥ .
  4 2 2 12 02c kadā sutaṃ tṛṣāṇa oka ā gama indra svabdīva vaṃsagaḥ .. 865
  4 2 2 12 03a kaṇvebhirdhṛṣṇavā dhṛṣadvājaṃ darṣi sahasriṇam .
  4 2 2 12 03c piśaṅgarūpaṃ maghavanvicarṣaṇe makṣū gomantamīmahe .. 866
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.12.01: We who have pressed [<s>Soma</s>], having spread the sacred grass — like waters [flowing] — at the streams of the filter, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the praisers sit around. (864)
4.2.2.12.02: The men sing to you at the pressed [<s>Soma</s>], O beneficent one, reciters of <s>ukthas</s> (praises), at the pouring forth. When will you come, thirsting, to [our] home and to the pressed [<s>Soma</s>], O <s>Indra</s>, like a reed-warbler to [its nest]? (865)
4.2.2.12.03: Among the <s>Kaṇvas</s>, boldly and daringly, grant a thousandfold prize! Tawny in form, O bountiful one, far-seeing — we seek quickly [one] rich in cattle. (866)

body.text:
4 2 2 13 01a taraṇiritsiṣāsati vājaṃ purandhyā yujā .
  4 2 2 13 01c ā va indraṃ puruhūtaṃ name girā nemiṃ taṣṭeva sudruvam .. 867
  4 2 2 13 02a na duṣṭutirdraviṇodeṣu śasyate na sredhantaṃ rayirnaśat .
  4 2 2 13 02c suśaktirinmaghavaṃ tubhyaṃ māvate deṣṇaṃ yatpārye divi .. 868
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.13.01: The swift one strives to win the prize, with wisdom as his ally. I bow with my song to your <s>Indra</s>, the much-invoked — like a craftsman [bending] a rim for easy rolling. (867)
4.2.2.13.02: The poorly praised [hymn] is not recited among the wealth-giving ones; nor does prosperity reach the negligent. Effective indeed, O bountiful one, is the gift that is available to you — the gift given on the supreme day [of sacrifice]. (868)

body.text:
4 2 2 14 01a tisro vāca udīrate gāvo mimanti dhenavaḥ .
  4 2 2 14 01c harireti kanikradat .. 869
  4 2 2 14 02a abhi brahmīranūṣata yahvīrṛtasya mātaraḥ .
  4 2 2 14 02c marjayantīrdivaḥ śiśum .. 870
  4 2 2 14 03a rāyaḥ samudrāṃścaturo 'smabhyaṃ soma viśvataḥ .
  4 2 2 14 03c ā pavasva sahasriṇaḥ .. 871
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.14.01: Three voices rise up; the cows, the milch cows, low. The tawny one moves on, resounding. (869)
4.2.2.14.02: The sacred words (<s>brahma</s>) have sounded upon the mighty mothers of cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>) — cleansing the child of heaven. (870)
4.2.2.14.03: The four oceans of wealth, O <s>Soma</s>, from all sides — flow forth for us, thousandfold! (871)

body.text:
4 2 2 15 01a sutāso madhumattamāḥ somā indrāya mandinaḥ .
  4 2 2 15 01c pavitravanto akṣaraṃ devāngacchantu vo madāḥ .. 872
  4 2 2 15 02a indurindrāya pavata iti devāso abruvan .
  4 2 2 15 02c vācaspatirmakhasyate viśvasyeśāna ojasāḥ .. 873
  4 2 2 15 03a sahasradhāraḥ pavate samudro vācamīṅkhayaḥ .
  4 2 2 15 03c somaspatī rayīṇāṃ sakhendrasya divedive .. 874
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.15.01: The most honey-sweet pressed <s>Soma</s> juices, gladdening for <s>Indra</s> — flowing through the filter, imperishable — may your intoxications reach the gods! (872)
4.2.2.15.02: 'The drop is purified for <s>Indra</s>' — thus the gods said. The lord of speech is glorified — the lord of all, by his might. (873)
4.2.2.15.03: The thousand-streamed one flows forth, the ocean, stirring speech. The lord of <s>Soma</s>, of riches, the friend of <s>Indra</s>, day after day. (874)

body.text:
4 2 2 16 01a pavitraṃ te vitataṃ brahmaṇaspate prabhurgātrāṇi paryeṣi viśvataḥ .
  4 2 2 16 01c ataptatanūrna tadāmo aśnute śṛtāsa idvahantaḥ saṃ tadāśata .. 875
  4 2 2 16 02a tapoṣpavitraṃ vitataṃ divaspade 'rcanto asya tantavo vyasthiran .
  4 2 2 16 02c avantyasya pavītāramāśavo divaḥ pṛṣṭhamadhi rohanti tejasā .. 876
  4 2 2 16 03a arūrucaduṣasaḥ pṛśniragriya ukṣā mimeti bhuvaneṣu vājayuḥ .
  4 2 2 16 03c māyāvino mamire asya māyayā nṛcakṣasaḥ pitaro garbhamā dadhuḥ .. 877
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.16.01: Your filter is spread wide, O <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s>! The lord passes around all limbs on every side. One whose body is unheated does not attain that; only those who are cooked [by discipline], bearing [the fire], have shared in that. (875)
4.2.2.16.02: The filter of austerity is spread in the seat of heaven. Those who praise — its threads have stood firm. The swift ones attend upon its purifier; they ascend the back of heaven with [their] splendor. (876)
4.2.2.16.03: The dappled dawns have shone forth first; the bull bellows in the worlds, seeking the prize. The crafty ones fashioned his craft; the fathers, beholding men, placed [him] in the womb. (877)

body.text:
4 2 2 17 01a pra maṃhiṣṭhāya gāyata ṛtāvne bṛhate śukraśociṣe .
  4 2 2 17 01c upastutāso agnaye .. 878
  4 2 2 17 02a ā vaṃsate maghavā vīravadyaśaḥ samiddho dyumnyāhutaḥ .
  4 2 2 17 02c kuvinno asya sumatirbhavīyasyacchā vājebhirāgamat .. 879
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.17.01: Sing to the most bountiful one, to the upholder of <s>ṛta</s>, the great one, of bright flame! — praised, to <s>Agni</s>. (878)
4.2.2.17.02: The bountiful one attains fame rich in heroes, when kindled, brilliant, invoked with oblations. May his goodwill be ours! May he come to us with prizes! (879)

body.text:
4 2 2 18 01a taṃ te madaṃ gṛṇīmasi vṛṣaṇaṃ pṛkṣu sāsahim .
  4 2 2 18 01c u lokakṛtnumadrivo hariśriyam .. 880
  4 2 2 18 02a yena jyotīṃṣyāyave manave ca viveditha .
  4 2 2 18 02c mandāno asya barhiṣo vi rājasi .. 881
  4 2 2 18 03a tadadyā citta ukthino 'nu ṣṭuvanti pūrvathā .
  4 2 2 18 03c vṛṣapatnīrapo jayā divedive .. 882
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.18.01: We celebrate that intoxication of yours, O bull, conquering in battles — the world-maker, O stone-wielder, adorned with bay [horses]. (880)
4.2.2.18.02: By which you found the lights for <s>Āyu</s> and for <s>Manu</s> — delighting in this sacred grass, you shine forth. (881)
4.2.2.18.03: That [deed], today, the praisers celebrate in the manner of the ancients — win the waters whose lord is the bull, day after day! (882)

body.text:
4 2 2 19 01a śrudhī havaṃ tiraścyā indra yastvā saparyati .
  4 2 2 19 01c suvīryasya gomato rāyaspūrdhi mahāṃ asi .. 883
  4 2 2 19 02a yasta indra navīyasīṃ giraṃ mandrāmajījanat .
  4 2 2 19 02c cikitvinmanasaṃ dhiyaṃ pratnāmṛtasya pipyuṣīm .. 884
  4 2 2 19 03a tamu ṣṭavāma yaṃ gira indramukthāni vāvṛdhuḥ .
  4 2 2 19 03c purūṇyasya nauṃsyā siṣāsanto vanāmahe .. 885
body.translated_text:
4.2.2.19.01: Hear the call from afar, O <s>Indra</s>, [from him] who honors you! Fill [us] with wealth of good heroes and cattle! You are great! (883)
4.2.2.19.02: He who has produced for you, O <s>Indra</s>, a new, delightful song — a thought-rich devotion, the ancient one, swelling with <s>ṛta</s>, O wise one! (884)
4.2.2.19.03: Let us praise him whom hymns have magnified — <s>Indra</s>! Striving, may we win his many manly [deeds]! (885)

body.text:
tṛtīya prapāṭhakaḥ . prathamo 'rdhaḥ
  4 3 1 01 01a pra ta āśvinīḥ pavamāna dhenavo divyā asṛgranpayasā dharīmaṇi .
  4 3 1 01 01c prāntarikṣātsthāvirīste asṛkṣata ye tvā mṛjantyṛṣiṣāṇa vedhasaḥ .. 886
  4 3 1 01 02a ubhayataḥ pavamānasya raśmayo dhruvasya sataḥ pari yanti ketavaḥ .
  4 3 1 01 02c yadī pavitre adhi mṛjyate hariḥ sattā ni yonau kalaśeṣu sīdati .. 887
  4 3 1 01 03a viśvā dhāmāni viśvacakṣa ṛbhvasaḥ prabhoṣṭe sataḥ pari yanti ketavaḥ .
  4 3 1 01 03c vyānaśī pavase soma dharmaṇā patirviśvasya bhuvanasya rājasi .. 888
body.translated_text:
Third <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, First Half.
4.3.1.01.01: Forth, O <s>Pavamāna</s>, your <s>Aśvinī</s> milch cows have streamed forth, the heavenly ones, with their milk, upon the seat. From the atmosphere, the mighty ones have sent forth [their streams] — those who cleanse you, O <s>ṛṣi</s>-seeking sages! (886)
4.3.1.01.02: On both sides, the rays of <s>Pavamāna</s> — the beams of the stable one — go around. When the tawny one is polished upon the filter, sitting established, he settles in the vessels. (887)
4.3.1.01.03: All abodes, O all-seeing, O powerful one — your beams, of the stable one, go around. You purify, O <s>Soma</s>, by your law, pervading; you reign as lord of the whole universe. (888)

body.text:
4 3 1 02 01a pavamāno ajījanaddivaścitraṃ na tanyatum .
  4 3 1 02 01c jyotirvaiśvānaraṃ bṛhat .. 889
  4 3 1 02 02a pavamāna rasastava mado rājannaducchunaḥ .
  4 3 1 02 02c vi vāramavyamarṣati .. 890
  4 3 1 02 03a pavamānasya te raso dakṣo vi rājati dyumān .
  4 3 1 02 03c jyotirviśvaṃ svardṛśe .. 891
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.2.889: <s>Pavamāna</s> (purifying Soma) has generated from heaven a wondrous [sound] like thunder — the great light of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>.
4.3.1.2.890: O <s>Pavamāna</s>, your juice, your intoxication, O king, free from evil — it flows through the woolen filter.
4.3.1.2.891: O <s>Pavamāna</s>, your brilliant juice and skill shine forth — a light for the vision of all, for seeing the sun.

body.text:
4 3 1 03 01a pra yadgāvo na bhūrṇayastveṣā ayāso akramuḥ .
  4 3 1 03 01c ghnantaḥ kṛṣṇāmapa tvacam .. 892
  4 3 1 03 02a suvitasya manāmahe 'ti setuṃ durāyyam .
  4 3 1 03 02c sāhyāma dasyumavratam .. 893
  4 3 1 03 03a śṛṇve vṛṣṭeriva svanaḥ pavamānasya śuṣmiṇaḥ .
  4 3 1 03 03c caranti vidyuto divi .. 894
  4 3 1 03 04a ā pavasva mahīmiṣaṃ gomadindo hiraṇyavat .
  4 3 1 03 04c aśvavatsoma vīravat .. 895
  4 3 1 03 05a pavasva viśvacarṣaṇa ā mahī rodasī pṛṇa .
  4 3 1 03 05c uṣāḥ sūryo na raśmibhiḥ .. 896
  4 3 1 03 06a pari naḥ śarmayantyā dhārayā soma viśvataḥ .
  4 3 1 03 06c sarā raseva viṣṭapam .. 897
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.3.892: When, like surging cattle, the fierce, rushing [streams] strode forth, stripping away the black skin.
4.3.1.3.893: We think of well-being — crossing the bridge difficult to traverse. May we overcome the lawless <s>Dasyu</s>.
4.3.1.3.894: The sound of the mighty <s>Pavamāna</s> is heard, like [the sound] of rain. Lightnings move across the sky.
4.3.1.3.895: O <s>Indu</s> (Soma drop), purify yourself toward great nourishment, [bringing] cattle and gold, horses and heroes.
4.3.1.3.896: Purify yourself, O all-seeing one; fill the great heaven and earth — like <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) [or] the sun with [its] rays.
4.3.1.3.897: O <s>Soma</s>, with your sheltering stream surround us on every side — like a river [filling] a lake.

body.text:
4 3 1 04 01a āśurarṣa bṛhanmate pari priyeṇa dhāmnā .
  4 3 1 04 01c yatra devā iti bruvan .. 898
  4 3 1 04 02a pariṣkṛṇvannaniṣkṛtaṃ janāya yātayanniṣaḥ .
  4 3 1 04 02c vṛṣṭiṃ divaḥ pari srava .. 899
  4 3 1 04 03a ayaṃ sa yo divaspari raghuyāmā pavitra ā .
  4 3 1 04 03c sindhorūrmā vyakṣarat .. 900
  4 3 1 04 04a suta eti pavitra ā tviṣiṃ dadhāna ojasā .
  4 3 1 04 04c vicakṣāṇo virocayan .. 901
  4 3 1 04 05a āvivāsanparāvato atho arvāvataḥ sutaḥ .
  4 3 1 04 05c indrāya sicyate madhu .. 902
  4 3 1 04 00a samīcīnā anūṣata hariṃ hinvantyadribhiḥ .
  4 3 1 04 00c indumindrāya pītaye .. 903
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.4.898: O swift one, flow with great song, with your dear brightness — to where the gods say 'thus!'
4.3.1.4.899: Adorning the unadorned, granting nourishment to the people — flow around with the rain from heaven.
4.3.1.4.900: This is he who, from beyond heaven, swift-moving, [enters] the filter — a wave of the river has streamed forth.
4.3.1.4.901: Pressed, he enters the filter, bearing splendor with [his] might — the all-seeing one, illuminating.
4.3.1.4.902: Seeking [friends] from afar and from near, the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] — honey is poured for <s>Indra</s>.
4.3.1.4.903: Facing together, they urge the golden one with the pressing-stones — <s>Indu</s>, for <s>Indra</s>'s drinking.

body.text:
4 3 1 05 01a hinvanti sūramusrayaḥ svasāro jāmayaspatim .
  4 3 1 05 01c mahāminduṃ mahīyuvaḥ .. 904
  4 3 1 05 02a pavamāna rucārucā devo devebhyaḥ sutaḥ .
  4 3 1 05 02c viśvā vasūnyā viśa .. 905
  4 3 1 05 03a ā pavamāna suṣṭutiṃ vṛṣṭiṃ devebhyo duvaḥ .
  4 3 1 05 03c iṣe pavasva saṃyatam .. 906
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.5.904: The dawns, the sisters, impel the sun, [who is also] the husband of [their] kin — the great <s>Indu</s>, the great magnifiers.
4.3.1.5.905: O <s>Pavamāna</s>, pressed for the gods with brightness upon brightness — enter all the goods.
4.3.1.5.906: O <s>Pavamāna</s>, [bring] good praise, rain, worship for the gods. Purify yourself for nourishment, held together.

body.text:
4 3 1 06 01a janasya gopā ajaniṣṭa jāgṛviragniḥ sudakṣaḥ suvitāya navyase .
  4 3 1 06 01c ghṛtapratīko bṛhatā divispṛṣā dyumadvi bhāti bharatebhyaḥ śuciḥ .. 907
  4 3 1 06 02a tvāmagne aṅgiraso guhā hitamanvavindañchiśriyāṇaṃ vanevane .
  4 3 1 06 02c sa jāyase mathyamānaḥ saho mahatvāmāhuḥ sahasasputramaṅgiraḥ .. 908
  4 3 1 06 03a yajñasya ketuṃ prathamaṃ purohitamagniṃ narastriṣadhasthe samindhate .
  4 3 1 06 03c indreṇa devaiḥ sarathaṃ sa barhiṣi sīdanni hotā yajathāya sukratuḥ .. 909
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.6.907: The guardian of the people was born, ever watchful — <s>Agni</s> of good skill, for a newer well-being. Ghee-faced, touching heaven with [his] greatness, he shines brightly and purely for the <s>Bharatas</s>.
4.3.1.6.908: You, O <s>Agni</s>, the <s>Aṅgirases</s> found hidden, shining in forest after forest. You are born when churned, a great force — they call you the son of strength, O <s>Aṅgiras</s>.
4.3.1.6.909: Men kindle <s>Agni</s>, the banner of the sacrifice, the foremost, the placed-before priest, in the three abodes. Sharing the chariot with <s>Indra</s> and the gods, he sits upon the sacred grass — the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the one of good wisdom, for the sacrifice.

body.text:
4 3 1 07 01a ayaṃ vāṃ mitrāvaruṇā sutaḥ soma ṛtāvṛdhā .
  4 3 1 07 01c mamediha śrutaṃ havam .. 910
  4 3 1 07 02a rājānāvanabhidruhā dhruve sadasyuttame .
  4 3 1 07 02c sahasrasthūṇa āśāte .. 911
  4 3 1 07 03a tā samrājā ghṛtāsutī ādityā dānunaspatī .
  4 3 1 07 03c sacete anavahvaram .. 912
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.7.910: This <s>Soma</s> is pressed for you two, O <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, O increasers of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order). Hear my invocation here!
4.3.1.7.911: The two kings, without hostility, in the firm and highest seat — they share in the thousand-pillared [abode].
4.3.1.7.912: Those two supreme rulers, with ghee-offerings, <s>Ādityas</s>, lords of generosity — they accompany without negligence.

body.text:
4 3 1 08 01a indro dadhīco asthabhirvṛtrāṇyapratiṣkutaḥ .
  4 3 1 08 01c jaghāna navatīrnava .. 913
  4 3 1 08 02a icchannaśvasya yacchiraḥ parvateṣvapaśritam .
  4 3 1 08 02c tadvidaccharyaṇāvati .. 914
  4 3 1 08 03a atrāha goramanvata nāma tvaṣṭurapīcyam .
  4 3 1 08 03c itthā candramaso gṛhe .. 915
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.8.913: <s>Indra</s>, with the bones of <s>Dadhīci</s>, irresistible, slew ninety-nine [forts of] <s>Vṛtra</s>.
4.3.1.8.914: Seeking the head of the horse, hidden in the mountains — he found it at <s>Śaryaṇāvat</s> [lake].
4.3.1.8.915: There they discovered the hidden name of the cow — [the name] of <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>. Thus, in the house of the moon.

body.text:
4 3 1 09 01a iyaṃ vāmasya manmana indrāgnī pūrvyastutiḥ .
  4 3 1 09 01c abhrādvṛṣṭirivājani .. 916
  4 3 1 09 02a śṛṇutaṃ jariturhavamindrāgnī vanataṃ giraḥ .
  4 3 1 09 02c īśānā pipyataṃ dhiyaḥ .. 917
  4 3 1 09 03a mā pāpatvāya no narendrāgnī mābhiśastaye .
  4 3 1 09 03c mā no rīradhataṃ nide .. 918
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.9.916: This is the first praise of your inspiration, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> — born like rain from the cloud.
4.3.1.9.917: Hear the invocation of the singer, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>; accept [our] songs! Being lords, fill the thoughts [with blessings]!
4.3.1.9.918: Lead us not to evil, O men [among gods], O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, nor to reproach. Do not deliver us to the scorner.

body.text:
4 3 1 10 01a pavasva dakṣasādhano devebhyaḥ pītaye hare .
  4 3 1 10 01c marudbhyo vāyave madaḥ .. 919
  4 3 1 10 02a saṃ devaiḥ śobhate vṛṣā kaviryonāvadhi priyaḥ .
  4 3 1 10 02c pavamāno adābhyaḥ .. 920
  4 3 1 10 03a pavamāna dhiyā hito3 'bhi yoniṃ kanikradat .
  4 3 1 10 03c dharmaṇā vāyumāruhaḥ .. 921
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.10.919: O golden one, purify yourself for the gods to drink, O skill-accomplishing one — an intoxication for the <s>Maruts</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>.
4.3.1.10.920: The bull, the poet, shines with the gods upon his dear birthplace — <s>Pavamāna</s>, the undeceivable.
4.3.1.10.921: <s>Pavamāna</s>, placed by thought, crying aloud toward [his] birthplace — by [his] law, you have ascended to <s>Vāyu</s> (wind/breath).

body.text:
4 3 1 11 01a tavāhaṃ soma rāraṇa sakhya indo divedive .
  4 3 1 11 01c purūṇi babhro ni caranti māmava paridhīṃ rati tāṃihi .. 922
  4 3 1 11 02a tavāhaṃ naktamuta soma te divā duhāno babhra ūdhani .
  4 3 1 11 02c ghṛṇā tapantamati sūryaṃ paraḥ śakunā iva paptima .. 923
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.11.922: O <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indu</s>, I delight in your friendship day after day. Many [blessings], O tawny one, flow down to me — pass beyond the enclosure, cross over it!
4.3.1.11.923: O <s>Soma</s>, by night and by day I milk you, O tawny one, at [your] udder. Beyond the sun, scorching with heat — like birds we have flown.

body.text:
4 3 1 12 01a punāno akramīdabhi viśvā mṛdho vicarṣaṇiḥ .
  4 3 1 12 01c śumbhanti vipraṃ dhītibhiḥ .. 924
  4 3 1 12 02a ā yonimaruṇo ruhadgamadindraṃ vṛṣā sutam .
  4 3 1 12 02c dhruve sadasi sīdatu .. 925
  4 3 1 12 03a nū no rayiṃ mahāmindo 'smabhyaṃ soma viśvataḥ .
  4 3 1 12 03c ā pavasva sahasriṇam .. 926
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.12.924: Purifying himself, the all-seeing one has stridden over all hostilities. The wise ones adorn the inspired one with their thoughts.
4.3.1.12.925: The reddish-brown bull has ascended to [his] birthplace; the pressed [<s>Soma</s>] has gone to <s>Indra</s>. Let him sit in the firm seat.
4.3.1.12.926: Now, O great <s>Indu</s>, O <s>Soma</s>, purify yourself with thousandfold [wealth] — [bringing] us riches from every side.

body.text:
4 3 1 13 01a pibā somamindra madantu tvā yaṃ te suṣāva haryaśvādriḥ .
  4 3 1 13 01c soturbāhubhyāṃ suyato nārvā .. 927
  4 3 1 13 02a yaste mado yujyaścārurasti yena vṛtrāṇi haryaśva haṃsi .
  4 3 1 13 02c sa tvāmindra prabhūvaso mamattu .. 928
  4 3 1 13 03a bodhā su me maghavanvācamemāṃ yāṃ te vasiṣṭho arcati praśastim .
  4 3 1 13 03c imā brahma sadhamāde juṣasva .. 929
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.13.927: Drink the <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Indra</s>; let [the juices] intoxicate you — which the pressing-stone has pressed for you, O bay-horsed one, well-guided from the presser's arms like a steed.
4.3.1.13.928: That intoxication of yours which is yoked [to you] and dear, by which you slay the <s>Vṛtras</s>, O bay-horsed one — may it gladden you, O <s>Indra</s>, O lord of great wealth!
4.3.1.13.929: Heed well, O <s>Maghavan</s>, this speech of mine which <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> sings to you as praise. Enjoy these sacred words at the common feast.

body.text:
4 3 1 14 01a viśvāḥ pṛtanā abhibhūtaraṃ naraḥ sajūstatakṣurindraṃ jajanuśca rājase .
  4 3 1 14 01c kratve vare sthemanyāmurīmutogramojiṣṭhaṃ tarasaṃ tarasvinam .. 930
  4 3 1 14 02a nemiṃ namanti cakṣasā meṣaṃ viprā abhisvare .
  4 3 1 14 02c sudītayo vo adruho 'pi karṇe tarasvinaḥ samṛkvabhiḥ .. 931
  4 3 1 14 03a samu rebhaso asvarannindraṃ somasya pītaye .
  4 3 1 14 03c svaḥpatiryadī vṛdhe dhṛtavrato hyojasā samūtibhiḥ .. 932
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.14.930: The men fashioned and generated <s>Indra</s>, the most all-conquering, to rule over all armies together — for wisdom, for choice, for firmness, and for expansion — the fierce one, the mightiest, the speedy one of speed.
4.3.1.14.931: The wise ones bend the rim [of the pressing-stone] with [their] gaze, [bend] the ram in the invitation. Of good kindling, you guileless ones, [attend] at the ear of the speedy one with [your] hymns.
4.3.1.14.932: Together the singers have sung to <s>Indra</s> for the drinking of <s>Soma</s>. The lord of heaven — if for [our] increase — of firm vow, by his might, with aids.

body.text:
4 3 1 15 01a yo rājā carṣaṇīnāṃ yātā rathebhiradhriguḥ .
  4 3 1 15 01c viśvāsāṃ tarutā pṛtanānāṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ yo vṛtrahā gṛṇe .. 933
  4 3 1 15 02a indraṃ taṃ śumbhya puruhanmannavase yasya dvitā vidharttari .
  4 3 1 15 02c hastena vajraḥ prati dhāyi darśato mahāṃ devo na sūryaḥ .. 934
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.15.933: He who is king of the peoples, who travels with chariots, the swift one — the overcomer of all armies. I sing of the greatest one, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>.
4.3.1.15.934: Adorn that <s>Indra</s> for [our] protection, O man of many slaughters, in whose two hands the <s>vajra</s> is held firm — a great god visible like the sun.

body.text:
4 3 1 16 01a pari priyā divaḥ kavirvayāṃsi naptyorhitaḥ .
  4 3 1 16 01c svānairyāti kavikratuḥ .. 935
  4 3 1 16 02a sa sūnurmātarā śucirjāto jāte arocayat .
  4 3 1 16 02c mahānmahī ṛtāvṛdhā .. 936
  4 3 1 16 03a prapra kṣayāya panyase janāya juṣṭo adruhaḥ .
  4 3 1 16 03c vītyarṣa paniṣṭaye .. 937
  4 3 1 17 01a tvaṃ hyā3ṃṅga daivyā pavamāna janimāni dyumattamaḥ .
  4 3 1 17 01c amṛtatvāya ghoṣayan .. 938
  4 3 1 17 02a yenā navagvo dadhyaṅṅaporṇute yena viprāsa āpire .
  4 3 1 17 02c devānāṃ sumne amṛtasya cāruṇo yena śravāṃsyāśata .. 939
body.translated_text:
4.3.1.16.935: Around [heaven], the dear poet, placed [by] the waters, moves — with his sounds, the one of poetic wisdom.
4.3.1.16.936: He, the bright son, born, illumined both mothers — the great one, the great, increasing <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order).
4.3.1.16.937: Flow forth freely for the people, to their dwelling, to their admiration — guileless, for enjoyment; flow for [our] gain.
4.3.1.17.938: For you indeed, O <s>Pavamāna</s>, [encompass] the divine births, O most luminous one, proclaiming immortality.
4.3.1.17.939: By which the <s>Navagvas</s> and <s>Dadhyañc</s> uncovered [the hidden cattle]; by which the inspired sages attained [the light] — in the favor of the gods, the dear one of the immortal — by which they won [their] glories.

body.text:
4 3 1 18 01a somaḥ punāna ūrmiṇāvyaṃ vāraṃ vi dhāvati .
  4 3 1 18 01c agre vācaḥ pavamānaḥ kanikradat .. 940
  4 3 1 18 02a dhībhirmṛjanti vājinaṃ vane krīḍantamatyavim .
  4 3 1 18 02c abhi tripṛṣṭhaṃ matayaḥ samasvaran .. 941
  4 3 1 18 03a asarji kalaśāṃ abhi mīḍhvāntsaptirna vājayuḥ .
  4 3 1 18 03c punāno vācaṃ janayannasiṣyadat .. 942
body.translated_text:
940: <s>Soma</s>, purifying himself, runs through the woolen filter with a wave — the Self-purifying one (<s>Pavamāna</s>), sounding forth before speech.
941: With prayers they cleanse the prize-winning one, playing in the forest [of wool], the swift one — the thoughts resounded toward the three-ridged one.
942: The bountiful one was released toward the vessels, like a steed seeking the prize — purifying, generating speech, he streamed forth.

body.text:
4 3 1 19 01a somaḥ pavate janitā matīnāṃ janitā divo janitā pṛthivyāḥ .
  4 3 1 19 01c janitāgnerjanitā sūryasya janitendrasya janitota viṣṇoḥ .. 943
  4 3 1 19 02a brahmā devānāṃ padavīḥ kavīnāṃ ṛṣirviprāṇāṃ mahiṣomṛgāṇām .
  4 3 1 19 02c śyeno gṛdhrāṇāṃ svadhitirvanānāṃ somaḥ pavitramatyeti rebhan .. 944
  4 3 1 19 03a prāvīvipadvāca ūrmiṃ na sindhurgira stomānpavamāno manīṣāḥ .
  4 3 1 19 03c antaḥ paśyanvṛjanemāvarāṇyā tiṣṭhati vṛṣabho goṣu jānan .. 945
body.translated_text:
943: <s>Soma</s> flows purified — the generator of thoughts, the generator of heaven, the generator of earth, the generator of <s>Agni</s>, the generator of <s>Sūrya</s>, the generator of <s>Indra</s>, and the generator of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
944: The priest (<s>Brahmā</s>) of the gods, the tracker of poets, the seer of the inspired, the buffalo of beasts, the eagle of vultures, the axe of forests — <s>Soma</s> passes through the filter, resounding.
945: He set trembling the wave of speech like a river — the Self-purifying one, the songs, the praises, the hymns. Looking within, seeing the lower realms through the enclosure, the bull stands among the cows, knowing.

body.text:
4 3 1 20 01a agniṃ vo vṛdhantamadhvarāṇāṃ purūtamam .
  4 3 1 20 01c acchā naptre sahasvate .. 946
  4 3 1 20 02a ayaṃ yathā na ābhuvattvaṣṭā rūpeva takṣyā .
  4 3 1 20 02c asya kratvā yaśasvataḥ .. 947
  4 3 1 20 03a ayaṃ viśvā abhi śriyo 'gnirdeveṣu patyate .
  4 3 1 20 03c ā vājairupa no gamat .. 948
body.translated_text:
946: [I praise] for you <s>Agni</s>, the increaser of sacrifices, the most widely beneficent — toward the powerful grandson.
947: May he be ours, like <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> [fashioning] form by craft — by the will of this glorious one.
948: This <s>Agni</s> rules over all glories among the gods — may he come to us with prizes.

body.text:
4 3 1 21 01a imamindra sutaṃ piba jyeṣṭhamamartyaṃ madam .
  4 3 1 21 01c śukrasya tvābhyakṣarandhārā ṛtasya sādane .. 949
  4 3 1 21 02a na kiṣṭvadrathītaro harī yadindra yacchase .
  4 3 1 21 02c na kiṣṭvānu majmanā na kiḥ svaśva ānaśe .. 950
  4 3 1 21 03a indrāya nūnamarcatokthāni ca bravītana .
  4 3 1 21 03c sutā amatsurindavo jyeṣṭhaṃ namasyatā sahaḥ .. 951
body.translated_text:
949: O <s>Indra</s>, drink this pressed juice, the supreme, immortal intoxication — the streams of the bright one have flowed toward you, in the seat of truth (<s>ṛta</s>).
950: No one is a better charioteer than you, when you yoke your two bay horses, O <s>Indra</s> — none equals you in might, none with his own horses has attained you.
951: Sing now for <s>Indra</s>, and recite the hymns — the pressed drops have intoxicated; worship the supreme power.

body.text:
4 3 1 22 01a indra juṣasva pra vahā yāhi śūra hariha .
  4 3 1 22 01c pibā sutasya matirna madhoścakānaścārurmadāya .. 952
  4 3 1 22 02a indra jaṭharaṃ navyaṃ na pṛṇasva madhordivo na .
  4 3 1 22 02c asya sutasya svā3rnopa tvā madāḥ suvāco asthuḥ .. 953
  4 3 1 22 03a indrasturāṣāṇmitro na jaghāna vṛtraṃ yatirna .
  4 3 1 22 03c bibheda valaṃ bhṛgurna sasāhe śatrūnmade somasya .. 954
body.translated_text:
952: O <s>Indra</s>, be pleased, convey [us] forth, go, O hero, with your bay horses here — drink of the pressed [<s>Soma</s>], delighting in the mead, the beautiful one, for intoxication.
953: O <s>Indra</s>, fill your belly anew, as from heavenly mead — the intoxications of this pressed [<s>Soma</s>], well-spoken, stand near you.
954: <s>Indra</s>, the swift conqueror, like <s>Mitra</s>, slew <s>Vṛtra</s>; like a sage, he split <s>Vala</s> (the cave); like <s>Bhṛgu</s>, he vanquished enemies in the intoxication of <s>Soma</s>.

body.text:
tṛtīya prapāṭhakaḥ . dvitīyo 'rdhaḥ
  4 3 2 01 01a govitpavasva vasuviddhiraṇyavidretodhā indo bhuvaneṣvarpitaḥ .
  4 3 2 01 01c tvaṃ suvīro asi soma viśvavittaṃ tvā nara upa girema āsate .. 955
  4 3 2 01 02a tvaṃ nṛcakṣā asi soma viśvataḥ pavamāna vṛṣabha tā vi dhāvasi .
  4 3 2 01 02c sa naḥ pavasva vasumaddhiraṇyavadvayaṃ syāma bhuvaneṣu jīvase .. 956
  4 3 2 01 03a īśāna imā bhuvanāni īyase yujāna indo haritaḥ suparṇyaḥ .
  4 3 2 01 03c tāste kṣarantu madhumadghṛtaṃ payastava vrate soma tiṣṭhantu kṛṣṭayaḥ .. 957
body.translated_text:
Third <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, Second Half.
955: Flow, O finder of cattle, finder of wealth, finder of gold, seed-bestower, O <s>Indu</s>, established among the worlds — you are rich in heroes, O <s>Soma</s>, all-knowing; men sit near and praise you.
956: You are the watcher of men, O <s>Soma</s>, on every side; O Self-purifying bull, you course through those [worlds] — flow for us with wealth, with gold; may we live among the worlds.
957: As lord, you pervade these worlds, yoking, O <s>Indu</s>, the fair-winged tawny ones — may they flow for you with honey, ghee, and milk; in your ordinance, O <s>Soma</s>, may the peoples abide.

body.text:
4 3 2 02 01a pavamānasya viśvavitpra te sargā asṛkṣata .
  4 3 2 02 01c sūryasyeva na raśmayaḥ .. 958
  4 3 2 02 02a ketuṃ kṛṇvaṃ divaspari viśvā rūpābhyarṣasi .
  4 3 2 02 02c samudraḥ soma pinvase .. 959
  4 3 2 02 03a jajñāno vācamiṣyasi pavamāna vidharmaṇi .
  4 3 2 02 03c krandaṃ devo na sūryaḥ .. 960
body.translated_text:
958: O all-knowing Self-purifying one, your streams have been released forth — like the rays of the sun.
959: Making a banner beyond heaven, you flow toward all forms — you, O <s>Soma</s>, swell into an ocean.
960: Being born, you send forth speech, O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-purifying one), in diverse ways — resounding like the god, the Sun.

body.text:
4 3 2 03 01a pra somāso adhanviṣuḥ pavamānāsa indavaḥ .
  4 3 2 03 01c śrīṇānā apsu vṛñjate .. 961
  4 3 2 03 02a abhi gāvo adhanviṣurāpo na pravatā yatīḥ .
  4 3 2 03 02c punānā indramāśata .. 962
  4 3 2 03 03a pra pavamāna dhanvasi somendrāya mādanaḥ .
  4 3 2 03 03c nṛbhiryato vi nīyase .. 963
  4 3 2 03 04a indo yadadribhiḥ sutaḥ pavitraṃ paridīyase .
  4 3 2 03 04c aramindrasya dhāmne .. 964
  4 3 2 03 05a tvaṃ soma nṛmādanaḥ pavasva carṣaṇīdhṛtiḥ .
  4 3 2 03 05c sasniryo anumādyaḥ .. 965
  4 3 2 03 06a pavasva vṛtrahantama ukthebhiranumādyaḥ .
  4 3 2 03 06c śuciḥ pāvako adbhutaḥ .. 966
  4 3 2 03 07a śuciḥ pāvaka ucyate somaḥ sutaḥ sa madhumān .
  4 3 2 03 07c devāvīraghaśaṃsahā .. 967
body.translated_text:
961: The self-purifying <s>Soma</s> drops have streamed forth — mixing in the waters, they turn.
962: The [<s>Soma</s>] drops have streamed forth like waters flowing downhill — purifying themselves, they have reached <s>Indra</s>.
963: You stream forth, O Self-purifying <s>Soma</s>, intoxicating, for <s>Indra</s> — directed by men, you are led forth.
964: O <s>Indu</s>, when pressed by stones, you flow around the filter — sufficient for <s>Indra</s>'s abode.
965: You, O <s>Soma</s>, intoxicator of men, flow — sustainer of peoples, the conquering one, who is to be exulted over.
966: Flow, O best slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, to be praised with hymns — pure, purifying, wondrous.
967: Pure, purifying — so is the pressed <s>Soma</s> called, the honeyed one — the divine hero, slayer of the evil-speaking [demons].

body.text:
4 3 2 04 01a pra kavirdevavītaye 'vyā vārebhiravyata .
  4 3 2 04 01c sāhvānviśvā abhi spṛdhaḥ .. 968
  4 3 2 04 02a sa hi ṣmā jaritṛbhya ā vājaṃ gomantaminvati .
  4 3 2 04 02c pavamānaḥ sahasriṇam .. 969
  4 3 2 04 03a pari viśvāni cetasā mṛjyase pavase matī .
  4 3 2 04 03c sa naḥ soma śravo vidaḥ .. 970
  4 3 2 04 04a abhyarṣa bṛhadyaśo maghavadbhyo dhruvaṃ rayim .
  4 3 2 04 04c iṣaṃ stotṛbhya ā bhara .. 971
  4 3 2 04 05a tvaṃ rājeva suvrato giraḥ somāviveśitha .
  4 3 2 04 05c punāno vahne adbhuta .. 972
  4 3 2 04 06a sa vahnirapsu duṣṭaro mṛjyamāno gabhastyoḥ .
  4 3 2 04 06c somaścamūṣu sīdati .. 973
  4 3 2 04 07a krīḍurmakho na maṃhayuḥ pavitraṃ soma gacchasi .
  4 3 2 04 07c dadhatstotre suvīryam .. 974
body.translated_text:
968: The poet, for the gods' approach, was covered by the woolen filters — conquering all rivalries.
969: For he, the Self-purifying one, procures for the singers a prize rich in cattle, thousandfold.
970: You are cleansed on all sides with thought; you flow with prayers — O <s>Soma</s>, find glory for us.
971: Flow forth with great fame; [bring] enduring wealth for the bountiful — bring nourishment for the praisers.
972: You, like a king of good vows, have entered into the hymns, O <s>Soma</s> — purifying, O bearer, O wondrous one.
973: He, the bearer, hard to overcome in the waters, being cleansed between the hands — <s>Soma</s> settles in the vessels.
974: Playful, vigorous like a generous one, you go to the filter, O <s>Soma</s> — bestowing heroic might upon the praiser.

body.text:
4 3 2 05 01a yavaṃyavaṃ no andhasā puṣṭaṃpuṣṭaṃ pari srava .
  4 3 2 05 01c viśvā ca soma saubhagā .. 975
  4 3 2 05 02a indo yathā tava stavo yathā te jātamandhasaḥ .
  4 3 2 05 02c ni barhiṣi priye sadaḥ .. 976
  4 3 2 05 03a uta no govidaśvavitpavasva somāndhasā .
  4 3 2 05 03c makṣūtamebhirahabhiḥ .. 977
  4 3 2 05 04a yo jināti na jīyate hanti śatrumabhītya .
  4 3 2 05 04c sa pavasva sahasrajit .. 978
body.translated_text:
975: Grain upon grain with the plant, nourishment upon nourishment, flow around for us — and all good fortune, O <s>Soma</s>.
976: O <s>Indu</s>, as is your praise, as is born from the plant — [take] your seat on the beloved sacred grass.
977: And flow for us, O <s>Soma</s>, finder of cattle, finder of horses, with the plant — swiftly, on these days.
978: He who conquers and is not conquered, who slays the enemy by assault — flow, O thousand-winner.

body.text:
4 3 2 06 01a yāste dhārā madhuścuto 'sṛgraminda ūtaye .
  4 3 2 06 01c tābhiḥ pavitramāsadaḥ .. 979
  4 3 2 06 02a so arṣendrāya pītaye tiro vārāṇyavyayā .
  4 3 2 06 02c sīdannṛtasya yonimā .. 980
  4 3 2 06 03a tvaṃ soma pari srava svādiṣṭho aṅgirobhyaḥ .
  4 3 2 06 03c varivoviddhṛtaṃ payaḥ .. 981
body.translated_text:
979: Those streams of yours, dripping honey, that have flowed forth for aid, O <s>Indu</s> — by them you have reached the filter.
980: So flow for <s>Indra</s> to drink, across the woolen filters — seating yourself in the womb of truth.
981: You, O <s>Soma</s>, flow around, sweetest, for the <s>Aṅgirases</s> — finder of wide space, firm milk.

body.text:
4 3 2 07 01a tava śriyo varṣyasyeva vidyutogneścikitra uṣasāmivetayaḥ .
  4 3 2 07 01c yadoṣadhīrabhisṛṣṭo vanāni ca pari svayaṃ cinuṣe annamāsani .. 982
  4 3 2 07 02a vātopajūta iṣito vaśāṃ anu tṛṣu yadannā veviṣadvitiṣṭhase .
  4 3 2 07 02c ā te yatante rathyo3 yathā pṛthakśardhāṃsyagne ajarasya dhakṣataḥ .. 983
  4 3 2 07 03a medhākāraṃ vidathasya prasādhanamagniṃ hotāraṃ paribhūtaraṃ matim .
  4 3 2 07 03c tvāmarbhasya haviṣaḥ samānamittavāṃ maho vṛṇate nānyaṃ tvat .. 984
body.translated_text:
982: Your splendors, O <s>Agni</s>, are perceived like lightnings of a rain-cloud, like the courses of the dawns — when, released upon herbs and forests, you yourself gather food at your seat.
983: Driven by the wind, impelled, following your will — when craving food, you spread across dry [lands]. Your flames strive like chariot-horses, each separately — the hosts of ageless, burning <s>Agni</s>.
984: The creator of wisdom, the accomplisher of the assembly, <s>Agni</s> the <s>Hotṛ</s>, the all-surpassing thought — you alone, the partaker of the small offering; the great ones choose you; none other than you.

body.text:
4 3 2 08 01a purūruṇā ciddhyastyavo nūnaṃ vāṃ varuṇa .
  4 3 2 08 01c mitra vaṃsi vāṃ sumatim .. 985
  4 3 2 08 02a tā vāṃ samyagadruhvāṇeṣamaśyāma dhāma ca .
  4 3 2 08 02c vayaṃ vāṃ mitrā syāma .. 986
  4 3 2 08 03a pātaṃ no mitrā pāyubhiruta trāyethāṃ sutrātrā .
  4 3 2 08 03c sāhyāma dasyūṃ tanūbhiḥ .. 987
body.translated_text:
985: For your aid is indeed most ample, O <s>Varuṇa</s> — O <s>Mitra</s>, may I win your good will.
986: May we, going rightly, without guile, obtain from you both nourishment and an abode — may we be friends of you two.
987: Protect us, O <s>Mitra</s> [and <s>Varuṇa</s>], with your guards, and deliver us, O good deliverers — may we overcome the <s>Dasyus</s> with our bodies.

body.text:
4 3 2 09 01a uttiṣṭhannojasā saha pītvā śipre avepayaḥ .
  4 3 2 09 01c somamindra camūsutam .. 988
  4 3 2 09 02a anu tvā rodasī ubhe spardhamānamadadetām .
  4 3 2 09 02c indra yaddasyuhābhavaḥ .. 989
  4 3 2 09 03a vācamaṣṭāpadīmahaṃ navasraktimṛtāvṛdham .
  4 3 2 09 03c indrātparitanvaṃ mame .. 990
body.translated_text:
988: Rising with might, having drunk, you shook your two cheek-pieces — O <s>Indra</s>, [you drank] the <s>Soma</s> pressed in the vessel.
989: Both heaven and earth watched you as you strove — O <s>Indra</s>, when you became the <s>Dasyu</s>-slayer.
990: The eight-footed, nine-cornered speech that upholds truth — from <s>Indra</s> I measure out its form.

body.text:
4 3 2 10 01a indrāgnī yuvāmime3 'bhi stomā anūṣata .
  4 3 2 10 01c pibataṃ śambhuvā sutam .. 991
  4 3 2 10 02a yā vāṃ santi puruspṛho niyuto dāśuṣe narā .
  4 3 2 10 02c indrāgnī tābhirā gatam .. 992
  4 3 2 10 03a tābhirā gacchataṃ naropedaṃ savanaṃ sutam .
  4 3 2 10 03c indrāgnī somapītaye .. 993
body.translated_text: 991. O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, these praises have been sung to you two; drink the well-pressed [Soma]. || 991 || 992. Whatever much-desired teams you have for the worshipper, O heroes — come with those, O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>. || 992 || 993. Come with those, O heroes, to this pressing, to the pressed [Soma], O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, for the drinking of <s>Soma</s>. || 993 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 11 01a arṣā soma dyumattamo 'bhi droṇāni roruvat .
  4 3 2 11 01c sīdanyonau yoneṣvā .. 994
  4 3 2 11 02a apsā indrāya vāyave varuṇāya marudbhyaḥ .
  4 3 2 11 02c somā arṣantu viṣṇave .. 995
  4 3 2 11 03a iṣaṃ tokāya no dadhadasmabhyaṃ soma viśvataḥ .
  4 3 2 11 03c ā pavasva sahasriṇam .. 996
body.translated_text: 994. Flow forth, O <s>Soma</s>, most brilliant, bellowing toward the wooden vessels; sitting in your seat, in [your] seats. || 994 || 995. With their waters, the <s>Soma</s> juices flow forth to <s>Indra</s>, to <s>Vāyu</s>, to <s>Varuṇa</s>, to the <s>Maruts</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. || 995 || 996. Grant nourishment for our offspring, O <s>Soma</s>, from every side; flow forth, [winning] a thousandfold. || 996 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 12 01a soma u ṣvāṇaḥ sotṛbhiradhi ṣṇubhiravīnām .
  4 3 2 12 01c aśvayeva haritā yāti dhārayā mandrayā yāti dhārayā .. 997
  4 3 2 12 02a anūpe gomāngobhirakṣāḥ somo dugdhābhirakṣāḥ .
  4 3 2 12 02c samudraṃ na saṃvaraṇānyagmanmandī madāya tośate .. 998
body.translated_text: 997. <s>Soma</s>, urged by the pressers, upon the pressing-boards, out of the sheep's [wool] — he goes with a stream like a pair of tawny horses; he goes with a delightful stream. || 997 || 998. In the watery [place], <s>Soma</s>, rich in cattle, unspoilt with cows, milked out, unspoilt — like enclosures [coming] to the ocean, the intoxicating one roars for delight. || 998 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 13 01a yatsoma citramukthyaṃ divyaṃ pārthivaṃ vasu .
  4 3 2 13 01c tannaḥ punāna ā bhara .. 999
  4 3 2 13 02a vṛṣā punāna āyuṃṣi stanayannadhi barhiṣi .
  4 3 2 13 02c hariḥ sanyonimāsadaḥ .. 1000
  4 3 2 13 03a yuvaṃ hi sthaḥ svaḥpatī indraśca soma gopatī .
  4 3 2 13 03c īśānā pipyataṃ dhiyaḥ .. 1001
body.translated_text: 999. O <s>Soma</s>, whatever wonderful, praiseworthy, heavenly, earthly treasure [there is] — being purified, bring that to us. || 999 || 1000. The bull, being purified, thundering over lifespans upon the sacred grass — the golden one has reached the common womb. || 1000 || 1001. For you two are the lords of heaven — <s>Indra</s> and <s>Soma</s>, the lords of cattle; being lords, cause our prayers to swell. || 1001 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 14 01a indro madāya vāvṛdhe śavase vṛtrahā nṛbhiḥ .
  4 3 2 14 01c taminmahatsvājiṣūtimarbhe havāmahe sa vājeṣu pra no 'viṣat .. 1002
  4 3 2 14 02a asi hi vīra senyo 'si bhūri parādadiḥ .
  4 3 2 14 02c asi dabhrasya cidvṛdho yajamānāya śikṣasi sunvate bhūri te vasu .. 1003
  4 3 2 14 03a yadudīrata ājayo dhṛṣṇave dhīyate dhanām .
  4 3 2 14 03c yuṅkṣvā madacyutā harī kaṃ hanaḥ kaṃ vasau dadho 'smāṃ indra vasau dadhaḥ .. 1004
body.translated_text: 1002. <s>Indra</s>, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, has grown for intoxication, for strength, among men; him we invoke in great contests for aid in battle; may he help us in the [winning of] prizes. || 1002 || 1003. For you are a hero, a warrior; you are the great giver-away; you are the increaser even of the small; you bestow upon the sacrificer; your wealth is abundant for the presser. || 1003 || 1004. When the contests arise, wealth is placed for the bold one; yoke the two intoxication-shedding bay horses — whom do you slay? Whom do you place in wealth? Place us, O <s>Indra</s>, in wealth! || 1004 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 15 01a svādoritthā viṣūvato madhvaḥ pibanti gauryaḥ .

  4 3 2 15 02a tā asya pṛśanāyuvaḥ somaṃ śrīṇanti pṛśnayaḥ .
  4 3 2 15 02c priyā indrasya dhenavo vajraṃ hinvanti sāyakaṃ vasvīranu svarājyam .. 1006
  4 3 2 15 03a tā asya namasā sahaḥ saparyanti pracetasaḥ .
  4 3 2 15 03c vratānyasya saścire purūṇi pūrvacittaye vasvīranu svarājyam .. 1007
body.translated_text: 1005. The dappled [cows] drink of the sweet, all-pervading honey; they who travel together with <s>Indra</s>, the bull, rejoice for beauty — the rich ones, following sovereignty. || 1005 || 1006. Those dappled ones, his companions in color, mix the <s>Soma</s>; the dear milch-cows of <s>Indra</s> urge on the <s>vajra</s>-weapon — the rich ones, following sovereignty. || 1006 || 1007. Those watchful ones honor his might with homage; they have followed his many ordinances for prior meditation — the rich ones, following sovereignty. || 1007 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 16 01a asāvyaṃśurmadāyāpsu dakṣo giriṣṭhāḥ .
  4 3 2 16 01c śyeno na yonimāsadat .. 1008
  4 3 2 16 02a śubhramandho devavātamapsu dhautaṃ nṛbhiḥ sutam .
  4 3 2 16 02c svadanti gāvaḥ payobhiḥ .. 1009
  4 3 2 16 03a ādīmaśvaṃ na hetāramaśūśubhannamṛtāya .
  4 3 2 16 03c madho rasaṃ sadhamāde .. 1010
body.translated_text: 1008. The stalk has been pressed for intoxication; the vigorous one, dwelling in the waters, on the mountain — like an eagle he has reached his nest. || 1008 || 1009. The bright drink, desired by the gods, washed in the waters, pressed by men — the cows sweeten it with their milk. || 1009 || 1010. Then they have adorned him like a horse, a charioteer, for immortality — the essence of the mead, at the common feast. || 1010 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 17 01a abhi dyubhnaṃ bṛhadyaśa iṣaspate dīdihi deva devayum .
  4 3 2 17 01c vi kośaṃ madhyamaṃ yuva .. 1011
  4 3 2 17 02a ā vacyasva sudakṣa camvoḥ suto viśāṃ vahnirna viśpatiḥ .
  4 3 2 17 02c vṛṣṭiṃ divaḥ pavasva rītimapo jinvangaviṣṭaye dhiyaḥ .. 1012
body.translated_text: 1011. O possessor of great, widely-famed splendor, O lord of food, shine forth upon the one seeking the gods; open the middle receptacle, O youthful one. || 1011 || 1012. Make yourself heard, O skilful one, pressed in the two bowls; like the carrier of offerings, like the lord of the clan; flow, [sending] the rain of heaven, the stream of waters, for the winning of cattle, impelling the hymns. || 1012 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 18 01a prāṇā śiśurmahīnāṃ hinvannṛtasya dīdhitim .

  4 3 2 18 02a upa tritasya pāṣyo3rabhakta yadguhā padam .
  4 3 2 18 02c yajñasya sapta dhāmabhiradha priyam .. 1014
  4 3 2 18 03a trīṇi tritasya dhārayā pṛṣṭeṣvairayadrayim .
  4 3 2 18 03c mimīte asya yojanā vi sukratuḥ .. 1015
body.translated_text: 1013. The breath, the child of the great [waters], impelling the thought of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), became dear to all, and [became] twofold. || 1013 || 1014. At the heights of <s>Trita</s>, [the Soma] partook of what was hidden at the secret place; at the seven stations of the sacrifice, [he partook of] what is dear. || 1014 || 1015. Through the three streams of <s>Trita</s>, he caused wealth to move upon the heights; the wise one measures out his distances. || 1015 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 19 01a pavasva vājasātaye pavitre dhārayā sutaḥ .
  4 3 2 19 01c indrāya soma viṣṇave devebhyo madhumattaraḥ .. 1016
  4 3 2 19 02a tvāṃ rihanti dhītayo hariṃ pavitre adruhaḥ .
  4 3 2 19 02c vatsaṃ jātaṃ na mātaraḥ pavamāna vidharmaṇi .. 1017
  4 3 2 19 03a tvaṃ dyāṃ ca mahivrata pṛthivīṃ cāti jabhriṣe .
  4 3 2 19 03c prati drāpimamuñcathāḥ pavamāna mahitvanā .. 1018
body.translated_text: 1016. Flow through the filter with a stream for the winning of prizes, pressed — O <s>Soma</s>, the most honeyed, for <s>Indra</s>, for <s>Viṣṇu</s>, for the gods. || 1016 || 1017. The guileless devotions lick you, the golden one, in the filter — like mothers [licking] a new-born calf, O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying), in the ordering. || 1017 || 1018. You, O mighty in vow, have encompassed both heaven and earth; you have put on the cloak, O <s>Pavamāna</s>, with your greatness. || 1018 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 20 01a indurvājī pavate gonyoghā indre somaḥ saha invanmadāya .

  4 3 2 20 02a adha dhārayā madhvā pṛcānastiro roma pavate adridugdhaḥ .
  4 3 2 20 02c indurindrasya sakhyaṃ juṣāṇo devo devasya matsaro madāya .. 1020
  4 3 2 20 03a abhi vratāni pavate punāno devo devāntsvena rasena pṛñcan .
  4 3 2 20 03c indurdharmāṇyṛtuthā vasāno daśa kṣipo avyata sāno avye .. 1021
body.translated_text: 1019. The prize-winning drop flows, his milking-place is the cows; <s>Soma</s>, impelling strength, [flows] to <s>Indra</s> for intoxication; he slays the demons, drives away hostility, creating spaciousness, the king of the host. || 1019 || 1020. Moreover, with a stream mingled with honey, pressed from the stone, [he flows] across the wool; the drop, enjoying the friendship of <s>Indra</s>, the god, the intoxicant, for the god's delight. || 1020 || 1021. Being purified, he flows over the ordinances, the god filling the gods with his own sap; the drop, wearing the laws in due season, strained the ten fingers through the woolen [filter]. || 1021 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 21 01a ā te agna idhīmahi dyumantaṃ devājaram .

  4 3 2 21 02a ā te agna ṛcā haviḥ śukrasya jyotiṣaspate .
  4 3 2 21 02c suścandra dasma viśpate havyavāṭtubhyaṃ hūyata iṣaṃ stotṛbhya ā bhara .. 1023
  4 3 2 21 03a obhe suścandra viśpate darvī śrīṇīṣa āsani .
  4 3 2 21 03c uto na utpupūryā uktheṣu śavasaspata iṣaṃ stotṛbhya ā bhara .. 1024
body.translated_text: 1022. We kindle you, O <s>Agni</s>, brilliant, divine, ageless; that most marvelous [light] of yours, when kindled, blazes in heaven — bring nourishment to the praisers. || 1022 || 1023. O <s>Agni</s>, to you, the lord of bright light, the oblation with a hymn; O bright one, O wonderful one, O lord of the clan, the bearer of oblations is invoked for you — bring nourishment to the praisers. || 1023 || 1024. O bright one, O lord of the clan, fill the two ladles in your mouth; fill us up also; O lord of might, at the chanting of hymns — bring nourishment to the praisers. || 1024 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 22 01a indrāya sāma gāyata viprāya bṛhate bṛhat .
  4 3 2 22 01c brahmākṛte vipaścite panasyave .. 1025
  4 3 2 22 02a tvamindrābhibhūrasi tvaṃ sūryamarocayaḥ .
  4 3 2 22 02c viśvakarmā viśvadevo mahāṃ asi .. 1026
  4 3 2 22 03a vibhrājaṃ jyotiṣā tva3ragaccho rocanaṃ divaḥ .
  4 3 2 22 03c devāsta indra sakhyāya yemire .. 1027
body.translated_text: 1025. Sing a <s>Sāman</s> (chant) to <s>Indra</s>, a great [hymn] to the great inspired one; to the maker of prayer, to the wise, to the glorious one. || 1025 || 1026. You, O <s>Indra</s>, are the conqueror; you caused the sun to shine; the maker of all, the all-divine, you are great. || 1026 || 1027. Shining with radiance, you have reached the luminous realm of heaven; the gods, O <s>Indra</s>, have aligned themselves for your friendship. || 1027 ||

body.text:
4 3 2 23 01a asāvi soma indra te śaviṣṭha dhṛṣṇavā gahi .
  4 3 2 23 01c ā tvā pṛṇaktvindriyaṃ rajaḥ sūryo na raśmibhiḥ .. 1028
  4 3 2 23 02a ā tiṣṭha vṛtrahanrathaṃ yuktā te brahmaṇā harī .
  4 3 2 23 02c arvācīnaṃ su te mano grāvā kṛṇotu vagnunā .. 1029
  4 3 2 23 03a indramiddharī vahato 'pratidhṛṣṭaśavasam .
  4 3 2 23 03c ṛṣīṇāṃ suṣṭutīrupa yajñaṃ ca mānuṣāṇām .. 1030
body.translated_text: 1028. The <s>Soma</s> has been pressed for you, O <s>Indra</s>; O most powerful, come boldly; may the <s>Indra</s>-power fill you, like the sun with its rays. || 1028 || 1029. Mount, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, your chariot; the two bay horses are yoked by prayer; may the pressing-stone, with its sound, turn your mind hitherward. || 1029 || 1030. The two bay horses carry <s>Indra</s>, whose strength is irresistible, to the good praises of the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (seers) and to the sacrifice of men. || 1030 ||

caturtha prapāṭhakaḥ . prathamo 'rdhaḥ

body.translated_text: Fourth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), First Half. 1031. The light of the sacrifice flows, the dear honey, the father of the gods, the generator, rich in treasures; he bestows the hidden gem through self-power — the most intoxicating, exhilarating, powerful essence. || 1031 || 1032. Bellowing, the prize-winning one flows toward the vessel, the lord of heaven, hundred-streamed, all-seeing; the golden one sits in the seats of <s>Mitra</s>, being polished by the sheep's [wool], by the rivers, the bull. || 1032 || 1033. At the head of the rivers, <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying) flows; at the head of speech, the foremost one, you enter among the cows; at the head of prizes you share in the great wealth; well-armed, O <s>Soma</s>, you are pressed by the pressers. || 1033 ||

body.text:
4 4 1 02 01a asṛkṣata pra vājino gavyā somāso aśvayā .
  4 4 1 02 01c śukrāso vīrayāśavaḥ .. 1034
  4 4 1 02 02a śumbhamāno ṛtāyubhirmṛjyamānā gabhastyoḥ .

  4 4 1 02 03c pavantāmāntarikṣyā .. 1036
body.translated_text: 1034. The prize-winning [Soma juices] have flowed forth, seeking cattle, seeking horses — bright ones, seeking heroes, swift. || 1034 || 1035. Being adorned by those who follow <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), being polished by [their] hands, they are purified through the woolen filter. || 1035 || 1036. Those <s>Soma</s> juices purify all the treasures of the worshipper — heavenly, earthly, and atmospheric. || 1036 ||

body.translated_text: 1037. Flow forth, O <s>Soma</s>, for the worship of the gods, swiftly through the filter; enter <s>Indra</s>, O drop, O bull. || 1037 || 1038. Announce your great flood, O bull-like drop, O most brilliant one; [enter] your seat, the womb, the abode, O sustainer. || 1038 || 1039. They have milked out the dear honey, the streams of the pressed juice of the wise one; the most excellent one of good wisdom [has purified] the waters. || 1039 || 1040. You are great — the great waters and rivers flow after you, when you are to be clothed in milk. || 1040 || 1041. The ocean purified itself in the waters — the prop, the support of heaven; <s>Soma</s> [flows] in the filter, seeking us. || 1041 || 1042. The tawny bull has cried aloud, great, beautiful like <s>Mitra</s>; he has shone together with the sun. || 1042 || 1043. O drop, your songs are cleansed with power by the diligent ones, [the songs] with which you adorn yourself for intoxication. || 1043 || 1044. You, the bold one, the world-maker — we seek you for intoxication, for your great praise. || 1044 || 1045. O drop, you are the winner of cattle, the winner of men, the winner of horses, and the winner of prizes — the primordial soul of the sacrifice. || 1045 || 1046. O drop, flow forth for us with a stream of <s>Indra</s>-power from the honey, like the rain-giving <s>Parjanya</s> (rain-god). || 1046 ||

body.translated_text: 1047. Win, O <s>Soma</s>, and conquer great glory, O <s>Pavamāna</s> (self-purifying one); then make us more prosperous. || 1047 || 1048. 4.4.2.3.1140: The head of heaven, the guest of earth — <s>Agni</s> <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, born of <s>Ṛta</s>. The gods, approaching, generated a poet, sovereign, guest of the peoples — a vessel [for us].
4.4.2.3.1141: You, O immortal, all the gods greet as you are born, like a child. By your deeds they attained immortality, O <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, when you shone forth between the parents.
4.4.2.3.1142: The navel of sacrifices, the seat of riches — the great great ones greet. The gods generated <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, the charioteer of the rites, the banner of the sacrifice.

4.4.2.4.1143: Sing forth to <s>Mitra</s>, to <s>Varuṇa</s>, with inspired speech — the great-ruled ones, the lofty <s>Ṛta</s>.
4.4.2.4.1144: The supreme rulers, of ghee-born [origin], both <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> — gods praised among gods.
4.4.2.4.1145: Grant us, you two, great earthly and great heavenly wealth. Great is your dominion among the gods.

4.4.2.5.1146: Come, O <s>Indra</s>, O bright-rayed one! These [<s>Soma</s> juices] are prepared for you, purified through fine [filters] and bodies.
4.4.2.5.1147: Come, O <s>Indra</s>, urged by thought, impelled by the inspired! Come to the sacred words of the worshiper when the [<s>Soma</s>] is pressed.
4.4.2.5.1148: Come, O <s>Indra</s>, hastening! Come to the sacred words, O bay-horsed one! At the pressing, place your delight in us.

4.4.2.6.1150: The mortal who, when [<s>Agni</s>] is kindled, seeks to win <s>Indra</s>'s favor — [crosses] the waters more easily, for glory.
4.4.2.6.1151: Fill for us prize-bearing nourishment and swift steeds — to carry <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>.

4.4.2.7.1152: The drop has gone forth to <s>Indra</s>'s appointed [place]; a friend does not violate a friend's agreement. Like a youth with maidens, <s>Soma</s> mingles in the jar, going by a hundred paths.
4.4.2.7.1153: Your thoughts, joy-yoked, praise-yoked, wonder-yoked, have stridden forth at the [<s>Soma</s>]-coverings. The hymns sang of the golden one at play; the milch-cows have swelled with their milk.
4.4.2.7.1154: O <s>Soma</s>, purify yourself with your wave, O <s>Pavamāna</s>, [bringing] us held-together, overflowing nourishment — that which yields milk for us thrice daily without fail: rich in substance, prize-bearing, honey-sweet, granting good heroes.

4.4.2.8.1156: The unconquerable, the fierce one, the conqueror in battles, in whom the great rivers [trembled] — the milch-cows lowed at his birth; the heavens and the earths lowed.

4.4.2.9.1157: Sit down, O friends; sing forth to the one being purified. Adorn [him] with sacrifices, like a child, for beauty.
4.4.2.9.1158: Release him together, like a calf to its mothers — the home-finder, the godly intoxication, the twice-strong one.
4.4.2.9.1159: Purify the skill-accomplishing one — so that he be most peaceful for the warrior host's advance, for <s>Mitra</s>, for <s>Varuṇa</s>.

4.4.2.10.1162: O <s>Soma</s>, go forth into <s>Indra</s>'s belly — guided by men, pressed by stones.

4.4.2.11.1164: those among the <s>Ārjīkas</s>, among the [people of] <s>Kṛtva</s>, those in the midst of the homesteads, or among the five peoples —
4.4.2.11.1165: may they purify rain from heaven for us, [and grant us] good heroism — the sweetly-sounding divine drops.

4.4.2.12.1167: For everywhere you are alike; you are lord over all directions. We invoke you in battles.
4.4.2.12.1168: In battles we invoke <s>Agni</s> for aid, seeking prizes — him of wondrous gifts in the contests.

4.4.2.13.1169: Bring us, O <s>Indra</s>, might and manly strength, O hundred-powered, O all-seeing one — a hero, conqueror of armies.
4.4.2.13.1170: For you are our father, O <s>Vasu</s>; you have become our mother, O hundred-powered one. Therefore we seek your favor.
4.4.2.13.1171: You, O mighty one, O much-invoked, the prize-seeking one — I call upon you, O thousand-powered one. Grant us good heroism.
4.4.2.13.1172: If, O wondrous <s>Indra</s>, there is nothing here not given by you, O stone-armed one — may that wealth find us, O <s>Vasu</s>; bring [it] with both hands.
4.4.2.13.1173: What you consider most choiceworthy, O <s>Indra</s>, that luminous [gift] — bring it here. May we know of your limitless giving.
4.4.2.13.1174: Your mind, which grants wealth in all directions, is heard [to be] great. With that, O stone-armed one, may you enable [us] to win the firm prize.

4.5.1.1.1175: The <s>Maruts</s> groom and adorn the newborn, delightful child, the inspired one, with their host. The poet, by [his] poetry a poet indeed, <s>Soma</s> passes through the filter, resounding with songs.
4.5.1.1.1176: Seer-minded, seer-making, self-radiant, of a thousand paths, the track of the poets — seeking to win the third realm, <s>Soma</s> the mighty rules in the pattern of the <s>virāj</s> [metre].
4.5.1.1.1177: Dwelling in the vessel, the eagle, the bird bearing [riches], the cow-finder, the drop bearing weapons — joining the wave of the waters and the ocean, the mighty one declares the fourth realm.

4.5.1.2.1178: These <s>Soma</s> drops have flowed toward the dear desire of <s>Indra</s>, increasing his heroism.
4.5.1.2.1181: The purifying ones, dwelling in the vessel, going to <s>Vāyu</s> and the <s>Aśvins</s> — may they bestow upon us good heroism.
4.5.1.2.1180: For <s>Indra</s>'s generosity, O <s>Soma</s>, purifying yourself, urge on [his] heart — [seeking] the birthplace of the gods.
4.5.1.2.1181: Ten fingers groom you; seven thoughts impel you. The inspired ones have intoxicated [themselves] in accordance [with you].
4.5.1.2.1182: For the gods, for intoxication, I release you to flow across the sheepskin. We clothe you with cow's [milk].
4.5.1.2.1183: The reddish-golden one purifies himself into the jars — his garments of cattle [i.e., milk] he weaves around.
4.5.1.2.1184: O bountiful one, purify yourself for us; slay every hatred. O <s>Indu</s>, enter as our friend.
4.5.1.2.1185: You, the man-watching one, drunk by <s>Indra</s>, the light-finder — may we partake of nourishment for progeny.
4.5.1.2.1186: Flow around with rain from heaven, with glory over the earth. O <s>Soma</s>, place strength for us in battles.

body.translated_text: 1187. <s>Soma</s>, being purified, flows forth, thousand-streamed, through the sheep's [wool], to the appointed place of <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Indra</s>. || 1187 || 1188. Sing forth, O desiring ones, to <s>Pavamāna</s> (the Self-Purifying), the wise one, well-pressed for the invocation of the gods. || 1188 || 1189. The <s>Soma</s> juices of thousandfold power are purified for the winning of prizes, being praised for the invocation of the gods. || 1189 || 1190. Flow forth also for our winning of prizes, great nourishment; brilliantly, O <s>Indu</s> (Soma-drop), [grant us] heroic power. || 1190 || 1191. Like horses urged on by charioteers, the swift ones have flowed forth for the winning of prizes, through the woolen filter. || 1191 || 1192. May those divine drops, being pressed, purify for us thousandfold wealth [and] heroic power. || 1192 || 1193. The lowing drops flow forth like mothers toward a calf; they have hastened [from] the hands. || 1193 || 1194. Pleasing, intoxicating, crying aloud for <s>Indra</s>, O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying) — slay all hatreds. || 1194 || 1195. Smiting the niggardly, the self-purifying ones, beholding the sun — sit in the womb of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order). || 1195 ||

body.translated_text: 1196. The <s>Soma</s> drops have flowed forth, pressed, with the stream of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), most sweet for <s>Indra</s>. || 1196 || 1197. The inspired ones have praised [him], like milch-cows toward a calf, <s>Indra</s>, for the drinking of <s>Soma</s>. || 1197 || 1198. Shedding intoxication, he dwells in [his] seat; the wise wave of the river — <s>Soma</s>, resting upon the [milk of] cows. || 1198 || 1199. At the navel of heaven, all-seeing, he exalts himself in the woolen filter — <s>Soma</s>, who is the wise sage of good deeds. || 1199 || 1200. Whatever <s>Soma</s> is placed within the vessels, within the filter — that drop has embraced. || 1200 || 1201. The drop propels the voice from the surface of the ocean, quickening the honey-dripping vessel. || 1201 || 1202. The ever-praised lord of the forest [is like] a milch-cow, full of nourishing [milk] within, urged on by the yoke-companions of men. || 1202 || 1203. O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying), pour forth with your stream wealth of thousandfold splendor, born of itself, for us, O <s>Indu</s>. || 1203 || 1204. The dear sage, the inspired one of heaven, pressed with a stream, <s>Soma</s> is impelled from afar. || 1204 ||

body.translated_text: 1205. Your mighty powers surge forth, like the sound of a river's wave; urge on the wheel of the reed. || 1205 || 1206. At your impulsion, three voices rise up, eager for battle, when you pass over the woolen ridge. || 1206 || 1207. With woolen filters, they urge on the dear golden one with the pressing-stones — <s>Pavamāna</s> (the Self-Purifying), dripping with honey. || 1207 || 1208. Flow forth, O most intoxicating one, through the filter with your stream, O sage; sit in the seat of the hymn. || 1208 || 1209. Flow, O most intoxicating one, being anointed with cows [i.e., milk] and with nights; enter the belly of <s>Indra</s>. || 1209 ||

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1210. With this offering flow around, you who, O <s>Indu</s> (Soma-drop), in intoxications, have slain ninety-nine [foes]. || 1210 || 1211. Who forthwith, like a fortress, for the faith of <s>Divodāsa</s>, [overthrew] <s>Śambara</s>; moreover that <s>Turvaśa</s> and <s>Yadu</s> — || 1211 || 1212. Flow around for us, O <s>Indu</s> (Soma-drop), horse-finding, cattle-rich, gold-bearing; pour forth thousandfold nourishment. || 1212 ||

body.translated_text: 1213. Smiting the enemies, <s>Soma</s> flows, [smiting] the niggardly; going to the appointed place of <s>Indra</s>. || 1213 || 1214. O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying), bring us great wealth; slay the enemies; grant us, O <s>Indu</s>, fame rich in heroes. || 1214 || 1215. Neither a hundred nor [any] hurts diminish you when you would give your bounty, when being purified you are eager for battle. || 1215 ||

body.translated_text: 1216. Flow with that stream by which you caused the sun to shine, impelling the waters of men. || 1216 || 1217. <s>Pavamāna</s> (the Self-Purifying) has yoked the swift steed over the mind, to travel through the atmosphere. || 1217 || 1218. And <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) yoked the tawny mares to the chariot for travel, the drop declaring 'I am <s>Indra</s>.' || 1218 ||

body.translated_text: 1219. Make <s>Agni</s>, your god, the most sacrificial messenger in the rite, together with [other] fires; he who among mortals is trustworthy, whose laws are true, whose head is burning, who feeds on <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter), the purifier. || 1219 || 1220. Snorting like a horse at pasture, he spread abroad when he arose from the great enclosure; his wind blows after his flame; and moreover, your path is black [with smoke]. || 1220 || 1221. The ageless [flames] of yours, O <s>Agni</s>, blaze forth, of the newly-born bull; your ruddy smoke goes toward heaven; for you go, O <s>Agni</s>, as a messenger to the gods. || 1221 ||

body.translated_text: 1222. We urge that <s>Indra</s> on for the slaying of the great <s>Vṛtra</s>; may he become the bull, the powerful one. || 1222 || 1223. <s>Indra</s> is made for the gift-giving, the mightiest; he is set for strength; brilliant, famous, he is the <s>Soma</s>-lover. || 1223 || 1224. Gathered by song, like a thunderbolt, strong-armed, unshakeable — the fierce, unconquered one has grown. || 1224 ||

body.translated_text: 1225. O <s>Adhvaryu</s> (priest), bring the <s>Soma</s> pressed with stones to the filter; purify it for <s>Indra</s> to drink. || 1225 || 1226. Of your juice, O <s>Indu</s>, the gods have partaken of the sweet, O <s>Pavamāna</s>, [and] the <s>Maruts</s>. || 1226 || 1227. The supreme nectar of heaven, the <s>Soma</s> for <s>Indra</s> the <s>vajra</s>-wielder — press the most honeyed one. || 1227 ||
