body.translated_text: 1228. The upholder of heaven flows, the creative essence, the skill of the gods, to be rejoiced in by men; the golden one, released like a steed among competitors, freely makes his splendors in the rivers. || 1228 || 1229. Like a hero, he seizes weapons in [his] hands, seeking to win the heavenly [world]; [he is] a charioteer in cattle-raids; impelling the fury of <s>Indra</s>, the active drop is urged on by the sages. || 1229 || 1230. O <s>Soma</s>, O <s>Pavamāna</s>, enter the belly of <s>Indra</s> with your wave, growing strong; fill us like a lightning-cloud [fills] both worlds; prosper us continually with prizes through [our] devotion. || 1230 ||

body.translated_text: 1231. Whether, O <s>Indra</s>, you are invoked by men in the east, the west, the north, or the south — you are a mighty one among many men; for <s>Anu</s>, you are the helper; for <s>Turvaśa</s>, the protector. || 1231 || 1232. Whether in [the abode of] <s>Ruma</s>, <s>Ruśama</s>, or <s>Śyāvaka</s>, O <s>Indra</s>, you delight in their company — the <s>Kaṇvas</s>, bearers of sacred prayer, send you hymns of praise; O <s>Indra</s>, granting [our wish], come. || 1232 ||

body.translated_text: 1233. May <s>Indra</s> hear both [calls] of ours, this word from near; may the bounteous one come with all [his powers] for the drinking of <s>Soma</s>, the most powerful one, with devotion. || 1233 || 1234. For the two <s>Dhiṣaṇas</s> (ritual bowls) have fashioned him, the self-ruling bull, with their strength; and you sit first among the comparisons — for your mind desires <s>Soma</s>. || 1234 ||

body.translated_text: 1235. Flow, O divine one, for long life; let your intoxication go to <s>Indra</s>; mount <s>Vāyu</s> by your law. || 1235 || 1236. O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying), you shower down famous wealth, O <s>Soma</s>; enter the ocean, O <s>Indu</s>. || 1236 || 1237. Smiting the enemies, you flow, O <s>Soma</s>, the intoxicating, knower of deeds; push away the godless people. || 1237 ||

body.translated_text: 1238. Flow forth for us the most prize-winning wealth, desired a hundredfold, O drop, sustaining a thousandfold, of great brilliance, dazzling. || 1238 || 1239. Of this your bounty, O wealth, O dwelling, much-desired — may we be nearest to the food; may we be in your favor, O supporter of the needy. || 1239 || 1240. That sounding drop has flowed over the wool, releasing intoxication; [he] the stream which, rising at the sacrifice, goes forth like a gleam, seeking cattle. || 1240 || 1241. Flow forth, O <s>Soma</s>, the great ocean, the father of the gods, [pervading] all the realms. || 1241 || 1242. Bright, flow forth, O <s>Soma</s>, for the gods, for heaven and earth, and as a blessing for offspring. || 1242 || 1243. You are the sustainer of heaven, the bright colostrum; O prize-winner, flow forth in the true dispensation. || 1243 ||

Like a poet worthy of praise, whom the gods have thus placed doubly among mortals. || 1245 || 1246. O youngest one, protect the men of the worshipper; hear the songs; protect the offspring and [protect us] by yourself. || 1246 ||

body.translated_text: 1247. Come to us, O <s>Indra</s>, dear one, ever-victorious, unconcealed; wide on every side like a mountain, lord of heaven. || 1247 || 1248. For truly, O <s>Soma</s>-drinker, you have pervaded both heaven and earth; O <s>Indra</s>, you are the increaser of the presser, lord of heaven. || 1248 || 1249. For you, O <s>Indra</s>, are the upholder of ancient cities; the slayer of the <s>Dasyu</s> (foe), the increaser of [pious] purpose, lord of heaven. || 1249 ||

body.translated_text: 1250. The breaker of cities, the young sage, of immeasurable strength, was born — <s>Indra</s>, the upholder of all action, the thunderbolt-wielder, much-praised. || 1250 || 1251. You, O <s>Indra</s>, opened the cave of <s>Vala</s> rich in cattle; the gods who were without fear came to you, being praised. || 1251 || 1252. <s>Indra</s>, the lord of strength, they have praised with hymns; whose gifts are a thousand, or even more. || 1252 ||

body.translated_text: Fifth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), Second Half. 1253. The ocean has stepped forth in the first dispensation, generating offspring, the guardian of the world; the great <s>Soma</s>, the bull, has grown in the filter, on the summit of the wool, sounding like a stone. || 1253 || 1254. Being purified, you gladden <s>Vāyu</s> for our seeking and for our bounty; you gladden <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>; you gladden the host of the <s>Maruts</s>; you gladden the gods; you gladden heaven and earth, O divine <s>Soma</s>. || 1254 || 1255. <s>Soma</s> the great bull accomplished that great [deed] — when the embryo of the waters chose the gods; the <s>Pavamāna</s> (self-purifying one) placed power in <s>Indra</s>; the drop generated light in the sun. || 1255 ||

body.translated_text: 1256. This immortal god flies like a winged one; sitting in the wooden vessels. || 1256 || 1257. This god, praised by the inspired ones, plunges into the waters, bestowing treasures upon the worshipper. || 1257 || 1258. This hero, the <s>Pavamāna</s> (self-purifying one), seeks to win all desirable things, like a warrior with his companions. || 1258 || 1259. This god drives like a charioteer; the <s>Pavamāna</s> extends [in all] directions; he makes manifest the eloquent. || 1259 || 1260. This god, the <s>Pavamāna</s>, the tawny one, is cleansed by the praise-loving ones, the followers of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order), for the prize. || 1260 || 1261. This god, fashioned by the inspired one, runs past [all] crookedness; the <s>Pavamāna</s>, the inviolable. || 1261 || 1262. This one runs through heaven, beyond the realms, in a stream; the <s>Pavamāna</s>, crying aloud. || 1262 || 1263. This one has pervaded heaven, beyond the realms, untouched; the <s>Pavamāna</s>, whose rite is good. || 1263 || 1264. This god, with ancient birth, pressed for the gods — the tawny one flows through the filter. || 1264 || 1265. This one, of many vows, being born, generating nourishment — being pressed, he flows forth in a stream. || 1265 ||

body.translated_text: 1266. This hero goes with wisdom through the fine [filter], like with swift chariots; going to the appointed place of <s>Indra</s>. || 1266 || 1267. This one is much contemplated with wisdom, for the great worship of the gods; where the immortals sat. || 1267 || 1268. The descendants of <s>Āyu</s> cleanse this one who is to be cleansed, in the vessels; him who is spreading out great nourishment. || 1268 || 1269. This one, placed, is led through the purifying path; when the shining ones urge [him] onward. || 1269 || 1270. This prize-winner goes forth with golden ornaments, with shining drops; becoming the lord of rivers. || 1270 || 1271. This one shakes his horns, the bull of the herd sharpens [them]; bearing manly strength with power. || 1271 || 1272. This one who absorbs treasures goes beyond the obstacles; he comes down to the dwellings. || 1272 || 1273. These ten fingers urge the tawny one to go, the well-armed, the most intoxicating. || 1273 ||

body.translated_text: 1274. This bull-like chariot is woven with woolen strainers; going to the thousandfold prize. || 1274 || 1275. The maidens of <s>Trita</s> urge the tawny one with the stones — the drop for <s>Indra</s> to drink. || 1275 || 1276. This one settles among human [settlements] like a falcon among the peoples; going like a lover to a maiden. || 1276 || 1277. This intoxicating juice, the child of heaven, gazes downward — the drop that has entered the strainer. || 1277 || 1278. This tawny one, the sustainer, flows forth for the drinking, pressed; crying aloud toward the dear womb. || 1278 || 1279. The ten tawny [fingers] cleanse this one, the diligent ones; [the songs] by which he adorns himself for intoxication. || 1279 ||

body.translated_text: 1280. This prize-winner, urged by men, the lord of all-discovering mind, runs through the woolen strainer. || 1280 || 1281. This <s>Soma</s>, pressed for the gods, has flowed into the filter, entering all the realms. || 1281 || 1282. This immortal god shines upon his seat, the slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the most god-worshipping. || 1282 || 1283. This <s>Pavamāna</s> has illumined the sun above in heaven; the intoxicating intoxication in the filter. || 1284 || 1285. This one delights together with the sun, dwelling with <s>Vivasvat</s>; the inviolable lord of speech. || 1285 ||

body.translated_text: 1286. This sage, much-praised, exults in the filter; being purified, destroying enemies. || 1286 || 1287. This one is poured around for <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, the heaven-winning, the accomplisher of skill, in the filter. || 1287 || 1288. This one, pressed, is led by men — the crown of heaven, the bull, <s>Soma</s>, the all-knowing, in the forest. || 1288 || 1289. This one, the <s>Pavamāna</s>, seeking cattle, has cried aloud, seeking gold — the drop, ever-victorious, unconquered. || 1289 || 1290. This impetuous tawny bull, the drop, being purified, has sprinkled in the atmosphere, [filling] <s>Indra</s>. || 1290 || 1291. This impetuous, inviolable <s>Soma</s> flows forth being purified — divine, hero-like, slayer of the malicious. || 1291 ||

1341: He who alone distributes wealth to the mortal who worships — the lord, irresistible — truly he is <s>Indra</s>.
1342: Even he who, rich in pressings, seeks to serve you from many [quarters] — that fierce power he attains — truly he is <s>Indra</s>.
1343: When will he spurn the niggardly mortal like a mushroom with his foot? — truly he is <s>Indra</s>.

1346: Yoke your maned bay horses, the two bulls filling the girths — come hither, O much-invoked one, let them bring you to the sacrifice.

Sixth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, First Half.
1347: Well-kindled, bring us the gods, O <s>Agni</s>, to the one with oblation — O <s>Hotṛ</s>, O Purifier, and worship [them].
1348: O <s>Tanūnapāt</s> (Self-born fire), make our sacrifice honey-sweet among the gods, O poet — today, for the invocation.
1349: I invoke here the beloved <s>Narāśaṃsa</s> (Praise of Men) at this sacrifice — the honey-tongued one, adorner of the rite.
1350: Praise with worship the most glorious god who comes with his chariot — the dear guest of the clans, golden-jawed.

1355: Spurn with your foot the niggardly <s>Paṇis</s>; you are great — no one is your equal.
1356: You are lord of the pressed [<s>Somas</s>], O <s>Indra</s>, and of the unpressed — you are king of peoples.

1359: When, O <s>Soma</s>, you are cleansed by the wise ones with ten fingers, you are strained through the sheep's fleece — may <s>Indra</s> be intoxicated by your juices, O drop.

1366: For we delight in you, O pressed <s>Soma</s>, for the great battle — you destroy hatreds in the struggle for the prize.

body.text:

1368: Thus for the great immortal abode — flow, O bright one, the heavenly first milk (<s>pīyūṣa</s>).
1369: May <s>Indra</s> drink of your pressed [juice], O <s>Soma</s>, for wisdom, for skill — and all the gods.

1370: Like the sun's rays, the intoxicating drops stream forth together, impelled, causing motion — the swift ones [flow] around the stretched thread [of the filter]; without <s>Indra</s>, not even a single abode flows.
1371: The thought is mixed, the honey is poured; the joyful woman [Vāc/Speech] is stirred within the seat — the Self-purifying one, like a continuous stream of pressers, the honeyed one, flows to the hall.
1372: Like a warrior sent by a king, <s>Soma</s> the poet rushes forth through the filter — the wondrous offspring of heaven, the embryo of truth.

body.text:

body.translated_text:
1373: Men generated <s>Agni</s> from the fire-sticks with meditation, shaken forth by hand, the praiseworthy one — far-seeing, lord of the house, the priest.
1374: That <s>Agni</s> the <s>Vasus</s> placed for good vision, for protection from everywhere — he who is worthy of skill, who was always in the house.
1375: Once kindled, O <s>Agni</s>, shine before us with unceasing, quivering flame — may your troop of offspring never perish, O ageless one.

body.text:

  4 6 1 11 03c prati vastoraha dyubhiḥ .. 1378
body.translated_text:
1376: This speckled bull has come, setting [himself] before the mother — and approaching the father, [going to] heaven.
1377: He moves within the luminous spaces, breathing forth and in — the great bull has looked upon heaven.
1378: Thirty abodes he illumines; speech is directed to the winged [sun] — at the opening of dawn, day by day.

Sixth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, Second Half.
1379: Approaching the sacrifice, let us speak a <s>mantra</s> to <s>Agni</s> — who hears from afar and near.
1380: He who, the ancient one, in the clans when gathered at war, protected the home of the worshipper.
1381: May that most peaceful <s>Agni</s> protect for us our household wealth — both known and unknown to us.
1382: Encompass the haters on all sides, O all-knowing one — may we be masters of wealth, O <s>Agni</s>.

body.text:

  4 6 2 02 02c ā devāntsomapītaye .. 1384
  4 6 2 02 03a udagne bhārata dyumadajasreṇa davidyutat .
  4 6 2 02 03c śocā vi bhāhyajara .. 1385
body.translated_text:
1383: O <s>Agni</s>, yoke your steeds, O god, the good ones — the swift ones carry [you] well.
1384: Come toward us, bring forth the offerings for feasting — bring the gods for <s>Soma</s>-drinking.
1385: Blaze forth, O <s>Agni</s> of the <s>Bharatas</s>, with brilliant, unceasing trembling light — shine forth with flame, O ageless one.

body.text:

body.translated_text:
1386: For the presser of the plant, the mortal desires that speech — drive away the niggardly dog, like the <s>Bhṛgus</s> struck down the hostile one.
1387: The sister was enveloped in the garment, like a son for the parents' embrace — like a lover of women, like a bridegroom, he sat in the womb [of the filter].
1388: He, the hero, the accomplisher of skill, who propped apart heaven and earth — the lord of cattle, mighty, the lord of steeds.

body.text:

body.translated_text:
1389: Without a rival brother, alone, without a peer, O <s>Indra</s>, you are so from birth of old — in battle indeed you seek friendship.
1390: You find no wealthy [rival] for friendship; your divine steeds speed on — when you make the thundering, gathering [all] together, then you are called upon like a father.

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.05.01: Let a thousand, let a hundred [horses], yoked to the golden chariot — prayer-yoked, tawny, long-maned — carry you, O <s>Indra</s>, for the drinking of <s>Soma</s>! (1391)
4.6.2.05.02: Let the two tawny [horses] with peacock-like tails, white-backed, carry you in the golden chariot — for the drinking of the eloquent [<s>Soma</s>] juice, of the sweet one! (1392)
4.6.2.05.03: Drink of this pressed [<s>Soma</s>], O lover of songs, as [you were] the first drinker! This delightful offering of the adorned, juicy [<s>Soma</s>] awaits for intoxication. (1393)

body.text:

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.06.01: O pressers, pour around the praise-song like a swift horse, crossing the air — filling the forests, overflowing with water! (1394)
4.6.2.06.02: The thousand-streamed bull, the milk-yielding one, dear to the divine offspring — he who, born of cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>), has grown by cosmic order — the divine king, the great cosmic order. (1395)

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.07.01: May <s>Agni</s>, desiring riches, slay the <s>Vṛtras</s> with his shining — kindled, bright, receiving oblations! (1396)
4.6.2.07.02: The father of the father, flashing in the womb of the mother, in the imperishable — sitting in the womb of cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>). (1397)
4.6.2.07.03: Bring the sacred word (<s>brahma</s>) rich in offspring, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, O all-seeing one! O <s>Agni</s>, [that] which shines in heaven! (1398)

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.08.01: By his impulsion, in winter, being purified, the god has mixed his essence with the gods; pressed, he goes around the filter, resounding — like a friend, the invoker [goes to] the cattle-rich abode. (1399)
4.6.2.08.02: Wearing beautiful garments altogether, the great sage proclaiming utterances — announce yourself in the bowls, being purified, O far-seeing one, wakeful at the gods' feast! (1400)
4.6.2.08.03: The dear one is being cleansed at the summit in the sheep's [wool], the most glorious, ruling over the glorious, among us — resounding, running, being purified. May you [gods] protect us always with blessings! (1401)

4.6.2.09.01: Come now, let us praise <s>Indra</s>, the pure one, with a pure <s>Sāman</s>-song! May he who has grown great by pure praises, pure, with blessings, be gracious! (1402)
4.6.2.09.02: O <s>Indra</s>, come to us, pure! Pure, with pure aids! Pure, bestow wealth! Pure, be gladdened, O <s>Soma</s>-drinker! (1403)
4.6.2.09.03: For, O <s>Indra</s>, pure, you [bestow] wealth upon us; pure, [you give] treasures to the worshipper. Pure, you slay the <s>Vṛtras</s>; pure, you seek to win the prize. (1404)

body.text:

4.6.2.10.01: O <s>Agni</s>, we devise a praise-song, effective, heaven-touching, today — of the god who desires riches. (1405)
4.6.2.10.02: May <s>Agni</s> delight in our songs — the invoker (<s>Hotṛ</s>) who [dwells] among men. May he worship the divine folk! (1406)
4.6.2.10.03: You, O <s>Agni</s>, are widely renowned — the beloved invoker, the choicest. Through you they extend the sacrifice. (1407)

4.6.2.11.02: With a hero's troop, all-heroic, victorious — flow forth, O winner of riches! Sharp-weaponed, swift-bowed, in battles unvanquished, conquering foes in armies! (1409)
4.6.2.11.03: Making wide pastures fearless, flow forth together, O bountiful one! Seeking to win the waters, the dawns, the heavens — cry out great prizes for us! (1410)

body.text:

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.12.01: You, O <s>Indra</s>, are glorious — the residue-drinker, the lord of strength. You slay the irresistible <s>Vṛtras</s> — alone, the ancient one, preeminent, upholder of peoples. (1411)
4.6.2.12.02: That [is] you whom we now entreat, O <s>Asura</s>, O wise one — like a share of bounty. Great, like a hide, are your shelters, O <s>Indra</s> — may your favors reach us! (1412)

body.text:

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.13.01: We have chosen you, the most worshipful, the god, the immortal invoker (<s>Hotṛ</s>) among the gods — of good skill for this sacrifice. (1413)
4.6.2.13.02: The child of the waters (<s>Apāṃ Napāt</s>), the fortunate, the brightly shining — <s>Agni</s> of supreme flame. May he worship for us the favor of <s>Mitra</s>, of <s>Varuṇa</s>, and of the waters, in heaven. (1414)

body.text:

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.14.01: The mortal whom you, O <s>Agni</s>, protect in battles, whom you impel in contests — he shall gain perpetual nourishment. (1415)
4.6.2.14.02: No one's overpowering goes beyond him — the prize is worth hearing. (1416)
4.6.2.14.03: May he, beholding all peoples, be the conqueror with steeds — may he be the winner with inspired ones! (1417)

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.15.01: Together the sisters, the ten thoughts of the wise one, like bow-women, anoint the bull. The tawny one has run around the offspring of the sun — he has reached the wooden vessel like a swift racer. (1418)
4.6.2.15.02: Bellowing like a child with its mothers, the bull, abounding in choice gifts, has rushed with the waters. Like a young man going to the appointed [meeting] with a maiden, he meets the vessel with the dawn-cows. (1419)
4.6.2.15.03: And the drop (<s>Indu</s>) has swelled the udder of the uninjured [cow], the wise one accompanies with streams. The cows anoint the head in the vessels with milk — like [those adorned] with washed treasures. (1420)

body.text:

  4 6 2 1600a bhūyāma te sumatau vājino vayaṃ mā na starabhimātaye .

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.16.01: Drink of the pressed, juicy [<s>Soma</s>]! Be gladdened, O <s>Indra</s>, by the cattle-rich [offering]! Be our kinsman in the communal feast for increase! May your insights aid us! (1421)
4.6.2.16.02: May we, the prize-seekers, be in your good will! Do not abandon us to hostility! Protect us with brilliant aids! Guide us into [your] favors! (1422)

body.text:

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.17.01: Thrice seven milch cows have yielded the true mixture for him in the highest heaven. Four other worlds he made as coverings, lovely — when he grew by cosmic ordinances (<s>ṛta</s>). (1423)
4.6.2.17.02: He, partaking of the immortal's beauty, has pervaded both heavens by poetic art (<s>kāvya</s>). The sharpest waters have encompassed [him] with bounty — when they know the seat by the glory of the god. (1424)
4.6.2.17.03: May those banners of his be immortal, indestructible, through both births — by which [they who purify with] manly deeds and divine [power] purify; then with devotion they seized the king. (1425)

body.text:

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.18.01: Flow toward <s>Vāyu</s> for [his] enjoyment, being praised! Being purified, toward <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>! Toward the swift-thought hero standing in the chariot! Toward <s>Indra</s> the bull, the <s>vajra</s>-armed! (1426)
4.6.2.18.02: Flow toward fine garments, good raiment! Being purified, toward the well-milking cows! Toward shining gold for our sustenance! Toward horses with chariots, O divine <s>Soma</s>! (1427)
4.6.2.18.03: Flow toward us with heavenly riches! Being purified, toward all earthly [treasures]! Toward that by which we may obtain wealth — flow, O seer's son, for us, like <s>Jamadagni</s>! (1428)

body.text:

body.translated_text:
4.6.2.19.01: When you were born, O unprecedented bountiful one, for the slaying of <s>Vṛtra</s> — then you spread out the earth, then you propped up heaven. (1429)
4.6.2.19.02: Then was your sacrifice born, then the hymn and the laughter. You are the overlord of all — of what has been born and what is yet to be born. (1430)
4.6.2.19.03: Set forth the cooked among the raw! Cause the sun to mount in heaven! Like a hot [milk-offering], the great <s>Sāman</s>-chant, heated with beautiful praises — pleasing to the lover of songs. (1431)

4.6.2.20.01: Your great [ecstasy], O lord of bays, as if drinking from a [great] vessel — [your] intoxicating exhilaration! Your bull-like drop (<s>Indu</s>), O bull, the racer, the supreme winner of a thousand [prizes]. (1432)

Born together with purpose, grown together with strength, increased together with heroic powers, conquering enemies, all-seeing; the giver of desirable wealth to the praiser, O wise one — the true drop, the god, followed the god, the true <s>Indu</s> [followed] the true <s>Indra</s>. || 1487 || 1488. body.translated_text: Seventh <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), First Half. 1489. Praise <s>Indra</s>, the lord of cattle, with song, as is known; the firm lord of truth, the true lord. || 1489 || 1490. The ancient, primordial nectar, the praiseworthy one — from the great depth of heaven they milked it forth; all beings sounded forth toward <s>Indra</s> as he was being born. || 1494 || 1495. Then some, beholding him, the kinsman, the brightly-shining, the heavenly ones, sang praises; like the veil of heaven, <s>Savitṛ</s> opens [it]. || 1495 || 1496. And when, O <s>Pavamāna</s> (Self-Purifying), you [encompass] these two worlds and all these beings with your greatness — like a bull as the leader in the herd, you shine forth. || 1496 ||

You bestow in herds, many thousands and hundreds, for giving; we have made the breaker of forts, whose speech is wise, [our own] — singing to <s>Indra</s> for protection. || 1582 ||

body.text:

body.translated_text: He who distributes all wealth, the delightful <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker) of the peoples—may the first cups of honey-drink and hymns of praise go forth to <s>Agni</s>. (1583) Like a chariot-horse [adorned] with songs, the bountiful god-seeking ones polish him; O wondrous lord of the settlement, carry across for us both offspring and progeny—the bounty of the generous ones. (1584)

body.text:

  4 7 3 0601c tvāmavasyurā cake .. 1585
body.translated_text: Hear this call of mine, O <s>Varuṇa</s>, and be gracious to me today; desiring your protection, I cry out to you. (1585)

body.text:

  4 7 3 0701c kayā stotṛbhya ā bhara .. 1586
body.translated_text: By what aid do you delight in us, O bull? By what means do you bring [gifts] to the praisers? (1586)

body.text:

body.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> alone for divine worship, <s>Indra</s> when the sacrifice is offered, <s>Indra</s> we invoke in the contest of the forest-dwellers, <s>Indra</s> for the winning of wealth. (1587) <s>Indra</s> by his greatness spread abroad the two world-halves with his power; <s>Indra</s> made the sun shine forth; in <s>Indra</s> indeed all beings find their rest, in <s>Indra</s> the pressed <s>Soma</s> drops [find their home]. (1588)

body.text:
4 7 3 0901a viśvakarmanhaviṣā vāvṛdhānaḥ svayaṃ yajasva tanvā3ṃ svā hi te .

body.translated_text: O <s>Viśvakarman</s>, strengthened by the oblation, worship your own self—for yours indeed it is; let other people round about be bewildered; here may the generous patron be our benefactor. (1589)

body.text:

  4 7 3 1002a prācīmanu pradiśaṃ pāti cekitatsaṃ raśmibhiryatate darśato ratho daivyo darśato rathaḥ .
  4 7 3 1002c agmannukthāni pauṃsyendraṃ jaitrāya harṣayata .

  4 7 3 1003a tvaṃ ha tyatpaṇīnāṃ vido vasu saṃ mātṛbhirmarjayasi sva ā dama ṛtasya dhītibhirdame .

body.translated_text: Being purified with this golden splendor, he crosses over all hatreds with his yoke-fellows, like the sun with his yoke-fellows; the stream from his back shines forth—being purified, ruddy and golden—when he pervades all forms with his hymn-verses, with his seven mouths and hymn-verses. (1590) Along the eastern quarter the watchful one guards; like a brilliant chariot he extends with his rays—a divine, brilliant chariot; hymns of manly praise have come to <s>Indra</s>—urge him on to victory, along with the thunderbolt, when you two are unshakeable in battles, unshakeable [in contests]. (1591) You indeed have found the treasure of the <s>Paṇis</s>; you cleanse yourself with the mothers in your own home, in the home of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) with sacred thoughts; from afar comes that <s>Sāman</s> where the inspired thoughts rejoice; with the three-layered ruddy [flames] he has assumed vigor, shining he has assumed vigor. (1592)

body.text:
4 7 3 1101a uta no goṣaṇiṃ dhiyamaśvasāṃ vājasāmuta .
  4 7 3 1101c nṛvatkṛṇuhyūtaye .. 1593
body.translated_text: Grant us also a prayer that wins cattle, that wins horses and nourishment; make it rich in men for our protection. (1593)

body.text:

  4 7 3 1201c vidā kāmasya venataḥ .. 1594
body.translated_text: O men, of the toiling one, of the sweating one, of him of true power—know the desire of the longing one. (1594)

body.text:

  4 7 3 1301c sumṛḍīkā bhavantu naḥ .. 1595
body.translated_text: May the sons of immortality hear our songs; may they be gracious to us. (1595)

body.text:
4 7 3 1401a pra vāṃ mahi dyavī abhyupastutiṃ bharāmahe .
  4 7 3 1401c śucī upa praśastaye .. 1596
  4 7 3 1402a punāne tanvā mithaḥ svena dakṣeṇa rājathaḥ .
  4 7 3 1402c ūhyāthe sanādṛtam .. 1597
  4 7 3 1403a mahī mitrasya sādhathastarantī pipratī ṛtam .
  4 7 3 1403c pari yajñaṃ ni ṣedathuḥ .. 1598
body.translated_text: We bring forth to you two, O great heavenly ones, a great hymn of praise—to the bright ones, for glorification. (1596) Being purified, you two shine mutually in your bodies by your own skill; you uphold what is eternally established. (1597) Great ones, you accomplish <s>Mitra</s>'s work, crossing over, fulfilling <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order); you sit around the sacrifice. (1598)

body.text:

body.translated_text: This [hymn] is equal to you, like a pigeon [carrying] its young; that speech of yours you do not disregard. (1599) O lord of gifts, praise-loving hero, may the hymn of praise to you be bountiful and gracious. (1600) Stand upright for our protection in this contest, O <s>Śatakratu</s> (hundred-powered one); let us speak together in battles. (1601)

body.text:

body.translated_text: The cows approach the well, great ones, granting the essence of the sacrifice—both their ears are golden. (1602) The rocks came near; honey was poured into the lotus, at the opening of the well. (1603) With reverence they pour into the well—the revolving, far-traveling one above, with its opening below, imperishable. (1604)

body.text:
4 7 3 1701a mā bhema mā śramiṣmograsya sakhye tava .

  4 7 3 1702a savyāmanu sphigyaṃ vāvase vṛṣnā na dāno asya roṣati .

body.translated_text: May we not fear, may we not be weary in your fierce friendship, O mighty one; great is the deed accomplished for you, O bull—may we see <s>Turvaśa</s> and <s>Yadu</s>. (1605) Along the left hip he has clothed himself; like a bull he does not flinch in giving; mixed with honey and <s>saragha</s>-grain, the milk-cows [offer their streams]—come quickly, run and drink! (1606)

body.text:

  4 7 3 1802a ayaṃ sahasramṛṣibhiḥ sahaskṛtaḥ samudra iva paprathe .

body.translated_text: May these songs of mine strengthen you, O <s>Purūvasu</s> (rich in wealth)—bright-hued, pure, and wise, they praised with hymns. (1607) This one, made mighty by a thousand seers, has spread like the ocean; true is his greatness which I praise—his power in sacrifices, in the rule of the inspired. (1608)

body.text:

  4 7 3 1902a turaṇyavo madhumantaṃ ghṛtaścataṃ viprāso arkamānṛcuḥ .

body.translated_text: He whose [realm] this entire [world] is—both <s>Ārya</s> and <s>Dāsa</s>, the treasure-keeper and the hostile—even athwart, O shining one with the sieve-chariot, that wealth is offered to you. (1609) The zealous wise ones sang the honey-sweet, ghee-dripping hymn; among us wealth has spread, manly power, glory—among us the [<s>Soma</s>] drops that roar. (1610)

body.text:

body.translated_text: O <s>Indu</s> (<s>Soma</s>), rich in cattle and horses, when pressed, O skilled one, like a wealthy lord—and the bright color placed among the cows [milk]. (1611) O <s>Indu</s>, lord of the tawny steeds, most divine in form—be like a friend to a friend, O manly one, for splendor. (1612) Keep far from us every ungodly, devouring [foe]; O <s>Indu</s>, conquering, ward off oppression and duplicity. (1613)

body.text:

body.translated_text: They anoint, they adorn, they anoint together; they lick the sacred rite, they anoint with honey; the bull flying in the surge of the river—the golden-filtered ones seize the cattle in the waters. (1614) Sing to the wise <s>Pavamāna</s> (<s>Soma</s>); like a great [river] the juice-stream flows beyond; like a serpent he glides over the worn-out skin, like a steed at play the golden bull has run forth. (1615) The king at the fore is praised; measuring the days, he is established in the worlds—golden, ghee-dripping, beautiful, surging; having light as his chariot, he purifies himself for wealth and home. (1616)

body.text:
āṣṭama prapāṭhakaḥ . prathamo 'rdhaḥ
  4 8 1 0101a viśvebhiragne agnibhirimaṃ yajñamidaṃ vacaḥ .

body.translated_text: Eighth <s>prapāṭhaka</s>, first half. O <s>Agni</s>, with all the fires, [accept] this sacrifice, this speech; receive it with power, O brilliant one! (1617) For even if we worship god after god continuously, in you alone the oblation is offered. (1618) May the lord of the household be dear to us—the delightful, desirable <s>hotṛ</s> (invoker); may we be dear to the one with beautiful fires. (1619)

body.text:

  4 8 1 0202a sa no vṛṣannamuṃ caruṃ satrādāvannapā vṛdhi .

  4 8 1 0203a bṛṣā yūtheva vaṃsagaḥ kṛṣṭīriyartyojasā .

body.translated_text: We invoke <s>Indra</s> for you from all sides, from among the peoples; may he be ours exclusively. (1620) O bull, ever-giving, drink this oblation and increase for us, unresisted. (1621) Like a bull going among the herd, he rules the peoples with his might—sovereign, unresisted. (1622)

body.text:

body.translated_text: O wondrous <s>Vasu</s>, impel gifts for us with your aid; of this wealth, O <s>Agni</s>, you are the charioteer—find a ford for our offspring. (1623) Carry our offspring and progeny with your saviors, O you undeceived and unassailable; O <s>Agni</s>, ward off from us divine wrath and godless malice. (1624)

body.text:

  4 8 1 0402a pra tatte adya śipiviṣṭa havyamaryaḥ śaṃsāmi vayunāni vidvān .

  4 8 1 0403a vaṣaṭ te viṣṇavāsa ā kṛṇomi tanme juṣasva śipiviṣṭa havyam .

body.translated_text: Why do you conceal your name, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since you have declared 'I am <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>'? Do not hide that form from us, since you assumed another form in battle. (1625) Today I offer the oblation to you, O <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>; the noble one, knowing the sacred ordinances, I declare your [praises]; I praise you, the mightiest of the mighty, dwelling in the far distance of this dark space. (1626) I make the <s>Vaṣaṭ</s> offering to you, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>—enjoy this oblation of mine, O <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>; may my well-spoken praises and songs strengthen you—protect us always with blessings! (1627)

body.text:

  4 8 1 0502a indraśca vāyaveṣāṃ somānāṃ pītimarhathaḥ .

  4 8 1 0503a vāyavindraśca śuṣmiṇā sarathaṃ śavasaspatī .

body.translated_text: 1628. O <s>Vāyu</s>, the bright [<s>Soma</s>] is offered to you — the first portion of the honey at the heavenly rites; come to the <s>Soma</s>-drinking, O desirable god, with your team [of horses]. || 1628 || 1629. O <s>Indra</s> and <s>Vāyu</s>, you deserve the drink of these <s>Soma</s> juices; for the drops flow toward you two, as rivers [flow] downward together. || 1629 || 1630. O <s>Vāyu</s> and <s>Indra</s>, the impetuous ones, the lords of strength, sharing one chariot — come with your teams for our aid; come to the <s>Soma</s>-drinking. || 1630 ||

body.text:
4 8 1 0601a adha kṣapā pariṣkṛto vājāṃ abhi pra gāhate .

  4 8 1 0602a tamasya marjayāmasi mado ya indrapātamaḥ .

  4 8 1 0603a taṃ gāthayā purāṇyā punānamabhyanūṣata .

body.translated_text: 1631. Then, adorned by the night, he plunges forth toward the prizes; when the thoughts of <s>Vivasvat</s>'s [descendants] urge the tawny one to go. || 1631 || 1632. We cleanse that intoxication of his which is most fit for <s>Indra</s> to drink; which the cows gave with their mouths, [both] formerly and now, [given by] the sages. || 1632 || 1633. Him they praised with an ancient song while being purified; and the devotions bearing the names of the gods trembled [with joy]. || 1633 ||

body.text:
4 8 1 0701a aśvaṃ na tvā vāravantaṃ vandadhyā agniṃ namobhiḥ .
  4 8 1 0701c samrājantamadhvarāṇām .. 1634
  4 8 1 0702a sa ghā naḥ sūnuḥ śavasā pṛthupragāmā suśevaḥ .
  4 8 1 0702c mīḍhvāṃ asmākaṃ babhūyāt .. 1635
  4 8 1 0703a sa no dūrāccāsācca ni martyādaghāyoḥ .
  4 8 1 0703c pāhi sadamidviśvāyuḥ .. 1636
body.translated_text: 1634. Like a horse adorned with trappings, I would honor <s>Agni</s> with homages — the sovereign ruler of sacrifices. || 1634 || 1635. May that son of ours, broad-stepping with strength, the gracious, the bountiful one, become [a protector] for us. || 1635 || 1636. From afar and from near, from the mortal who seeks harm, O ever-living one, protect [us] always. || 1636 ||

body.text:
4 8 1 0801a tvamindra pratūrtiṣvabhi viśvā asi spṛdhaḥ .

  4 8 1 0802a anu te śuṣmaṃ turayantamīyatuḥ kṣoṇī śiśuṃ na mātarā .
  4 8 1 0802c viśvāste spṛdhaḥ śnathayanta manyave vṛtraṃ yadindra tūrvasi .. 1638
body.translated_text: 1637. You, O <s>Indra</s>, surpass all rivals in conflicts; the slayer of the foe-less, the father, the conqueror of <s>Vṛtra</s> — you overcome those who would contend. || 1637 || 1638. The two worlds followed your rushing might, as two mothers [follow] a child; all your rivals fall before your fury, O <s>Indra</s>, when you conquer <s>Vṛtra</s>. || 1638 ||

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1639. The sacrifice increased <s>Indra</s> when he turned the earth; making a work of art in heaven. || 1639 || 1640. He extended beyond the atmosphere, in the intoxication of <s>Soma</s>, [into] the shining realms; when <s>Indra</s> split open <s>Vala</s>. || 1640 || 1641. He drove forth the cows for the <s>Aṅgirases</s>, revealing those that were hidden; he pushed <s>Vala</s> backward. || 1641 ||

body.text:
4 8 1 1001a tyamu vaḥ satrāsāhaṃ viśvāsu gīrṣvāyatam .

  4 8 1 1003c avā naḥ pārye dhane .. 1644
body.translated_text: 1642. That ever-conquering one, sought in all songs — rouse him for [our] aid. || 1642 || 1643. The warlike, the irresistible, the <s>Soma</s>-drinker, the unfailing — the man of unhindered wisdom. || 1643 || 1644. <s>Indra</s> alone is the ruler over all riches, the king; he attains for himself [all] powers, as a rim encompasses the wheel-spokes. || 1644 ||

body.text:

body.translated_text: 1714. Your furies have risen, O stone-armed one, smashing the <s>Rakṣas</s> (demon); push away those who contend against [you]. || 1714 || 1715. By this [hymn] he has struck down [the foe] with might, [as] in a chariot-contest when the prize is set — praise with an unfearing heart. || 1715 || 1716. The vows of this self-purifying one are not to be defied, nor [his] determination; he crushes whoever opposes you. || 1716 || 1717. They urge on the golden one who sheds intoxication, the swift steed in the rivers — the drop, for <s>Indra</s>, the exhilarating one. || 1717 ||

body.translated_text: 1718. Come, O <s>Indra</s>, with your delightful, peacock-plumed bay horses; let none restrain you, neither binding ones — cross over them like a desert. || 1718 || 1719. The devourer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, you burst open the cave <s>Vala</s>, the shatterer of fortresses, born of the waters; standing [in the chariot] of the bay steeds, the roaring <s>Indra</s> bursts even the firm [defenses]. || 1719 || 1720. You fill [your] resolve like a deep ocean, [you increase] cattle; like well-tended cows [going] to pasture, [the streams] have reached the lake as channels [flow to it]. || 1720 ||

May the drops intoxicate you, O bounteous <s>Indra</s>, for the giving of bounty to the presser; from that [bowl], you drank the <s>Soma</s> pressed in the two vessels — you thereby seized the supreme might. || 1722 ||

body.translated_text: 1723. You indeed, O most mighty god, protect the mortal; there is no other comforter than you, O bounteous one — I speak my word to you, O <s>Indra</s>. || 1723 || 1724. May your bounties, may your aids, O dweller [in all], never fail us; bestow upon us all the human treasures, for [all] peoples. || 1724 ||

Like a brilliant mare, ruddy, the mother of cows, upholder of <s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) — <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) has become the companion of the <s>Aśvins</s>. || 1726 || 1727. You are indeed the companion of the <s>Aśvins</s>, and the mother of cows; O <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), you rule over wealth. || 1727 ||

body.translated_text: 1728. This unprecedented <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn) shines forth, beloved of heaven; I praise you greatly, O <s>Aśvins</s>. || 1728 || 1729. You two wondrous ones, whose mother is the river, more generous than [all] treasures — O divine ones, finders of wealth, [inspired] by devotion. || 1729 || 1730. Your towering [steeds] are proclaimed at the ancient seat; when your chariot speeds wide. || 1730 ||

O <s>Uṣas</s>, today shine here, rich in cattle, rich in horses, O radiant one; shine richly upon us, O bounteous one. || 1732 || 1733. Yoke your prize-winning ruddy horses today, O <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn); then bring us all good fortune. || 1733 ||

body.text:

1734: O <s>Aśvins</s>, bring your protection toward us, with cattle, O wondrous ones, with gold — turn your chariot hither, of one mind.
1735: Let the wondrous gods, the bringers of joy, of golden path, waking at dawn, convey [them] here for <s>Soma</s>-drinking.
1736: You two who thus made fame and light from heaven for the people — bring us nourishment, O <s>Aśvins</s>, you two.

body.translated_text:
1737: I think of that <s>Agni</s> as the wealth — to whose home the milk-cows go, to whose home the swift steeds; he, the constant, the prize-winner — bring nourishment for the praisers.
1738: For <s>Agni</s>, seen by all peoples, gives the prize-winner to the clan; <s>Agni</s> [gives] self-born [wealth] for riches — pleased, he goes to the desirable; bring nourishment for the praisers.
1739: That <s>Agni</s> who is praised as the wealth — to whom the milk-cows come together, the swift-running steeds, the well-born patrons — bring nourishment for the praisers.

1740: Awaken us today for great wealth, O <s>Uṣas</s> (Dawn), rich in heaven — as you have awakened us before, O [Dawn] of true fame, desirable, well-born, rich in horses and truth.
1741: You who shine forth in good guidance, on your bright chariot, O daughter of heaven — shine forth, O mightier one, of true fame, desirable, well-born, rich in horses and truth.
1742: May she bring us wealth today; shine forth, O daughter of heaven — you who shine mightier, of true fame, desirable, well-born, rich in horses and truth.

body.translated_text:

1744: Come past, O <s>Aśvins</s>, beyond all my former [prayers] — wondrous ones, of golden path, gracious, river-borne — O honey-sweet ones, hear my call.
1745: Come to us bearing treasures, O <s>Aśvins</s>, you two — <s>Rudras</s>, of golden path, delighting, rich in prizes and wealth — O honey-sweet ones, hear my call.

body.text:

body.translated_text:
1746: <s>Agni</s> has been awakened by the kindling of peoples, [shining] toward Dawn approaching like a cow; rising like young ones spreading their wings, the rays stream forth toward heaven.
1747: The <s>Hotṛ</s> has been awakened to worship the gods; <s>Agni</s> has risen upward, well-disposed, in the morning — the shining splendor of the kindled one has been seen; the great god has been released from darkness.
1748: When he loosened the bond of the troop, the pure <s>Agni</s> adorns himself with pure rays of light — then the prize-seeking gift is yoked; he drank from the upward-lifted [ladles] with his flames.

body.text:

1750: The bright [Dawn] has come, with bright calf, white; the dark [Night] has yielded her dwelling-places — of common kin, immortal, following each other, the two heavens move, changing their color.
1751: Common is the path of the two sisters, endless — one after the other they travel, guided by the gods; they do not clash, they do not stand still, well-fixed — Night and Dawn, of one mind, of different form.

1753: She does not diminish the prepared [offering], the swiftest [Dawn] — come now near, O <s>Aśvins</s>, praised here — at the day's middle, swiftest with help, bestowing return and the best blessings on the worshipper.
1754: And come at the meeting-time, at the morning, at midday, at the rising of the sun — by day and night with most peaceful aid; the drinking of the <s>Aśvins</s> has not ceased now.

1757: They shine like working women at their tasks, from the distance with the same yoke — bearing nourishment for the good-doer, the good giver, indeed every day for the sacrificer who presses.

1759: When you yoke the bull-chariot, O <s>Aśvins</s>, sprinkle our lordly power with ghee and honey — enliven our prayers in battles; may we share in the spoils won by heroes.
1760: Hither may the three-wheeled, honey-bearing chariot of the <s>Aśvins</s> come, well-praised, with swift horses — the three-seated, bountiful, all-fortunate one; may it bring blessing for our two-footed and four-footed [creatures].

1769: To you indeed, O lord of strength, the songs go forth, like [arrows] joined.
1770: As streams [flow] along paths, so, O <s>Indra</s>, may your gifts come from you.

body.text:

1774: He who illumined the artful city, the swift poet, the heavenly one, not slow — shining like the sun, of a hundred selves.
1775: The twice-born one, blazing, stood over the three luminous realms and all the spaces — the <s>Hotṛ</s>, most worshipful, in the seat of the waters.
1776: This is that <s>Hotṛ</s> who is twice-born, who holds all desirable things, [seeking] fame — the mortal who has generously worshipped him [prospers].

body.translated_text:
1777: O <s>Agni</s>, today [grant us] that [blessing] like a swift horse, with praises — like a good, heart-touching power; may we prosper by your aids.
1778: For indeed, O <s>Agni</s>, you have become the charioteer of good power, of skill, of accomplishment — of the great truth.
1779: With these hymns of ours, be near to us — like heavenly light; O <s>Agni</s>, with all your faces, well-disposed.

4.9.1.18.01: I consider <s>Agni</s> the invoker (<s>Hotṛ</s>), the generous, the son of strength, <s>Jātavedas</s> — like an inspired sage, <s>Jātavedas</s>. 4.9.1.18.02: We, the sacrificers, call upon you, the most worshipful, the eldest of the <s>Aṅgirasas</s>, O inspired one, with thoughts — with inspired, pure thoughts! Like the encompassing heaven, the invoker of peoples — flame-haired, bull-like — may these clans urge him forward, these clans! (1814)

Ninth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s>, Second Half.
4.9.2.01.01: O <s>Agni</s>, your fame, your vigor — great, your rays shine, O resplendent one! O great-lustered one, with your strength you bestow the praise-worthy prize upon the worshipper, O sage! (1816)
4.9.2.01.02: Of purifying brilliance, of bright brilliance, of undiminished brilliance — you rise up with your beam! As a son wandering [between] the two mothers, you approach; you fill both heaven and earth. (1817)
4.9.2.01.03: O child of nourishment, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, be gladdened by fine praises, by devotions, [you who are] established! In you they have placed refreshments — the manifold-formed, the brilliantly-aided, the well-born. (1818)
4.9.2.01.04: Reigning, O <s>Agni</s>, extend [your domain] among creatures, [bring] riches to us, O immortal! You shine forth with visible beauty; you fulfill the visible purpose. (1819)
4.9.2.01.05: The performer of the sacrifice, the wise one, ruling over great bounty — you bestow the blessed gift of the dear, great refreshment, wealth for winning. (1820)
4.9.2.01.06: The people have placed <s>Agni</s> before [them] for favor — the orderly one, the mighty buffalo, visible to all. With their hymn, the human generations [praise] you, the attentive-eared, the most widely famed, the divine one. (1821)

body.translated_text: 1834. If, O <s>Indra</s>, I were lord of wealth as you are, alone indeed, the praiser would be my friend of cattle. || 1834 || 1835. I would bestow upon him, I would give to the wise one, O lord of might (<s>Śacīpati</s>), if I were the lord of cattle. || 1835 || 1836. Your cow, O <s>Indra</s>, is gracious bounty for the worshipper who presses [<s>Soma</s>]; overflowing, she yields cattle and horses. || 1836 ||

body.text:
4 9 2 1001a āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvastā na ūrje dadhātana .
  4 9 2 1001c mahe raṇāya cakṣase .. 1837
  4 9 2 1002a yo vaḥ śivatamo rasastasya bhājayateha naḥ .
  4 9 2 1002c uśatīriva mātaraḥ .. 1838
  4 9 2 1003a tasmā araṃ gamāma vo yasya kṣayāya jinvatha .
  4 9 2 1003c āpo janayathā ca naḥ .. 1839
body.translated_text: 1837. Waters, indeed you are the source of bliss; grant us nourishment, for the great and joyful vision. || 1837 || 1838. Of your most auspicious essence, make us partakers here, like loving mothers. || 1838 || 1839. To that [<s>Agni</s>] for whose dwelling you give strength, let us eagerly go; O waters, generate us. || 1839 ||

body.text:
4 9 2 1101a vāta ā vātu beṣajaṃ śambhu mayobhu no hṛde .
  4 9 2 1101c pra na ayūṃṣi tāriṣat .. 1840
  4 9 2 1102a uta vāta pitāsi na uta bhrātota naḥ sakhā .
  4 9 2 1102c sa no jīvātave kṛdhi .. 1841
  4 9 2 1103a yadado vāta te gṛhe3 'mṛtaṃ nihitaṃ guhā .
  4 9 2 1103c tasyo no dehi jīvase .. 1842
body.translated_text: 1840. Let <s>Vāta</s> (Wind) blow [as] medicine, auspicious and blissful to our hearts; may he prolong our lives. || 1840 || 1841. You, O <s>Vāta</s>, are our father, and our brother, and our friend; grant us life. || 1841 || 1842. That immortal [essence] which is stored away in your house, O <s>Vāta</s> — of that grant us, that we may live. || 1842 ||

body.text:
4 9 2 1201a abhi vājī viśvarūpo janitraṃ hiraṇyayaṃ bibhradatkaṃ suparṇaḥ .
  4 9 2 1201c sūryasya bhānumṛtuthā vasānaḥ pari svayaṃ medhamṛjro jajāna .. 1843
  4 9 2 1202a apsu retaḥ śiśriye viśvarūpaṃ tejaḥ pṛthivyāmadhi yatsambabhūva .
  4 9 2 1202c antarikṣe svaṃ mahimānaṃ mimānaḥ kanikranti vṛṣṇo aśvasya retaḥ .. 1844
  4 9 2 1203a ayaṃ sahasrā pari yuktā vasānaḥ sūryasya bhānuṃ yajño dādhāra .
  4 9 2 1203c sahasradāḥ śatadā bhūridāvā dharttā divo bhuvanasya viśpatiḥ .. 1845
body.translated_text: 1843. Swift, all-formed, bearing a golden garment, the beautiful-winged one [went] to the birthplace; wearing the radiance of <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun) according to the seasons, the swift-moving one himself has begotten the sacrifice. || 1843 || 1844. In the waters the all-formed seed was deposited; the splendour that arose upon the earth — measuring his own greatness in the mid-space, the seed of the mighty stallion-horse resounds. || 1844 || 1845. This [sacrifice], clad with a thousandfold, has upheld the radiance of <s>Sūrya</s>; giver of thousands, giver of hundreds, giver of much — upholder of heaven, lord of beings. || 1845 ||

body.text:
4 9 2 1301a nāke suparṇamupa yatpatantaṃ hṛdā venanto abhyacakṣata tvā .
  4 9 2 1301c hiraṇyapakṣaṃ varuṇasya dūtaṃ yamasya yonau śakunaṃ bhuraṇyum .. 1846
  4 9 2 1302a ūrdhvo gandharvo adhi nāke asthātpratyañcitrā bibhradasyāyudhāni .
  4 9 2 1302c vasāno atkaṃ surabhiṃ dṛśe kaṃ sva3rṇa nāma janata priyāṇi .. 1847
  4 9 2 1303a drapsaḥ samudramabhi yajjigāti paśyangṛdhrasya cakṣasā vidharman .
  4 9 2 1303c bhānuḥ śukreṇa śociṣā cakānastṛtīye cakre rajasi priyāṇi .. 1848
body.translated_text: 1846. The beautiful-winged one flying upward to heaven — with the heart perceiving, they beheld you; the golden-winged messenger of <s>Varuṇa</s>, the active bird in the realm of <s>Yama</s>. || 1846 || 1847. The <s>Gandharva</s> stood upright on high in heaven, displaying his brilliant weapons; wearing a fragrant garment, beautiful to behold — like the sun, he produces dear [things] by name. || 1847 || 1848. The drop [of <s>Soma</s>] moves toward the ocean — beholding with the eye of the eagle in the expanse; the ray, shining with bright splendour, [produces] dear things in the third realm of space. || 1848 ||

body.text:
navama prapāṭhakaḥ . tṛtīyo 'rdhaḥ
  4 9 3 0101a āśuḥ śiśāno vṛṣabho na bhīmo ghanāghanaḥ kṣobhaṇaścarṣaṇīnām .
  4 9 3 0101c saṅkrandano 'nimiṣa ekavīraḥ śataṃ senā ajayatsākamindraḥ .. 1849
  4 9 3 0102a saṅkrandanenānimiṣeṇa jiṣṇunā yutkāreṇa duścyavanena dhṛṣṇunā .
  4 9 3 0102c tadindreṇa jayata tatsahadhvaṃ yudho nara iṣuhastena vṛṣṇā .. 1850
  4 9 3 0103a sa iṣuhastaiḥ sa niṣaṅgibhirvaśī saṃsraṣṭā sa yudha indro gaṇena .
  4 9 3 0103c saṃ sṛṣṭajitsomapā bāhuśardhyū3gradhanvā pratihitābhirastā .. 1851
body.translated_text: Ninth <s>Prapāṭhaka</s> (Chapter), Third Half. 1849. Swift, sharpening [his weapons], fearsome as a bull, smiter of smiters, shaker of peoples, roaring, unwinking, the sole hero — <s>Indra</s> conquered a hundred armies at once. || 1849 || 1850. With the roaring, unwinking, victorious, war-crying, unshakable, bold one — with <s>Indra</s> conquer, endure together the battles, O men, with the arrow-handed bull. || 1850 || 1851. He with arrows in hand, he with quivers, the ruler, the mingler in battle — <s>Indra</s> with his troop — conquering in close combat, drinker of <s>Soma</s>, strong-armed, fierce-bowed, with arrows fitted and shot. || 1851 ||

body.text:
4 9 3 0201a bṛhaspate pari dīyā rathena rakṣohāmitrāṃ apabādhamānaḥ .
  4 9 3 0201c prabhañjansenāḥ pramṛṇo yudhā jayannasmākamedhyavitā rathānām .. 1852
  4 9 3 0202a balavijñāyaḥ sthaviraḥ pravīraḥ sahasvānvājī sahamāna ugraḥ .
  4 9 3 0202c abhivīro abhisatvā sahojā jaitramindra rathamā tiṣṭha govit .. 1853
  4 9 3 0203a gotrabhidaṃ govidaṃ vajrabāhuṃ jayantamajma pramṛṇantamojasā .
  4 9 3 0203c imaṃ sajātā anu vīrayadhvamindraṃ sakhāyo anu saṃ rabhadhvam .. 1854
body.translated_text: 1852. O <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, drive around with your chariot, repelling the <s>rakṣas</s>-demons (fiends) and enemies; shattering armies, crushing in battle, be victorious — the champion of our chariots. || 1852 || 1853. Known for strength, firm, great hero, powerful, victorious, mighty, fierce — surpassing in heroes, surpassing in warriors, born of strength — mount the conquering chariot, O <s>Indra</s>, finder of cattle. || 1853 || 1854. Him who breaks open the cow-pens, who finds the cattle, whose arm holds the thunderbolt, who conquers in onset, who crushes with might — follow this [hero], O kinsmen; follow <s>Indra</s>, O comrades, hold fast to him. || 1854 ||

body.text:
4 9 3 0301a abhi gotrāṇi sahasā gāhamāno 'dayo vīraḥ śatamanyurindraḥ .
  4 9 3 0301c duścyavanaḥ pṛtanāṣāḍayudhyo3 'smākaṃ senā avatu pra yutsu .. 1855
  4 9 3 0302a indra āsāṃ netā bṛhaspatirdakṣiṇā yajñaḥ pura etu somaḥ .
  4 9 3 0302c devasenānāmabhibhañjatīnāṃ jayantīnāṃ maruto yantvagram .. 1856
  4 9 3 0303a indrasya vṛṣṇo varuṇasya rājña ādityānāṃ marutāṃ śardha ugram .
  4 9 3 0303c mahāmanasāṃ bhuvanacyavānāṃ ghoṣo devānāṃ jayatāmudasthāt .. 1857
body.translated_text: 1855. Penetrating the cow-pens with force, the indomitable hero, hundred-wrathed <s>Indra</s> — unshakable, victorious in battle, invincible — may he protect our armies and advance in conflicts. || 1855 || 1856. <s>Indra</s> is the leader of these [armies]; <s>Bṛhaspati</s> is the right flank; may the sacrifice and <s>Soma</s> go before; may the <s>Maruts</s> march at the front of the shattering, conquering divine armies. || 1856 || 1857. The fierce war-cry of the heroic <s>Indra</s>, the royal <s>Varuṇa</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, the host of <s>Maruts</s> — of the great-spirited ones who shake the world — the shout of the conquering gods has risen. || 1857 ||

body.text:
4 9 3 0401a uddharṣaya maghavannāyudhānyutsatvanāṃ māmakānāṃ manāṃsi .
  4 9 3 0401c udvṛtrahanvājināṃ vājinānyudrathānāṃ jayatāṃ yantu ghoṣāḥ .. 1858
  4 9 3 0402a asmākamindraḥ samṛteṣu dhvajeṣvasmākaṃ yā iṣavastā jayantu .
  4 9 3 0402c asmākaṃ vīrā uttare bhavantvasmāṃ u devā avatā haveṣu .. 1859
  4 9 3 0403a asau yā senā marutaḥ pareṣāmabhyeti na ojasā spardhamānā .
  4 9 3 0403c tāṃ gūhata tamasāpavratena yathaiteṣāmanyo anyaṃ na jānāt .. 1860
body.translated_text: 1858. Arouse, O Bounteous One (<s>Maghavan</s>), the weapons; lift up the spirits of my warriors; raise up, O slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, the strength of the steeds; let the shouts of the conquering charioteers arise. || 1858 || 1859. May <s>Indra</s> be [with us] in our encounters and amid our banners; may our arrows be victorious; may our heroes be supreme; may the gods aid us at our invocations. || 1859 || 1860. That army of the enemies, O <s>Maruts</s>, which advances against us, striving with force — hide it in darkness, in lawlessness, so that not one of them may know the other. || 1860 ||

body.text:
4 9 3 0501a amīṣāṃ cittaṃ pratilobhayantī gṛhāṇāṅgānyapve parehi .
  4 9 3 0501c abhi prehi nirdaha hṛtsu śokairandhenāmitrāstamasā sacantām .. 1861
  4 9 3 0502a pretā jayatā nara indro vaḥ śarma yacchatu .
  4 9 3 0502c ugrā vaḥ santu bāhavo 'nādhṛṣyā yathāsatha .. 1862
  4 9 3 0503a avasṛṣṭā parā pata śaravye brahmasaṃśite .
  4 9 3 0503c gacchāmitrānpra padyasva māmīṣāṃ kaṃ ca nocchiṣaḥ .. 1863
body.translated_text: 1861. Confounding the minds of those [enemies], seize their limbs and go forth; advance upon them, burn the anguish in their hearts — may the foes be encompassed in blinding darkness. || 1861 || 1862. Go forth, conquer, O men! May <s>Indra</s> grant you protection; may your arms be mighty, so that you be unassailable. || 1862 || 1863. Released, fly far, O arrow, sharpened by sacred prayer; go to the enemies, strike — leave not a single one of them remaining. || 1863 ||

body.text:
4 9 3 0601a kaṅkāḥ suparṇā anu yantvenāngṛdhrāṇāmannamasāvastu senā .
  4 9 3 0601c maiṣāṃ mocyaghahāraśca nendra vayāṃsyenānanusaṃyantu sarvān .. 1864
  4 9 3 0602a amitrasenāṃ maghavannasmāñchatruyatīmabhi .
  4 9 3 0602c ubhau tāmindra vṛtrahannagniśca dahataṃ prati .. 1865
  4 9 3 0603a yatra bāṇāḥ sampatanti kumārā viśikhā iva .
  4 9 3 0603c tatrā no brahmaṇaspatiraditiḥ śarma yacchatu viśvāhā śarma yacchatu .. 1866
body.translated_text: 1864. May the kites, the eagles follow this [army]; may vultures and birds of prey attend; may this be the army's food — may not a single life-taker [among the foes] be freed; may all the birds follow them. || 1864 || 1865. O Bounteous One (<s>Maghavan</s>), the hostile army that seeks to destroy us — both you, O <s>Indra</s>, slayer of <s>Vṛtra</s>, and <s>Agni</s>, burn it in return. || 1865 || 1866. Where arrows fly together like boys with shaved locks, there may <s>Brahmaṇaspati</s> and <s>Aditi</s> grant us protection — grant us protection always. || 1866 ||

body.text:
4 9 3 0701a vi rakṣo vi mṛdho jahi vi vṛtrasya hanū ruja .
  4 9 3 0701c vi manyumindra vṛtrahannamitrasyābhidāsataḥ .. 1867
  4 9 3 0702a vi na indra mṛdho jahi nīcā yaccha pṛtanyataḥ .
  4 9 3 0702c yo asmāṃ abhidāsatyadharaṃ gamayā tamaḥ .. 1868
  4 9 3 0703a indrasya bāhū sthavirau yuvānāvanādhṛṣyau supratīkāvasahyau .
  4 9 3 0703c tau yuñjīta prathamau yoga āgate yābhyāṃ jitamasurāṇāṃ saho mahat .. 1869
body.translated_text: Smash the demons, smash the foes, break the jaws of <s>Vṛtra</s>; O <s>Indra</s> <s>Vṛtrahan</s> (slayer of Vṛtra), smash the fury of the assailing enemy. (1867) Smash the foes for us, O <s>Indra</s>, bring low the attackers; whoever assaults us—send him down to darkness. (1868) The two arms of <s>Indra</s>, firm and youthful, unassailable, fair-appearing, invincible—let him yoke those two first when the occasion arises, by which the great might of the <s>Asuras</s> was conquered. (1869)

body.text:
4 9 3 0801a marmāṇi te varmaṇā cchādayāmi somastvā rājāmṛtenānu vastām .
  4 9 3 0801c urorvarīyo varuṇaste kṛṇotu jayantaṃ tvānu devā madantu .. 1870
  4 9 3 0802a andhā amitrā bhavatāśīrṣāṇo 'haya iva .
  4 9 3 0802c teṣāṃ vo agninunnānāmindro hantu varaṃvaram .. 1871
  4 9 3 0803a yo naḥ svo 'raṇo yaśca niṣṭyo jighāṃsati .
  4 9 3 0803c devāstaṃ sarve dhūrvantu brahma varma mamāntaraṃ śarma varma mamāntaram .. 1872
body.translated_text: I cover your vital parts with armor; may King <s>Soma</s> clothe you with immortality; may <s>Varuṇa</s> make [your realm] wider than wide; may the gods rejoice in you as you conquer. (1870) May the enemies become blind, headless like serpents; of those driven forth by <s>Agni</s>, may <s>Indra</s> slay the foremost of the foremost. (1871) Whoever among our own or a stranger or an outsider wishes to harm us—may all the gods destroy him; the sacred word (<s>Brahman</s>) is my inner armor, shelter is my inner armor. (1872)

body.text:
4 9 3 0901a mṛgo na bhīmaḥ kucaro giriṣṭhāḥ parāvata ā jaganthā parasyāḥ .
  4 9 3 0901c sṛkaṃ saṃśāya pavimindra tigmaṃ vi śatrūṃ tāḍhi vi mṛdho nudasva .. 1873
  4 9 3 0902a bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devā bhadraṃ paśyemākṣabhiryajatrāḥ .
  4 9 3 0902c sthirairaṅgaistuṣṭuvāṃ sastanūbhirvyaśemahi devahitaṃ yadāyuḥ .. 1874
  4 9 3 0903a svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ .
  4 9 3 0903c svasti nastārkṣyo ariṣṭanemiḥ svasti no bṛhaspatirdadhātu ..
  4 9 3 0903e Oṃ svasti no bṛhaspatirdadhātu .. 1875
body.translated_text: Like a fearsome beast roaming and dwelling in the mountains, you have come from the farthest distance; sharpen the arrow and the keen point, O <s>Indra</s>—strike the enemies, push away the foes! (1873) May we hear what is auspicious with our ears, O gods; may we see what is auspicious with our eyes, O worshipful ones; with firm limbs and strong bodies, having praised, may we enjoy the full span of life allotted by the gods. (1874) May <s>Indra</s> of great fame grant us well-being; may <s>Pūṣan</s>, the all-knowing, grant us well-being; may <s>Tārkṣya</s> of uninjured wheel-rim grant us well-being; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> grant us well-being—<s>Oṃ</s>, may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> grant us well-being! (1875)

body.text: .. ityuttarārcikaḥ ..
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Uttarārcika</s> (later collection of verses).
